sentences.zh: 馬錄，字君卿，信陽人。正德三年進士。授固安知縣。居官廉明，征為御史，按江南諸府。世宗即位，疏言：「江南之民最苦糧長。白糧輸內府一石，率費四五石。他如酒醋局、供應庫以至軍器、胖襖、顏料之屬輸內府者，費皆然。戶部侍郎秦金等請從錄言，命石加耗一斗，毋得苛求。中官黃錦誣劾高唐判官金坡，詔逮之，連五百餘人。錄言：祖宗內設法司，外設撫、按，百餘年刑清政平。先帝時，劉瑾、錢寧輩蠱惑聖聰，動遣錦衣官校，致天下洶洶。陛下方勤新政，不虞復有高唐之命。」給事中許復禮等亦以為言，獄得少解。嘉靖二年大計天下庶官，被黜者多訐撫、按，以錄言禁止。

translations.literal: Ma Lu, courtesy name Junqing, was from Xinyang. He became a jinshi in the third year of Zhengde. He was appointed magistrate of Gu'an. In office he was honest and clear, and he was summoned to be censor, inspecting the prefectures of Jiangnan. When Shizong ascended the throne, he submitted a memorial, saying: "The people of Jiangnan suffer most from grain-chief service. For each shi of white grain transported to the inner palace, the cost commonly reaches four or five shi. Other deliveries to the inner palace, such as those for the Wine and Vinegar Office, the Supply Storehouse, and even military equipment, padded coats, and pigments, all cost the same. Vice Minister of Revenue Qin Jin and others requested that Lu's words be followed, and an order was issued adding one dou of wastage allowance per shi and forbidding harsh exactions. The eunuch Huang Jin falsely impeached Jin Po, Assistant Magistrate of Gaotang, and an edict ordered his arrest, implicating more than five hundred people. Lu said that the ancestors established judicial offices within and grand coordinators and regional inspectors without, and for more than a hundred years punishments had been clear and government peaceful. In the former emperor's time, Liu Jin, Qian Ning, and their kind misled the sacred intelligence and repeatedly dispatched Embroidered Uniform Guard officers and constables, causing turmoil throughout the realm. Your Majesty is now diligently pursuing new government, and one would not expect another Gaotang order." Supervising Secretary Xu Fuli and others also spoke on this, and the prison case was somewhat eased. In the second year of Jiajing, when officials throughout the realm underwent the grand evaluation, many of those dismissed attacked the grand coordinators and regional inspectors. Because of Lu's words this was prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lu, courtesy name Junqing, was a native of Xinyang. A jinshi of Zhengde 3, he was appointed magistrate of Gu'an. He governed with integrity and clarity, and was summoned as censor to inspect the prefectures of Jiangnan. When Shizong came to the throne, he memorialized: "The people of Jiangnan suffer most from grain-chief service. For every shi of white grain sent to the inner palace, the expense usually reaches four or five shi. Other deliveries to the inner palace, from the Wine and Vinegar Office and Supply Storehouse to military equipment, padded coats, and pigments, are all the same. Vice Minister of Revenue Qin Jin and others asked that Lu's proposal be adopted, so an order added one dou of allowance per shi and forbade harsh exactions. The eunuch Huang Jin falsely impeached Jin Po, Assistant Magistrate of Gaotang, and an edict ordered his arrest, implicating more than five hundred people. Lu said that the ancestors established judicial offices inside the capital and grand coordinators and inspectors outside it, so punishments had been clear and government peaceful for more than a century. Under the former emperor, Liu Jin, Qian Ning, and their sort deceived the imperial judgment and repeatedly sent out Embroidered Uniform Guard officers and constables, throwing the realm into alarm. Your Majesty is now diligently renewing government, so one would not expect another Gaotang order." Supervising Secretary Xu Fuli and others also spoke, and the case was somewhat eased. In Jiajing 2, during the grand evaluation of officials across the realm, many dismissed men accused the grand coordinators and inspectors. Because of Lu's statement, this was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 五年出按山西，而妖賊李福達獄起。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he went out as touring censor for Shanxi, and the case of the demonic rebel Li Fuda arose.
translations.idiomatic: In his fifth year in office he was dispatched as touring censor to Shanxi, where the case of the heretic rebel Li Fuda broke out.

sentences.zh: 福達者，崞人。

translations.literal: Fuda was a man of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Fuda was a native of Guo.

sentences.zh: 初坐妖賊王良、李鉞黨，戍山丹衛。

translations.literal: At first he was convicted as a follower of the demonic rebels Wang Liang and Li Yue and was banished to garrison service at the Shandan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was first convicted as an accomplice of the heretics Wang Liang and Li Yue and sent to penal service at the Shandan Guard.

sentences.zh: 逃還，更名午，為清軍御史所勾，再戍山海衛。

translations.literal: He fled back, changed his name to Wu, was seized by a Qing-army censor, and was banished again to the Shanhai Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He escaped home, took the name Wu, was rounded up by a censor charged with clearing stragglers, and was banished again to the Shanhai Guard.

sentences.zh: 復逃居洛川，以彌勒教誘愚民邵進祿等為亂。

translations.literal: He fled again and lived in Luochuan, using the Maitreya teaching to entice the foolish commoner Shao Jinlu and others into rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He fled once more and settled in Luochuan, where he used Maitreya sect teachings to stir up the commoner Shao Jinlu and others in revolt.

sentences.zh: 事覺，進祿伏誅，福達先還家，得免。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, Jinlu was executed, but Fuda had already returned home and escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was uncovered, Jinlu was put to death, but Fuda had already gone home and went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 更姓名曰張寅，往來徐溝間，輸粟得太原衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He changed his name again to Zhang Yin, traveled between Xu and Gou, and by delivering grain obtained the post of commander of the Taiyuan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He changed his name again to Zhang Yin, traveled between Xu and Gou, and bought his way into the post of commander of the Taiyuan Guard by delivering grain.

sentences.zh: 子大仁、大義、大禮皆冒京師匠籍。

translations.literal: His sons Daren, Dayi, and Dali all fraudulently enrolled in the capital artisan registers.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Daren, Dayi, and Dali all fraudulently enrolled on the capital artisan rolls.

sentences.zh: 用黃白術幹武定侯郭勛，勛大信幸。

translations.literal: By means of alchemy he approached the Marquis of Wuding, Guo Xun, who greatly trusted and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: He approached the Marquis of Wuding, Guo Xun, with alchemical arts, and Xun came to trust and favor him deeply.

sentences.zh: 其仇薛良訟於錄，按問得實。

translations.literal: His enemy Xue Liang brought suit before Lu; on investigation the facts were established.
translations.idiomatic: His enemy Xue Liang brought the case before Ma Lu, and investigation confirmed the facts.

sentences.zh: 檄洛川父老雜辨之，益信。

translations.literal: He summoned the elders of Luochuan to identify him in a mixed inquiry, and confidence increased.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Luochuan elders to identify the man in a group inquiry, which only strengthened the case.

sentences.zh: 勛為遺書錄祈免，錄不從，偕巡撫江潮具獄以聞，且劾勛庇奸亂法。

translations.literal: Xun sent a letter asking Lu to plead for exemption; Lu refused, and together with the surveillance commissioner Jiang Chao prepared the full case for report, also impeaching Xun for shielding a villain and subverting the law.
translations.idiomatic: Xun wrote to Lu asking that he be spared; Lu refused, and together with Surveillance Commissioner Jiang Chao submitted the completed case to the throne while also impeaching Xun for shielding a criminal and corrupting justice.

sentences.zh: 章下都察院，都御史聶賢等覆如錄奏，力言勛黨逆罪。

translations.literal: The memorial went to the Censorate; the Censor-in-chief Nie Xian and others replied as Lu had reported, strongly stating Xun's complicity in treason.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the Censorate, where Censor-in-chief Nie Xian and others endorsed Lu's findings and insisted that Xun was party to treason.

sentences.zh: 詔福達父子論死，妻女為奴，沒其產，責勛對狀。

translations.literal: An edict sentenced Fuda and his sons to death, made wife and daughters slaves, confiscated their property, and ordered Xun to answer the charges in person.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sentenced Fuda and his sons to death, enslaved their wives and daughters, confiscated their property, and ordered Xun to answer the charges in person.

sentences.zh: 勛懼，乞恩，因為福達代辨，帝置不問。

translations.literal: Xun was afraid and begged grace, pleading on Fuda's behalf; the Emperor set the matter aside.
translations.idiomatic: Xun grew afraid and begged for mercy, pleading Fuda's case himself; the Emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 會給事中王科、鄭一鵬、程輅、常泰、劉琦、鄭自璧、趙廷瑞、沈漢、秦祐、張逵、陳臯謨，御史程啟充、盧瓊、邵豳、高世魁、任淳，南京御史姚鳴鳳、潘壯、戚雄、王獻，評事杜鸞，刑部郎中劉仕，主事唐樞，交章劾勛，謂罪當連坐。

translations.literal: Thereupon the supervising secretaries Wang Ke, Zheng Yipeng, Cheng Lu, Chang Tai, Liu Qi, Zheng Zibi, Zhao Tingrui, Shen Han, Qin You, Zhang Kui, and Chen Gaomo; the censors Cheng Qichong, Lu Qiong, Shao Bin, Gao Shikui, and Ren Chun; the Nanjing censors Yao Mingfeng, Pan Zhuang, Qi Xiong, and Wang Xian; the reviewing official Du Luan; the Ministry of Punishments bureau director Liu Shi; and the section chief Tang Shu all submitted memorials impeaching Xun, saying his crime warranted joint punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At this point a stream of memorials arrived impeaching Xun: from supervising secretaries Wang Ke, Zheng Yipeng, Cheng Lu, Chang Tai, Liu Qi, Zheng Zibi, Zhao Tingrui, Shen Han, Qin You, Zhang Kui, and Chen Gaomo; from censors Cheng Qichong, Lu Qiong, Shao Bin, Gao Shikui, and Ren Chun; from Nanjing censors Yao Mingfeng, Pan Zhuang, Qi Xiong, and Wang Xian; from reviewing official Du Luan; from Ministry of Punishments bureau director Liu Shi; and from section chief Tang Shu—all arguing that Xun's crimes warranted joint punishment.

sentences.zh: 勛亦累自訴，且以議禮觸眾怒為言，帝心動。

translations.literal: Xun also repeatedly pleaded his own case, saying moreover that he had provoked popular anger through the Rites Controversy; the Emperor's mind was moved.
translations.idiomatic: Xun pleaded his own case again and again, claiming he had only provoked the court's wrath through the Rites Controversy; the Emperor began to waver.

sentences.zh: 勛復乞張璁、桂萼為援。

translations.literal: Xun again begged Zhang Cong and Gui E for support.
translations.idiomatic: Xun again appealed to Zhang Cong and Gui E for help.

sentences.zh: 璁、萼素惡廷臣攻己，亦欲借是舒宿憤，乃謂諸臣內外交結，借端陷勛，將漸及諸議禮者。

translations.literal: Cong and E had long hated court officials for attacking them and also wished to vent old resentments through this affair; they therefore said the officials were conspiring inside and outside the court, seizing a pretext to trap Xun, and would gradually extend the attack to all who had favored the new rites.
translations.idiomatic: Cong and E had long resented the court officials who attacked them and saw a chance to settle old scores; they claimed the officials were conspiring inside and outside the court, using the case as a pretext to trap Xun and would soon turn on everyone who had supported the new rites.

sentences.zh: 帝深入其言，而外廷不知，攻勛益急。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deeply swayed by their words, but the outer court did not know this and pressed its attack on Xun ever harder.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was deeply persuaded, but the outer court knew nothing of this and pressed its attack on Xun ever harder.

sentences.zh: 帝益疑，命取福達等至京下三法司訊，既又命會文武大臣更訊之，皆無異詞。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew more suspicious and ordered Fuda and the others brought to the capital for interrogation by the Three Judicial Offices; he then ordered a joint re-examination by civil and military grandees, and in every case the testimony was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Growing more suspicious, the Emperor ordered Fuda and the others brought to the capital for trial by the Three Judicial Offices, then ordered civil and military grandees to re-examine the case together; every account still matched.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，將親訊，以楊一清之言而止，仍下廷鞫。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and was about to interrogate them in person, but stopped on Yang Yiqing's advice and still sent the case down for court trial.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and was about to interrogate them himself, but Yang Yiqing dissuaded him; the case was still sent down for court trial.

sentences.zh: 尚書顏頤壽等不敢自堅，改擬妖言律斬。

translations.literal: The ministers Yan Yishou and others did not dare stand firm and revised the sentence to execution under the demonic-speech statute.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yan Yishou and the others did not dare hold firm and revised the sentence to execution under the statute on demonic speech.

sentences.zh: 帝猶怒，命法司俱戴罪辦事，遣官往械錄、潮及前問官布政使李璋、按察使李玨、僉事章綸、都指揮馬豕等。

translations.literal: The Emperor was still angry, ordered the judicial offices all to continue their duties while bearing guilt, and sent officials to arrest Lu, Chao, and the former investigating officials—the provincial administration commissioner Li Zhang, the surveillance commissioner Li Jue, the assistant surveillance commissioner Zhang Lun, and the regional commander Ma Shi, among others.
translations.idiomatic: Still furious, the Emperor ordered the judicial offices to continue their duties under suspended guilt, and sent officials to arrest Ma Lu, Jiang Chao, and the former investigators—Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Zhang, Surveillance Commissioner Li Jue, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Lun, and Regional Commander Ma Shi, among others.

sentences.zh: 時璋、玨已遷都御史，璋巡撫寧夏，玨巡撫甘肅，皆下獄廷訊。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang and Jue had already been promoted to censors-in-chief; Zhang was surveillance commissioner of Ningxia and Jue of Gansu, and both were imprisoned for court interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhang and Jue had already been promoted to censors-in-chief—Zhang as surveillance commissioner of Ningxia and Jue of Gansu—and both were thrown into prison for court interrogation.

sentences.zh: 乃反前獄，抵良誣告罪。

translations.literal: The case was then reversed from the earlier verdict and Xue Liang was charged with false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier verdict was overturned and Xue Liang was charged with false accusation instead.

sentences.zh: 帝以罪不及錄，怒甚。

translations.literal: Because the crime did not reach Lu, the Emperor was very angry.
translations.idiomatic: Because the charges did not reach Ma Lu, the Emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 命璁、萼、方獻夫分署三法司事，盡下尚書頤壽，侍郎劉玉、王啟，左都御史賢，副都御史劉文莊，僉都御史張潤，大理卿湯沐，少卿徐文華、顧佖，寺丞汪淵獄，嚴刑推問遂搜錄篋，得大學士賈詠、都御史張仲賢、工部侍郎閔楷、御史張英及寺丞淵私書。

translations.literal: He ordered Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Fang Xianfu to divide supervision of the Three Judicial Offices, threw into prison the ministers Yan Yishou; the vice ministers Liu Yu and Wang Qi; the Left Censor-in-chief Xian; the Vice Censor-in-chief Liu Wenzhuang; the Assistant Censor-in-chief Zhang Run; the Court of Review president Tang Mu; the vice presidents Xu Wenhua and Gu Yi; and the Court registrar Wang Yuan, and under severe torture pursued the inquiry; they then searched Lu's box and obtained private letters from Grand Secretary Jia Yong, Censor-in-chief Zhang Zhongxian, Works Vice Minister Min Kai, Censor Zhang Ying, and Registrar Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He put Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Fang Xianfu in charge of the Three Judicial Offices, imprisoned Minister Yan Yishou, Vice Ministers Liu Yu and Wang Qi, Left Censor-in-chief Nie Xian, Vice Censor-in-chief Liu Wenzhuang, Assistant Censor-in-chief Zhang Run, Court of Review President Tang Mu, Vice Presidents Xu Wenhua and Gu Yi, and Registrar Wang Yuan, and under severe torture pursued the inquiry; searching Ma Lu's papers they found private letters from Grand Secretary Jia Yong, Censor-in-chief Zhang Zhongxian, Works Vice Minister Min Kai, Censor Zhang Ying, and Registrar Yuan.

sentences.zh: 詠引罪致仕去，仲賢等亦下獄。

translations.literal: Yong pleaded guilty and retired; Zhongxian and the others were also imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yong confessed guilt and retired; Zhongxian and the others were imprisoned as well.

sentences.zh: 萼等上言：「給事中琦、泰，郎中仕，聲勢相倚，挾私彈事，佐錄殺人。

translations.literal: E and the others memorialized: "The supervising secretaries Qi and Tai, and the bureau director Shi, rely on each other's power, bring private charges in memorials, and helped Lu kill a man.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E and the others memorialized: "Supervising Secretaries Liu Qi and Chang Tai and Bureau Director Liu Shi rely on each other's influence, lodge partisan impeachments, and helped Ma Lu secure a man's death.

sentences.zh: 給事中科、一鵬、祐、漢、輅，評事鸞，御史鳴鳳、壯、雄，扶同妄奏，助成奸惡。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Ke, Yipeng, You, Han, and Lu; the reviewing official Luan; and the censors Mingfeng, Zhuang, and Xiong joined in false memorials and helped bring the villainy to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Wang Ke, Zheng Yipeng, Qin You, Shen Han, and Cheng Lu; Reviewing Official Du Luan; and Censors Yao Mingfeng, Pan Zhuang, and Qi Xiong joined in reckless memorials and helped the crime along.

sentences.zh: 給事中逵，御史世魁，方幸寅就死，得誣勛謀逆，率同連名，同聲駕禍。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Kui and the censor Shikui, just as Yin was about to die, were able to slander Xun with plotting rebellion; they led others in joint signatures and raised their voices together to bring disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Kui and Censor Gao Shikui, seeing their chance when Yin was about to die, framed Xun for plotting rebellion, led others in joint signatures, and raised a chorus of accusation to bring disaster down on him.

sentences.zh: 郎中司馬相妄引事例，故意增減，誣上行私。

translations.literal: The bureau director Sima Xiang falsely cited precedents, deliberately adding and subtracting, and slandered his superiors for private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Director Sima Xiang falsely cited precedents, deliberately twisting them to slander his superiors for private ends.

sentences.zh: 邇者言官締黨求勝，內則奴隸公卿，外則草芥司屬，任情恣橫，殆非一日，請大奮乾斷，彰國法。」

translations.literal: Of late remonstrating officials have formed factions to seek victory; within they treat grandees as slaves, without they treat subordinates as weeds; they indulge their will and act tyrannically—this has gone on for more than a day. We beg Your Majesty to exert great decisive authority and make the national law manifest."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials of late have formed factions to win at any cost—treating grandees as servants within the court and subordinates as chaff without, indulging their will with impunity for far too long. We beg Your Majesty to act with decisive authority and make the law plain."

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，並下諸人獄，收系南京刑部。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted their words, threw all these men into prison, and detained them at the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted their argument, imprisoned all these men, and held them at the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 先是，廷臣會訊，太仆卿汪元錫、光祿少卿余才偶語曰：「此獄已得情，何再鞫？」

translations.literal: Earlier, when court officials met for joint interrogation, the Court of the Imperial Stud president Wang Yuanxi and the Court of Imperial Entertainments vice president Yu Cai happened to say to each other: "This case has already obtained the facts—why interrogate again?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when court officials met for joint interrogation, Court of the Imperial Stud President Wang Yuanxi and Court of Imperial Entertainments Vice President Yu Cai happened to remark to each other, "This case already has its facts settled—why interrogate again?"

sentences.zh: 偵者告萼，以聞，亦逮問。

translations.literal: An informer reported this to E, who passed it on; they too were arrested and questioned.
translations.idiomatic: An informer reported this to Gui E, who passed it on; they too were arrested and questioned.

sentences.zh: 萼等遂肆搒掠。

translations.literal: E and the others then freely applied beating and torture.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E and his allies then freely applied beating and torture.

sentences.zh: 錄不勝刑，自誣故入人罪。

translations.literal: Lu could not endure the punishment and confessed to deliberately imposing guilt on others.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lu could not endure the torture and confessed to deliberately imposing guilt on others.

sentences.zh: 萼等乃定爰書，言寅非福達，錄等恨勛，構成冤獄，因列諸臣罪名。

translations.literal: E and the others then fixed the written verdict, saying Yin was not Fuda, that Lu and the others bore hatred for Xun and fabricated a wrongful case, and they listed the crimes of the various officials.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E and his allies then drew up the written verdict, declaring that Yin was not Fuda, that Ma Lu and the others bore a grudge against Xun and had fabricated a wrongful case, and they listed charges against every official involved.

sentences.zh: 帝悉從其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed all their words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted everything they proposed.

sentences.zh: 謫戍極邊，遇赦不宥者五人：璋、玨、綸、豕、前山西副使遷大理少卿文華。

translations.literal: Banished to garrison the farthest frontier with no amnesty on general pardon—five men: Zhang, Jue, Lun, Shi, and the former Shanxi vice commissioner promoted to Court of Review vice president Wenhua.
translations.idiomatic: Five men were banished to garrison the farthest frontier with no amnesty on general pardon: Li Zhang, Li Jue, Zhang Lun, Ma Shi, and the former Shanxi vice commissioner who had been promoted to Court of Review Vice President Xu Wenhua.

sentences.zh: 謫戍邊衛者七人：琦、逵、泰、瓊、啟充、仕及知州胡偉。

translations.literal: Banished to garrison border guards—seven men: Qi, Kui, Tai, Qiong, Qichong, Shi, and the prefect Hu Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Seven were banished to border garrisons: Liu Qi, Zhang Kui, Chang Tai, Lu Qiong, Cheng Qichong, Liu Shi, and Prefect Hu Wei.

sentences.zh: 為民者十一人：賢、科、一鵬、祐、漢、輅、世魁、淳、鳴鳳、相、鸞。

translations.literal: Reduced to commoner status—eleven men: Xian, Ke, Yipeng, You, Han, Lu, Shikui, Chun, Mingfeng, Xiang, and Luan.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven were reduced to commoner status: Nie Xian, Wang Ke, Zheng Yipeng, Qin You, Shen Han, Cheng Lu, Gao Shikui, Ren Chun, Yao Mingfeng, Sima Xiang, and Du Luan.

sentences.zh: 革職閑住者十七人：頤壽、玉、啟、潮、文莊、沐、佖、淵、元錫、才、楷、仲賢、潤、英、壯、雄、前大理丞遷僉都御史毛伯溫。

translations.literal: Dismissed from office and left idle—seventeen men: Yishou, Yu, Qi, Chao, Wenzhuang, Mu, Yi, Yuan, Yuanxi, Cai, Kai, Zhongxian, Run, Ying, Zhuang, Xiong, and the former Court of Review vice registrar promoted to Assistant Censor-in-chief Mao Bowen.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen were dismissed and left idle: Yan Yishou, Liu Yu, Wang Qi, Jiang Chao, Liu Wenzhuang, Tang Mu, Gu Yi, Wang Yuan, Wang Yuanxi, Yu Cai, Min Kai, Zhang Zhongxian, Zhang Run, Zhang Ying, Pan Zhuang, Qi Xiong, and the former Court of Review vice registrar who had been promoted to Assistant Censor-in-chief Mao Bowen.

sentences.zh: 其他下巡按逮問革職者，副使周宣等復五人。

translations.literal: Others sent down to touring censors for arrest, questioning, and dismissal from office—five more, including the vice commissioner Zhou Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Five more, including Vice Commissioner Zhou Xuan, were sent down to touring censors for arrest, questioning, and dismissal.

sentences.zh: 良抵死，眾證皆戍，寅還職。

translations.literal: Liang was punished with death; all who had testified were banished to garrison; Yin was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Liang was put to death; everyone who had testified against Yin was banished; Yin was restored to his post.

sentences.zh: 錄以故入人死未決，當徒。

translations.literal: Lu, for deliberately imposing death on others when the case was not yet decided, was sentenced to penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lu, for deliberately imposing a capital charge before the case was settled, was sentenced to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 帝以為輕，欲坐以奸黨律斬。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought this too light and wished to punish him with execution under the statute on villainous factions.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thought this too lenient and wanted him executed under the statute on villainous factions.

sentences.zh: 萼等謂張寅未死，而錄代之死，恐天下不服，宜永戍煙瘴地，令緣及子孫。

translations.literal: E and the others said Zhang Yin was not yet dead while Lu died in his place, and they feared the realm would not be satisfied; he should be banished forever to miasmic lands, with punishment extending to descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E and his allies argued that Zhang Yin was still alive while Ma Lu had been made to die in his place, which the realm would never accept; he should be banished forever to the miasmic south, with punishment extending to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 乃戍廣西南丹衛，遇赦不宥。

translations.literal: He was then banished to garrison the Nandan Guard in Guangxi, with no amnesty on general pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished to garrison the Nandan Guard in Guangxi, with no amnesty on general pardon.

sentences.zh: 帝意猶未慊，語楊一清等曰：「與其佼及後世，不若誅止其身，從《舜典》『罰弗及嗣』之意。」

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind was still not satisfied; he said to Yang Yiqing and others: "Rather than let companions reach later generations, better to execute only his person, following the meaning of the 《Canon of Shun》, 'Punishment does not reach the heir.'"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was still not satisfied and told Yang Yiqing and others, "Rather than let his associates reach later generations, it would be better to execute only the man himself, following the 《Canon of Shun》: 'Punishment does not reach the heir.'"

sentences.zh: 一清曰：「祖宗制律具有成法，錄罪不中死律。

translations.literal: Yiqing said: "The ancestral code of laws has established statutes; Lu's crime does not fit the statutes for death.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing replied, "The ancestral code has fixed statutes; Ma Lu's crime does not warrant death under the law.

sentences.zh: 若法外用刑，吏將緣作奸，人無所措手足矣。」

translations.literal: If punishment is applied outside the law, officials will use it as a pretext for villainy and people will have nowhere to place hand or foot."
translations.idiomatic: If you punish outside the law, officials will use that as a pretext for abuse and no one will know where he stands."

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor had no choice and followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had no choice but to accept this.

sentences.zh: 以萼等平反有功，勞諭之文華殿，賜二品服俸、金帶、銀幣，給三代誥命。

translations.literal: Because E and the others had merit in reversing the wrongful case, the Emperor rewarded them with an address at the Wenhua Hall, granted second-rank salary and robes, a gold belt, and silver coins, and issued patent letters of appointment for three generations.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gui E and his allies had merit in reversing the case, the Emperor addressed them at the Wenhua Hall, granted them second-rank salary and robes, a gold belt, and silver coins, and issued patent letters of appointment for three generations.

sentences.zh: 遂編《欽明大獄錄》頒示天下。

translations.literal: He then compiled the 《Record of the Augustly Clarified Great Case》 and promulgated it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He then compiled the 《Record of the Augustly Clarified Great Case》 and promulgated it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 時嘉靖六年九月壬午也。

translations.literal: This was on the renwu day of the ninth month of the sixth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: This was on the renwu day of the ninth month of Jiajing 6.

sentences.zh: 至十六年，皇子生，肆赦。

translations.literal: By the sixteenth year a prince was born and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when a prince was born, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 諸謫戍者俱釋還，惟錄不赦，竟卒於戍所。

translations.literal: All who had been banished to garrison were released and returned, except Lu, who was not pardoned and in the end died at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: All who had been banished were released and sent home, except Ma Lu, who was not pardoned and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 顏頤壽，巴陵人，居官有清望。

translations.literal: Yan Yishou was a man of Baling and enjoyed a reputation for integrity in office.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yishou, a native of Baling, enjoyed a reputation for integrity in office.

sentences.zh: 聶賢，長壽人。

translations.literal: Nie Xian was a man of Changshou.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Xian was a native of Changshou.

sentences.zh: 為御史清廉。

translations.literal: As a censor he was pure and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: As a censor he was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 奪官五年，用薦起工部尚書，改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Deprived of office for five years, he was raised on recommendation to Minister of Works and then transferred to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: After five years out of office he was raised on recommendation to Minister of Works, then transferred to Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and died.

sentences.zh: 謚榮襄。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Rongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Rongxiang.

sentences.zh: 湯沐，字新之，江陰人。

translations.literal: Tang Mu, style name Xinzhi, was a man of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Mu, whose style was Xinzhi, was a native of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the ninth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Hongzhi 9.

sentences.zh: 除崇德知縣，征授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Chongde, then summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Chongde, then summoned and made a censor.

sentences.zh: 正德初，嘗劾中官苗逵、保國公朱暉等罪，出為湖廣僉事。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengde he once impeached the eunuch Miao Kui, the Duke of Baoguo Zhu Hui, and others for crimes, and was sent out as an assistant surveillance commissioner in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he impeached the eunuch Miao Kui, the Duke of Baoguo Zhu Hui, and others, and was sent out as an assistant surveillance commissioner in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾以沐不附己，用牙儈同寅訐學士張芮事波及沐，謫武義知縣。

translations.literal: Liu Jin, because Mu would not attach himself to him, used a broker named Tong Yin to denounce Academician Zhang Rui in an affair that implicated Mu, and Mu was demoted to magistrate of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Because Mu would not attach himself to Liu Jin, Jin used a broker named Tong Yin to denounce Academician Zhang Rui in a case that implicated Mu, and Mu was demoted to magistrate of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復為廣東僉事。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Mu was restored as an assistant surveillance commissioner in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's execution he was restored as an assistant surveillance commissioner in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 累遷右副都御史，巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: He rose through successive posts to Right Vice Censor-in-chief and surveillance commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Right Vice Censor-in-chief and Surveillance Commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 請立土官世系籍，絕其爭襲之弊，而令其子弟入學，報可。

translations.literal: He requested establishing registers of hereditary native-official lineages to end the abuse of contested succession, and that their sons and younger brothers enter schools; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He requested registers of hereditary native-official lineages to end disputed successions and required their sons and younger brothers to enter schools; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年改撫四川，入為大理卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Sichuan, then entered the capital as president of the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 2 he was transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan, then entered the capital as Court of Review president.

sentences.zh: 既坐福達獄罷歸，家居六年，薦章數十上，不召，卒。

translations.literal: After he was implicated in the Fuda case and dismissed to return home, he lived at home for six years; dozens of recommendation memorials were submitted but he was not summoned, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: After he was caught up in the Fuda case and sent home, he lived in retirement for six years; dozens of recommendation memorials were submitted but he was never summoned, and he died.

sentences.zh: 沐居官三十載，屏絕饋遺，以廉潔稱。

translations.literal: Mu held office for thirty years, rejected all gifts, and was known for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Mu held office for thirty years, refused all gifts, and was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 劉琦，字廷珍，洛川人。

translations.literal: Liu Qi, style name Tingzhen, was a man of Luochuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi, whose style was Tingzhen, was a native of Luochuan.

sentences.zh: 正德九年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the ninth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Zhengde 9.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，由行人授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing he went from courier to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he went from courier to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時給京軍冬衣布棉恒過期，以琦請，即命琦立給。

translations.literal: At the time winter clothing of cloth and cotton for the capital garrison was always late; on Qi's request the Emperor immediately ordered Qi to distribute it at once.
translations.idiomatic: Winter cloth and cotton for the capital garrison were always late; at Qi's request the Emperor ordered him to distribute them immediately.

sentences.zh: 李福達逃洛川，琦知之甚悉。

translations.literal: Li Fuda fled to Luochuan; Qi knew the matter very thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Fuda fled to Luochuan, Qi knew the affair in full detail.

sentences.zh: 事覺，琦疏陳顛末，因劾郭勛黨逆，又與御史張問行劾勛侵盜草場租銀。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, Qi memorialized setting forth the whole course of events, impeached Guo Xun for complicity in treason, and together with Censor Zhang Wenxing impeached Xun for encroaching on and embezzling pasture-land rent silver.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was uncovered, Qi memorialized with the full story, impeached Guo Xun for complicity in treason, and together with Censor Zhang Wenxing charged Xun with encroaching on and embezzling pasture-land rent silver.

sentences.zh: 既而馬錄獄具，坐琦佐使殺人，下獄，謫戍沈陽。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, when Ma Lu's case was completed, Qi was convicted of aiding him in causing a man's death, imprisoned, and banished to garrison Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Lu's case was concluded, Qi was convicted of helping him secure a wrongful death sentence, imprisoned, and banished to Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 閱十年赦歸，卒。

translations.literal: After ten years he was pardoned and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years he was pardoned and sent home, then died.

sentences.zh: 盧瓊，字獻卿，浮梁人。

translations.literal: Lu Qiong, style name Xianqing, was a man of Fuliang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qiong, whose style was Xianqing, was a native of Fuliang.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Zhengde 6.

sentences.zh: 由固始知縣入為御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Gushi he entered service as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from magistrate of Gushi to censor.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖改元，上言：「景皇帝有撥亂大功，而實錄猶稱郕戾王。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title in Jiajing he memorialized: "The Jing Emperor had great merit in restoring order from chaos, yet the Veritable Record still calls him the Depraved Prince of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he memorialized: "The Jing Emperor had great merit in restoring order from chaos, yet the Veritable Record still calls him the Depraved Prince of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 敬皇帝深仁厚澤，而實錄成於焦芳手，是非顛倒。

translations.literal: The Jing Emperor was deep in benevolence and thick in grace, yet the Veritable Record was completed at Jiao Fang's hand, with right and wrong inverted.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing Emperor was deeply benevolent, yet the Veritable Record was written at Jiao Fang's hand, with right and wrong inverted.

sentences.zh: 乞詔儒臣改撰。」

translations.literal: I beg that Confucian officials be ordered to rewrite them."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Confucian officials be ordered to rewrite them."

sentences.zh: 帝惟命史官正《孝宗實錄》之不當者，然亦未有所正也。

translations.literal: The Emperor only ordered the historiographers to correct what was improper in the Veritable Record of Xiaozong, yet in fact nothing was corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor only ordered the historiographers to correct improper passages in the Veritable Record of Xiaozong, but in fact nothing was changed.

sentences.zh: 出按畿輔。

translations.literal: He went out as touring censor for the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched as touring censor for the capital region.

sentences.zh: 桂萼疾臺諫排己，考察京官既竣，令科道互糾劾。

translations.literal: Gui E resented the remonstrance bureaus for excluding him; after the capital officials' inspection was finished, he ordered the supervising secretaries and censors to impeach one another.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E resented the remonstrance bureaus for shutting him out; after the capital officials' inspection ended, he ordered supervising secretaries and censors to impeach one another.

sentences.zh: 吏科都給事中王俊民等爭之，瓊與同官劉隅等亦言交相批抵報復，非盛世事。

translations.literal: Wang Junmin, chief supervising secretary of the Bureau of Personnel, and others protested; Qiong and his colleague Liu Yu also said that mutual denunciation and retaliation were not affairs of a flourishing age.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junmin, chief supervising secretary of the Bureau of Personnel, and others protested; Qiong and his colleague Liu Yu argued that mutual denunciation and retaliation were unworthy of a flourishing age.

sentences.zh: 帝切責俊民、隅，奪其俸五月，瓊等皆三月，而命部院考之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sharply rebuked Junmin and Yu, stripped their salaries for five months, stripped Qiong and the others for three months, and ordered the ministries and courts to inspect them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sharply rebuked Junmin and Yu, stripped their salaries for five months and Qiong and the others for three, and ordered the ministries and courts to inspect them.

sentences.zh: 瓊竟以劾勛謫戍邊。

translations.literal: Qiong in the end was banished to garrison the frontier for impeaching Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was ultimately banished to a frontier garrison for impeaching Xun.

sentences.zh: 赦還，卒。

translations.literal: Pardoned and returned, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was pardoned and sent home, then died.

sentences.zh: 沈漢，字宗海，吳江人。

translations.literal: Shen Han, style name Zonghai, was a man of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Han, whose style was Zonghai, was a native of Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the sixteenth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Zhengde 16.

sentences.zh: 授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He became supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 中官馬俊、王堂久廢，忽自南京召至，漢論止之。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Ma Jun and Wang Tang had long been dismissed, but were suddenly summoned from Nanjing; Han argued that this should be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs Ma Jun and Wang Tang had long been dismissed but were suddenly summoned from Nanjing; Han argued that this should be stopped.

sentences.zh: 改元詔書蠲四方逋稅，漢以民間已納者多飽吏橐，請已征未解者，作來年正課。

translations.literal: The edict on the change of reign title remitted overdue taxes from all quarters; Han, because much that the people had already paid had filled officials' purses, requested that what had been collected but not remitted be counted as the next year's regular levy.
translations.idiomatic: The edict on the change of reign title remitted overdue taxes everywhere; Han argued that much of what the people had already paid had filled officials' purses and asked that collections not yet remitted be counted as the next year's regular levy.

sentences.zh: 又言近籍沒奸黨貲數千萬，請悉發以補歲入不足之數。

translations.literal: He also said that recently confiscated property of villainous factions amounted to tens of millions and begged that it all be disbursed to make up the shortfall in annual revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that the tens of millions recently confiscated from villainous factions be disbursed to cover the shortfall in annual revenue.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，以災異指斥時政。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he used omens and disasters to criticize current policy.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 2 he used omens and disasters to criticize current policy.

sentences.zh: 尚書林俊去位，復抗章爭之。

translations.literal: When Minister Lin Jun left his post, Han again submitted a defiant memorial protesting it.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Lin Jun was removed, Han submitted another defiant memorial in protest.

sentences.zh: 戶部郎中牟泰坐吏盜官帑，下詔獄貶官。

translations.literal: Mou Tai, bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, was implicated because clerks embezzled official funds; he was sent to the imperial prison and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Tai, a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, was implicated when clerks embezzled official funds; he was sent to the imperial prison and demoted.

sentences.zh: 漢言：「吏為奸利，在泰未任前。

translations.literal: Han said: "The clerks profited by villainy before Tai took office.
translations.idiomatic: Han said, "The clerks' fraud predated Tai's appointment.

sentences.zh: 事敗，泰發之。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, Tai reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When the fraud came to light, Tai was the one who exposed it.

sentences.zh: 泰無罪。」

translations.literal: Tai is without guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Tai is innocent."

sentences.zh: 因極言刑獄宜付法司，毋委鎮撫。

translations.literal: He therefore strongly urged that criminal cases should be entrusted to the judicial offices and not delegated to the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He strongly urged that criminal cases belong in the judicial offices, not with the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: This was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not accept this.

sentences.zh: 大獄起，法司皆下吏。

translations.literal: When the great case arose, the judicial officials were all thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: When the great case broke, the judicial officials were all imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 漢言：「祖宗之法不可壞，權幸之漸不可長，大臣不可辱，妖賊不可赦。」

translations.literal: Han said: "The laws of the ancestors cannot be destroyed; the encroachment of the powerful and favored cannot be allowed to grow; grand ministers cannot be humiliated; demonic rebels cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Han said, "The laws of the ancestors cannot be broken; the power of favorites cannot be allowed to grow; grand ministers cannot be humiliated; heretic rebels cannot be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 遂並漢收系，除其名。

translations.literal: Han too was then arrested and his name struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Han was arrested as well and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 家居二十年，卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for twenty years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for twenty years, then died.

sentences.zh: 曾孫璟，萬歷中為吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Jing, in the Wanli reign, was an assistant department director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Jing served in the Wanli reign as an assistant department director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 請王恭妃封號，忤旨，降行人司正。

translations.literal: He requested a title for Lady Wang the Respectful Consort; defying the imperial will, he was demoted to registrar of the Courier Service.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a title for Lady Wang the Respectful Consort; defying the imperial will, he was demoted to registrar of the Courier Service.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，贈少卿。

translations.literal: Early in Tianqi he was posthumously made vice president.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was posthumously made a vice president.

sentences.zh: 王科，字進卿，涉縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Ke, style name Jinqing, was a man of She County.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke, whose style was Jinqing, was a native of She County.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Zhengde 12.

sentences.zh: 授藍田知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: He served first as magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 城隘，且無水，科導西山水入城，拓而廣之，遂為望邑。

translations.literal: The city was narrow and had no water; Ke led water from the western hills into the city, expanded and widened it, and it became a renowned county seat.
translations.idiomatic: The city was cramped and had no water; Ke brought water from the western hills into town, expanded the walls, and turned it into a renowned county seat.

sentences.zh: 毀境內淫祠，以其材葺學宮。

translations.literal: He destroyed illicit shrines within the jurisdiction and used their materials to repair the school.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed illicit shrines in the county and used their materials to repair the school.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年征為工科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiajing he was summoned as supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 4 he was summoned as supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works.

sentences.zh: 嘗劾兵部尚書金獻民無功，總兵官趙文、種勛失事，及陜西織造內官擾民，郭勛任奸人郭彪、鄭鸞，剝軍害民狀。

translations.literal: He once impeached Minister of War Jin Xianmin for lack of merit, the regional commanders Zhao Wen and Zhong Xun for failures, the Shaanxi weaving eunuch for harassing the people, and Guo Xun for employing the villains Guo Biao and Zheng Luan and stripping the army to harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Minister of War Jin Xianmin for lack of merit, regional commanders Zhao Wen and Zhong Xun for military failures, the Shaanxi weaving eunuch for harassing the people, and Guo Xun for employing the villains Guo Biao and Zheng Luan and stripping the army to harm the people.

sentences.zh: 又言：「三司首領、州縣佐貳以秩卑為上官所輕棄，率貪冒不自惜，宜拔擢其廉能者。

translations.literal: He also said: "The heads of the three commissions and the assistant officials of prefectures and counties, because their rank is low, are lightly abandoned by their superiors and generally are greedy and reckless without restraint; those who are incorrupt and capable should be promoted.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Heads of the three commissions and prefectural and county deputies, being low in rank, were neglected by superiors and often grew greedy and reckless, and that the incorrupt and capable should be promoted.

sentences.zh: 而諸邊財計之職，不宜處下才。

translations.literal: The fiscal posts on the frontiers should not be filled with inferior talent.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier fiscal posts should not be filled with inferior talent.

sentences.zh: 鹽運官廉，當遷敘。」

translations.literal: Salt transport officials who are incorrupt should be promoted in rank."
translations.idiomatic: Incorrupt salt transport officials should be promoted."

sentences.zh: 大獄起，劾勛，遂下獄削籍。

translations.literal: When the great case arose he impeached Xun, was imprisoned, and was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When the great case broke he impeached Xun, was imprisoned, and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 方諸臣之被罪也，舉朝皆知其冤，莫敢白。

translations.literal: When the various officials were punished, the whole court knew they were wronged, but none dared speak for them.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials were punished, the whole court knew they were wronged, but none dared speak up.

sentences.zh: 逾月，南京御史吳彥獨抗章請寬之。

translations.literal: After more than a month the Nanjing censor Wu Yan alone submitted a defiant memorial asking that they be treated leniently.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later the Nanjing censor Wu Yan alone submitted a defiant memorial asking leniency for them.

sentences.zh: 上怒，斥於外。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and expelled him to the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and expelled him to the provinces.

sentences.zh: 已而御史張祿亦以為言。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Censor Zhang Lu also spoke to the same effect.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Censor Zhang Lu spoke to the same effect.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，切讓。

translations.literal: Defying the imperial will, he was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Defying the imperial will, he was sharply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 自是無敢言者。

translations.literal: From then on none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: After that no one dared speak.

sentences.zh: 十一年，桂萼已死，張璁亦免相，聶賢、毛伯溫始起用。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Gui E was already dead, Zhang Cong was also removed from the chancellorship, and Nie Xian and Mao Bowen were first raised to office again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Gui E was dead, Zhang Cong had left the chancellorship, and Nie Xian and Mao Bowen were restored to office.

sentences.zh: 張潤、汪元錫、李玨、閔楷亦相繼收錄。

translations.literal: Zhang Run, Wang Yuanxi, Li Jue, and Min Kai were also taken back into service in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Run, Wang Yuanxi, Li Jue, and Min Kai were also brought back in succession.

sentences.zh: 唯臺諫、曹郎竟無一人召復者。

translations.literal: Only among the remonstrance officials and bureau section chiefs was there not a single person summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Not a single remonstrance official or bureau section chief was summoned back.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，諸人皆復職贈官。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing all these men had their offices restored and were given posthumous ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign all were restored to office and given posthumous ranks.

sentences.zh: 錄首贈太仆少卿，琦、瓊俱光祿少卿，漢、科俱太常少卿。

translations.literal: Lu was first given posthumous rank as vice president of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Qi and Qiong were both made vice presidents of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Han and Ke were both made vice presidents of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lu was first posthumously made vice president of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Liu Qi and Lu Qiong vice presidents of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Shen Han and Wang Ke vice presidents of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 當萼等反福達之獄，舉朝不直萼等。而以寅、福達姓名錯互，亦或疑之。至四十五年正月，四川大盜蔡伯貫就擒。自言學妖術於山西李同。所司檄山西，捕同下獄。同供為李午之孫，大禮之子，世習白蓮教，假稱唐裔，惑眾倡亂，與大獄錄姓名無異，同竟伏誅。暨穆宗即位，御史龐尚鵬言：「據李同之獄，福達罪益彰，而當時流毒縉紳至四十餘人。衣冠之禍，可謂慘烈。郭勛世受國恩，乃黨巨盜，陷朝紳。職樞要者承其頤指，鍛煉周內。萬一陰蓄異謀，人人聽命，禍可勝言哉！乞追奪勛等官爵，優恤馬錄諸人，以作忠良之氣。」由是，福達獄始明。

translations.literal: When Gui E and the others overturned the case of Fu Da, the whole court knew E and the others were not right. But because the names of Yin and Fu Da were confused and interchanged, some also had doubts. In the first month of the forty-fifth year, the great Sichuan bandit Cai Boguan was captured. He said himself that he had learned sorcery from Li Tong of Shanxi. The authorities sent orders to Shanxi, arrested Tong, and imprisoned him. Tong confessed that he was the grandson of Li Wu and the son of Dali, that his family had practiced the White Lotus teaching for generations, and that he had falsely claimed Tang descent to delude the masses and instigate rebellion. His names did not differ from those in the Record of the Great Prison, and Tong was ultimately executed. When Muzong ascended the throne, Censor Pang Shangpeng said: "According to Li Tong's case, Fu Da's crimes are all the more manifest, while at the time his poison spread among more than forty gentry officials. The disaster to the ranks of caps and gowns may be called tragic and severe. Guo Xun had received state favor for generations, yet he joined with a great bandit and trapped court gentlemen. Those occupying pivotal offices followed his nods and gestures, forging charges and enclosing them all around. If by any chance he had secretly harbored treasonous designs, with everyone obeying his orders, how could the disaster be fully described? I request that Xun and the others be posthumously stripped of office and rank, and that Ma Lu and the others be generously consoled, in order to stir the spirit of loyal and good men." From this, the Fu Da case first became clear.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui E and the others reversed the Fu Da case, the whole court knew they were wrong. Yet because the names of Yin and Fu Da had become confused, some still had doubts. In the first month of Jiajing 45, the great Sichuan bandit Cai Boguan was captured. He said he had learned sorcery from Li Tong of Shanxi. Officials ordered Shanxi to arrest Tong, and he confessed that he was Li Wu's grandson and Dali's son, that his family had long practiced the White Lotus teaching, and that he had falsely claimed Tang descent to deceive the people and incite rebellion. His names matched those in the Record of the Great Prison, and Tong was executed. When Muzong came to the throne, Censor Pang Shangpeng said, "From Li Tong's case, Fu Da's crime is clearer than ever, while at the time its poison spread to more than forty gentry officials. The calamity that befell the official class may truly be called tragic. Guo Xun had received state favor for generations, yet he sided with a great bandit and entrapped court officials. Those in pivotal posts obeyed his every gesture, forging charges and hemming men in. If he had secretly harbored treasonous designs and everyone obeyed his orders, how could the disaster have been described? I request that Xun and the others be stripped posthumously of office and rank, and that Ma Lu and the others be generously consoled, to encourage the spirit of loyal and worthy men." From this point, the Fu Da case became clear.

sentences.zh: 程啟充，字以道，嘉定州人。

translations.literal: Cheng Qichong, style name Yidao, was a man of Jiading Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Qichong, whose style was Yidao, was a native of Jiading Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Zhengde 3.

sentences.zh: 除三原知縣，入為御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Sanyuan, then entered service as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Sanyuan, then made a censor.

sentences.zh: 嬖幸子弟家人濫冒軍功，有至都督賜蟒玉者。

translations.literal: Sons and household members of favored intimates fraudulently claimed military merit, some reaching regional commander and receiving python robes and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Sons and household members of imperial favorites fraudulently claimed military merit, some rising to regional commander and receiving python robes and jade.

sentences.zh: 啟充言：「定制，軍職授官，悉準首功。

translations.literal: Qichong said: "By established regulation, military appointments are all based on the first merit claim.
translations.idiomatic: Qichong said, "By regulation, military appointments must all be based on the primary merit claim.

sentences.zh: 今幸門大啟，有買功、冒功、寄名、竄名、並功之弊。

translations.literal: Now the gate of favor is wide open, with the abuses of bought merit, false merit, borrowed names, altered names, and combined merit.
translations.idiomatic: Now the gate of favor stands wide open, with bought merit, false merit, borrowed names, altered records, and combined merit.

sentences.zh: 權要家賄軍士金帛，以易所獲之級，是謂買功。

translations.literal: Powerful families bribe soldiers with gold and silk to exchange for the grades they had obtained—this is called bought merit.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families bribe soldiers with gold and silk to buy the merit grades they had earned—this is bought merit.

sentences.zh: 沖鋒斬馘者，甲也，而乙取之，甚者殺平民以為賊，是謂冒功。

translations.literal: The one who charged and beheaded the enemy was A, but B took the credit; in extreme cases they killed commoners and called them bandits—this is called false merit.
translations.idiomatic: The man who charged and took heads was A, but B claimed the credit; in the worst cases they killed civilians and called them bandits—this is false merit.

sentences.zh: 身不出門閭，而名隸行伍，是謂寄名。

translations.literal: The body never left the neighborhood gate, yet the name was enrolled in the ranks—this is called borrowed name.
translations.idiomatic: A man never left his neighborhood, yet his name appeared on the rolls—this is a borrowed name.

sentences.zh: 賄求掾吏，洗補文冊，是謂竄名。

translations.literal: Bribing clerks to wash and amend the documents—this is called altered name.
translations.idiomatic: Bribing clerks to alter the documents—this is an altered record.

sentences.zh: 至有一人之身，一日之間，不出京師，而東西南朔四處報功者，按名累級，驟至高階，是謂並功。

translations.literal: There were even cases of a single person in a single day, without leaving the capital, reporting merit in all four directions east, west, south, and north; by accumulating names and grades he suddenly rose to high rank—this is called combined merit.
translations.idiomatic: There were even men who in a single day, without leaving the capital, reported merit in all four directions; by accumulating names and grades they shot to high rank—this is combined merit.

sentences.zh: 此皆壞祖宗法，解將士體，乞嚴為察革。」

translations.literal: All these destroy the laws of the ancestors and dissolve the discipline of officers and soldiers; I beg that they be strictly investigated and reformed."
translations.idiomatic: All of this destroys ancestral law and undermines military discipline; I beg that it be strictly investigated and reformed."

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: The Emperor could not employ this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not act on this advice.

sentences.zh: 十一年正旦，群臣待漏入賀，日晡禮始成。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the eleventh year the officials waited for the water-clock drip to enter and offer congratulations; the ceremony was not completed until the sun was in the west.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the eleventh year officials waited for the water-clock to enter court and offer congratulations; the ceremony was not finished until late afternoon.

sentences.zh: 及散朝，已昏夜。

translations.literal: When court was dismissed it was already dark night.
translations.idiomatic: When court was dismissed it was already night.

sentences.zh: 眾奔趨而出，顛仆相踐踏。

translations.literal: The crowd rushed out, falling and trampling one another.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd rushed out, tripping and trampling one another.

sentences.zh: 將軍趙朗者，死於禁門。

translations.literal: The general Zhao Lang died at the forbidden gate.
translations.idiomatic: General Zhao Lang died at the forbidden gate.

sentences.zh: 啟充具奏其狀，請帝昧爽視朝，以圖明作之治。

translations.literal: Qichong fully memorialized the situation and asked the Emperor to hold court at dawn to seek enlightened governance.
translations.idiomatic: Qichong memorialized the full account and asked the Emperor to hold dawn court in pursuit of enlightened rule.

sentences.zh: 都督馬昂進妊身女弟，啟充等力爭。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Ma Ang presented his pregnant younger sister; Qichong and others strongly protested.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Ma Ang presented his pregnant younger sister to the palace; Qichong and others protested vigorously.

sentences.zh: 既又極陳冗官、冗兵、冗費之弊，乞通行革罷。

translations.literal: He then also strongly set forth the abuses of redundant officials, redundant troops, and redundant expenditures, begging that they be abolished throughout.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out the abuses of redundant officials, troops, and expenditures and asked that they be abolished throughout the government.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不省。

translations.literal: The Emperor paid no attention to any of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 騰驤四衛軍改編各衛者，奉詔撤回，而各衛遺籍仍支糧，糜倉儲八十七萬余石。

translations.literal: Soldiers of the four Tengxiang guards who had been reassigned to various guards were ordered by edict to return, yet the leftover registers of the various guards still drew grain pay, wasting more than 870,000 piculs of granary stores.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers of the four Tengxiang guards reassigned to other guards were ordered back by edict, yet leftover rolls still drew grain pay, wasting more than 870,000 piculs from the granaries.

sentences.zh: 啟充力言之，冒支弊絕。

translations.literal: Qichong strongly urged this, and the abuse of false claims was ended.
translations.idiomatic: Qichong pressed the point hard, and the abuse of false claims ended.

sentences.zh: 以憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，起故官，即爭興獻帝皇號。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, Qichong was raised to his former post and immediately contested the imperial title for the Jingxian Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor took the throne, Qichong was restored to his former post and immediately contested the imperial title for the Jingxian Emperor.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年正月郊祀方畢，清寧宮小房火。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Jiajing, just as the suburban sacrifice was finished, a small room of the Qingning Palace caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jiajing 1, just as the suburban sacrifice ended, a small room in the Qingning Palace caught fire.

sentences.zh: 啟充言：「災及內寢，良由徇情之禮有戾天常，僭逼之名深乖典則。

translations.literal: Qichong said: "The disaster reached the inner quarters, truly because partial rites violated heaven's constant and usurping titles deeply departed from canonical norms.
translations.idiomatic: Qichong said, "The disaster reached the inner quarters because partial rites violated heaven's constant and usurping titles departed deeply from canonical norms.

sentences.zh: 輔臣執議，禮臣建明，不能敵經生之邪說，佞幸之諛辭，動假母後以箝天下之口。

translations.literal: Assisting ministers held to their views and ritual officials made them clear, yet they could not withstand the heterodox doctrines of classicists and the flattery of sycophants, who constantly used the empress dowager to clamp shut the mouths of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Assisting ministers held firm and ritual officials spoke clearly, yet they could not withstand the heterodox doctrines of classicists and the flattery of sycophants, who constantly used the empress dowager to silence the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣謂不正大禮，不黜邪說，所謂修省皆具文也。

translations.literal: Your subject maintains that without rectifying the great rites and not dismissing heterodox doctrines, what is called self-examination is all empty form.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject maintains that without rectifying the great rites and dismissing heterodox doctrines, what is called self-examination is mere empty form.

sentences.zh: 況邇者旨由中出而內閣不知，奸黨獄成而曲為庇護。

translations.literal: Moreover, of late edicts have issued from within while the Grand Secretariat did not know; villainous factions' cases were completed yet were crookedly sheltered.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, edicts of late have issued from within while the Grand Secretariat knew nothing; villainous factions' cases were settled yet crookedly sheltered.

sentences.zh: 諫臣斥逐，耳目有壅蔽之虞；

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials were expelled and driven away—there is the worry that ears and eyes will be blocked;
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials have been expelled—there is danger that the Emperor's ears and eyes will be blocked;

sentences.zh: 大臣疏遠，股肱有痿痹之患。

translations.literal: grand ministers are kept at a distance—the limbs have the affliction of numb paralysis.
translations.idiomatic: grand ministers are kept at a distance—the throne's limbs suffer numb paralysis.

sentences.zh: 司禮之權重於宰相，樞機之地委之宦官。

translations.literal: The power of the Directorate of Ceremonial is heavier than that of the chancellor, and the place of vital mechanisms is entrusted to eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Ceremonial outweighs the chancellor, and vital mechanisms are entrusted to eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 邇臣貪濁，頻有遷除；

translations.literal: recent officials are greedy and corrupt, yet frequently receive transfers and appointments;
translations.idiomatic: Recent officials are greedy and corrupt, yet are frequently promoted;

sentences.zh: 邊帥僨師，不聞譴斥。

translations.literal: frontier commanders ruin their armies, yet one hears no reprimand or dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: frontier commanders ruin their armies, yet one hears no reprimand.

sentences.zh: 莊田之賞賚過多，潛邸之乞恩未已。

translations.literal: Rewards of estate fields are excessive, and petitions for favor from the former princely residence have not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards of estate fields are excessive, and petitions for favor from the former princely residence have not ceased.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下仰畏天明，俯察眾聽，親大臣，肅庶政，以回災變。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will look up in awe of heaven's brightness, look down and examine the multitude's hearing, be close to grand ministers, rectify common administration, and thereby turn back calamitous change."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will look up in awe of heaven, look down and heed the people, be close to grand ministers, rectify common administration, and thereby turn back calamity."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The memorial was noted.
translations.idiomatic: The court acknowledged receipt of the memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋出按江西。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as touring censor for Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was dispatched as touring censor to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 得宸濠通蕭敬、張銳、陸完等私書，欲亟去孫燧，云：「代者湯沐、梁宸可，其次王守仁亦可。」

translations.literal: He obtained private letters from Prince of Ning Chen Hao to Xiao Jing, Zhang Rui, Lu Wan, and others, wishing urgently to remove Sun Sui, saying: "As replacements Tang Mu or Liang Chen would do; next, Wang Shouren would also do."
translations.idiomatic: He obtained private letters from the Prince of Ning to Xiao Jing, Zhang Rui, Lu Wan, and others urgently seeking Sun Sui's removal, saying, "Tang Mu or Liang Chen would do as replacements; next, Wang Shouren would also do."

sentences.zh: 因論敬、銳等罪，並言守仁黨逆，宜追奪。

translations.literal: He then discussed the crimes of Jing, Rui, and the rest, and also stated that Shouren had joined the rebels and should have his honors stripped.
translations.idiomatic: He then reviewed the crimes of Jing, Rui, and the others, and argued that Shouren had sided with the rebel and that his titles should be revoked.

sentences.zh: 給事中汪應軫訟守仁功，言：「逆濠私書，有詔焚毀。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Wang Yingzhen argued for Shouren's merits, saying: "The private letters of the rebel Prince of Ning—an edict had ordered them burned.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wang Yingzhen spoke up for Shouren's service, saying, "The Prince of Ning's private letters were already ordered burned by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 啟充輕信被黜知縣章立梅捃摭之辭，復有此奏，非所以勸有功。」

translations.literal: Qichong lightly believed the collected phrases of the dismissed magistrate Zhang Limai, and again submitted this memorial—this is not the way to encourage those with merit."
translations.idiomatic: Qichong credulously accepted the gathered accusations of dismissed magistrate Zhang Limai and submitted this memorial again—hardly the way to reward meritorious service."

sentences.zh: 主事陸澄亦為守仁奏辨。

translations.literal: The section chief Lu Cheng also submitted a memorial in Shouren's defense.
translations.idiomatic: Section chief Lu Cheng likewise submitted a memorial defending Shouren.

sentences.zh: 御史向信因劾應軫與澄。

translations.literal: The censor Xiang Xin thereupon impeached Yingzhen and Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xiang Xin thereupon impeached Yingzhen and Cheng.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「守仁一聞宸濠變，仗義興兵，戡定大難，特加封爵，以酬大功，不必更議。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "As soon as Shouren heard of Chen Hao's rebellion, he took up righteousness and raised troops, quelled the great crisis, was specially ennobled to repay great merit—there is no need for further discussion."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "When Shouren first heard of the Prince of Ning's revolt, he acted on principle and raised an army, ending the crisis. He was specially ennobled to reward that great service, and the matter need not be reopened."

sentences.zh: 帝從太監梁棟請，遣中官督南京織造。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted the eunuch Liang Dong's request and dispatched a palace eunuch to supervise the Nanjing textile works.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved eunuch Liang Dong's request and sent a palace eunuch to oversee the Nanjing imperial workshops.

sentences.zh: 啟充偕同官及科臣張嵩等極諫，不納。

translations.literal: Qichong joined his colleagues and the department official Zhang Song and others in strongly remonstrating; they were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Qichong joined his colleagues and department official Zhang Song and others in strong remonstrance, but the Emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 啟充素蹇諤，張璁、桂萼惡之。

translations.literal: Qichong had always been upright and outspoken; Zhang Cong and Gui E hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Qichong had always been blunt and forthright, and Zhang Cong and Gui E resented him.

sentences.zh: 會郭勛庇李福達獄，為啟充所劾，璁、萼因指啟充挾私，謫戍邊衛。

translations.literal: When Guo Xun shielded those in the Li Fuda case and was impeached by Qichong, Cong and E took the occasion to accuse Qichong of harboring private motives and had him demoted to serve in a border garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Xun shielded defendants in the Li Fuda case and Qichong impeached him, Cong and E seized the chance to accuse Qichong of personal bias and had him banished to a frontier garrison.

sentences.zh: 十六年赦還。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was pardoned and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 言者交薦，不復用，卒。

translations.literal: Memorialists repeatedly recommended him, yet he was not reemployed, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Officials repeatedly recommended him, but he was never reappointed, and he died.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Longqing reign he was posthumously appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 張逵，字懋登，余姚人。正德十六年進士。改庶吉士。嘉靖元年，授刑科給事中。疏言：「陛下臨御之初，國是大定。今舉動漸乖，弊端旋復。齋醮繁興，爵賞無紀。政事不關於宰執者非一，刑罰不行於貴近者甚多。臺諫會奏而斥為瀆擾，大臣執法而責以回奏。至如崔元封侯，蔣輪市寵，陳萬言乞賜第，先朝貴戚未有若是恩幸也。廖鵬緩死，劉暉得官，李隆復遣官勘問，先朝罪人未有若是淹縱也。願陛下一反目前之所為。」報聞。給事中劉最、鄧繼曾謫官，逵疏救，不聽。尋伏闕爭「大禮」，下獄廷杖。

translations.literal: Zhang Kui, courtesy name Maodeng, was from Yuyao. He became a jinshi in the sixteenth year of Zhengde and was transferred to be a shujishi. In the first year of Jiajing, he was appointed Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Justice. He memorialized: "At the beginning of Your Majesty's rule, the fundamental policy of the state was greatly settled. Now actions and movements are gradually deviating, and abuses are swiftly returning. Daoist fasts and offerings flourish, while titles and rewards lack order. There is more than one matter of government that does not concern the chief ministers, and very many punishments are not carried out against the honored and near. Joint memorials from the censorate and remonstrance officials are dismissed as disturbance, and great ministers who uphold the law are blamed with demands for further replies. As for such matters as Cui Yuan being enfeoffed as marquis, Jiang Lun buying favor, and Chen Wanyan begging to be granted a mansion, no noble relatives of the former reign received such favor and fortune. Liao Peng had his death delayed, Liu Hui obtained office, and Li Long was again investigated by dispatched officials; no criminals of the former reign received such delay and indulgence. I hope Your Majesty will completely reverse present conduct." The memorial was noted. When Supervising Secretaries Liu Zui and Deng Jizeng were demoted, Kui submitted a memorial to save them, but it was not accepted. Soon he prostrated himself at the palace gate to contest the "Great Rites," was imprisoned, and was flogged at court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kui, courtesy name Maodeng, was a native of Yuyao. He became a jinshi in Zhengde 16 and was made a shujishi. In Jiajing 1 he was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice. He memorialized, "At the start of Your Majesty's reign, the state's fundamental policy was firmly settled. Now imperial conduct is gradually going astray and old abuses are quickly returning. Daoist rites are proliferating, titles and rewards have no order, many affairs of government bypass the chief ministers, and punishments often do not reach favored intimates. Joint memorials from censors and remonstrance officials are denounced as harassment, and great ministers who uphold the law are rebuked and ordered to reply again. Cui Yuan has been enfeoffed as marquis, Jiang Lun buys favor, and Chen Wanyan begs for a mansion; no imperial relatives in the former reign enjoyed such favor. Liao Peng has had death delayed, Liu Hui obtained office, and Li Long was again investigated by dispatched officials; no criminals of the former reign enjoyed such indulgence. I hope Your Majesty will completely reverse present practice." The memorial was noted. When Supervising Secretaries Liu Zui and Deng Jizeng were demoted, Kui memorialized to save them, but was not heeded. Soon he prostrated himself at the palace gate to contest the "Great Rites," was imprisoned, and was flogged at court.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月上疏曰：「近廷臣所上封事，陛下批答必曰『已有旨處置』，是已行者不可言也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year he submitted a memorial saying: "Of late, in sealed memorials submitted by court ministers, Your Majesty's written responses always say 'the matter has already been ordered disposed'—meaning what has already been done may not be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth year he submitted a memorial: "Lately, when court ministers submit sealed memorials, Your Majesty's replies always say, 'Orders have already been issued'—as if what is already done cannot be discussed.

sentences.zh: 曰『尚議處未定』，是未行者不可言也。

translations.literal: If the reply says 'still under deliberation, not yet decided,' that means what has not yet been done may not be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: If the reply says, 'Still under deliberation,' that means what has not yet been done cannot be discussed either.

sentences.zh: 二者不言，則是終無可言也。

translations.literal: If neither may be spoken of, then in the end there is nothing that can be said.
translations.idiomatic: If neither may be discussed, then in the end there is nothing left to say at all.

sentences.zh: 且今日言者，已非陛下初政時比矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who speak today already cannot compare with the time of Your Majesty's early administration.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those who speak out today are nothing like they were in the early years of Your Majesty's reign.

sentences.zh: 初年，事之大者，既會疏公言之，又各疏獨言之。

translations.literal: In the early years, on major matters, they would first speak jointly in collective memorials, and also speak separately in individual memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the early years, on major affairs ministers would speak jointly in collective memorials and also submit individual memorials of their own.

sentences.zh: 一不得行，則相聚環視，以不得其言為愧。

translations.literal: When a proposal was not adopted, they would gather in a circle and look at one another, taking it as shame that their words had not prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: When a proposal failed, they would gather and look at one another, ashamed that their counsel had not carried the day.

sentences.zh: 近者不然，會疏則刪削忌諱以避禍，獨疏則毛舉纖微以塞責。

translations.literal: Recently it is not so: in collective memorials they delete and cut what is taboo to avoid calamity; in individual memorials they pick out minute details to satisfy obligation.
translations.idiomatic: Lately it is otherwise: joint memorials are trimmed of anything taboo to avoid trouble, while individual ones nitpick trivialities merely to fulfill duty.

sentences.zh: 一不蒙譴，則交相慶賀，以茍免為幸。

translations.literal: When they are not punished, they congratulate one another, taking bare escape as good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: If they escape punishment, they congratulate one another, counting mere survival as good fortune.

sentences.zh: 消讜直之氣，長循默之風，甚非朝廷福也。」

translations.literal: It dissipates the spirit of forthright remonstrance and fosters the practice of silent compliance—hardly a blessing for the court."
translations.idiomatic: This drains the spirit of candid remonstrance and encourages habitual silence—a poor blessing indeed for the court."

sentences.zh: 章下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the appropriate department.

sentences.zh: 尋進右給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Right Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 王科、陳察劾郭勛，帝慰留之。

translations.literal: Wang Ke and Chen Cha impeached Guo Xun; the Emperor comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke and Chen Cha impeached Guo Xun, but the Emperor comforted Xun and retained him in office.

sentences.zh: 逵與同官鄭自璧、趙廷瑞言：「勛倚奸成橫，用酷濟貪，籠絡貨資，漁獵營伍，為妖賊李福達請屬，為逆黨陸完雪冤。

translations.literal: Kui together with his colleagues Zheng Zibi and Zhao Tingrui said: "Xun relies on the wicked to grow overbearing, uses cruelty to aid greed, networks for goods and money, preys upon the military camps, interceded on behalf of the demonic rebel Li Fuda, and cleared the guilt of the traitor Lu Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Kui and his colleagues Zheng Zibi and Zhao Tingrui said, "Xun has grown arrogant through villainous allies, using cruelty to fuel greed, networking for profit and preying on the military camps. He interceded for the sorcerer-rebel Li Fuda and cleared the traitor Lu Wan of guilt.

sentences.zh: 溫旨諭留，是旌使縱也。」

translations.literal: A warm edict instructing that he be retained—this is to commend and thereby release the unrestrained."
translations.idiomatic: A conciliatory edict keeping him in post amounts to commending wrongdoing and giving free rein to misconduct."

sentences.zh: 既復言：「福達誑惑愚民，稱兵犯順。

translations.literal: Later he again said: "Fuda deceived the foolish common people and raised troops in rebellion against the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to say, "Fuda deluded common people and took up arms in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 勛黨叛逆，罪不容誅。」
