translations.literal: Xun's faction aided rebellion; his crime does not allow less than execution."
translations.idiomatic: Xun's faction abetted rebellion—a crime that deserves nothing less than death."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 尋以言事忤旨，黜為吳江縣丞。

translations.literal: Soon, for speaking on affairs contrary to the imperial will, he was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, having offended the throne by remonstrating, he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 復坐福達獄逮問，謫戍遼東邊衛。

translations.literal: He was again implicated in the Li Fuda case, arrested and interrogated, and demoted to serve in a Liaodong border garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was again caught up in the Li Fuda case, arrested for questioning, and banished to a Liaodong frontier garrison.

sentences.zh: 居十年，母死不得歸，哀痛而卒。

translations.literal: After ten years there, when his mother died he could not return; he died in grief.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years in exile, when his mother died he was unable to return home, and he died in grief.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Longqing reign he was posthumously appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 鄭一鵬，字九萬，莆田人。正德十六年進士。改庶吉士。嘉靖初，官至戶科左給事中。一鵬性伉直，居諫垣中最敢言。御史曹嘉論大學士楊廷和，因言內閣柄太重。一鵬駁之曰：「太宗始立內閣，簡解縉等商政事，至漏下數十刻始退。自陛下即位，大臣宣召有幾？張銳、魏彬之獄，獻帝追崇之議，未嘗召廷和等面論。所擬旨，內多更定，未可謂專也。」

translations.literal: Zheng Yipeng, courtesy name Jiuwan, was from Putian. He became a jinshi in the sixteenth year of Zhengde and was transferred to be a shujishi. At the beginning of Jiajing, his office reached Left Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue. Yipeng was by nature upright and unyielding, and among the remonstrance officials he was the boldest in speaking. Censor Cao Jia criticized Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe and then said that the authority of the Inner Secretariat was too heavy. Yipeng refuted him, saying: "When Taizong first established the Inner Secretariat, he selected Xie Jin and others to discuss affairs of government, and they retired only after the water clock had passed several tens of marks. Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, how many times have great ministers been summoned? In the prisons of Zhang Rui and Wei Bin, and in the discussion of posthumously honoring Emperor Xian, Tinghe and the others were never summoned to discuss matters face to face. The drafted edicts were often changed from within; this cannot be called monopolizing power."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yipeng, courtesy name Jiuwan, was a native of Putian. A jinshi of Zhengde 16, he was made a shujishi. Early in Jiajing he rose to Left Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue. By nature Yipeng was upright and unyielding, and among the remonstrance officials he was the boldest speaker. When Censor Cao Jia criticized Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe and said the Inner Secretariat held too much power, Yipeng rebutted him: "When Taizong first established the Inner Secretariat, he chose Xie Jin and others to discuss government affairs, and they did not retire until the water clock had passed several tens of marks. Since Your Majesty came to the throne, how often have great ministers been summoned? In the cases of Zhang Rui and Wei Bin, and in the debate over posthumously honoring Emperor Xian, Tinghe and the others were never summoned for face-to-face discussion. Draft edicts were often altered from within the palace; this cannot be called monopolizing power."

sentences.zh: 帝用中官崔文言，建醮乾清、坤寧諸宮，西天、西番、漢經諸廠，五花宮兩暖閣、東次閣，莫不有之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, following the palace eunuch Cui Wenyan, established ritual prayer halls in the Qianqing and Kunning palaces, the Western Heaven, Tibetan, and Han sutra offices, the two warm chambers of Wuhua Palace, and the East Side Chamber—there was scarcely a place without them.
translations.idiomatic: At the urging of palace eunuch Cui Wenyan, the Emperor established prayer rituals throughout the Qianqing and Kunning palaces, the Western Heaven, Tibetan, and Han sutra offices, the two warm chambers of Wuhua Palace, and the East Side Chamber—hardly a corner of the palace was left without them.

sentences.zh: 一鵬言：「禱祀繁興，必魏彬、張銳余黨。

translations.literal: Yipeng said: "The proliferation of prayer rituals must be the work of the remaining faction of Wei Bin and Zhang Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Yipeng said, "This surge in prayer rituals must be the doing of holdovers from Wei Bin and Zhang Rui's faction.

sentences.zh: 先帝已誤，陛下豈容再誤？

translations.literal: The late Emperor already erred—how can Your Majesty allow error again?
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor already went astray—surely Your Majesty cannot repeat the mistake?

sentences.zh: 臣巡視光祿，見一齋醮蔬食之費，為錢萬有八千。

translations.literal: In my inspection of the Imperial Household, I saw that the cost of vegetarian fare for a single ritual fast was eighteen thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: In touring the Imperial Household, I found that the cost of vegetarian provisions for a single ritual observance came to eighteen thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 陛下忍斂民怨，而不忍傷佞幸之心。

translations.literal: Your Majesty can bear to gather the people's resentment, yet cannot bear to wound the hearts of favored sycophants.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is willing to incur the people's resentment yet unwilling to offend your favored sycophants.

sentences.zh: 況今天災頻降，京師道堇相望；

translations.literal: Moreover, heavenly disasters descend one after another, and on the roads of the capital corpses lie one after another;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, disasters from Heaven fall in succession, and on the roads of the capital the dead lie one after another;

sentences.zh: 邊境戍卒，日夜荷戈，不得飽食，而為僧道靡費至此，此臣所未解。」

translations.literal: On the frontiers the garrison soldiers day and night bear their weapons yet cannot eat their fill, while such extravagance is lavished on monks and Daoist priests—this your minister cannot understand."
translations.idiomatic: Frontier garrison troops bear arms night and day yet cannot eat their fill, while such vast sums are squandered on monks and Daoists—this I cannot fathom."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The memorial was noted.
translations.idiomatic: The court acknowledged receipt of the memorial.

sentences.zh: 東廠理刑千戶陶淳曲殺人，論謫戍。

translations.literal: Tao Chun, a thousand-household of the Eastern Depot's judicial section, killed a man wrongfully and was sentenced to demotion to a border garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Chun, a judicial thousand-household of the Eastern Depot, had a man killed unjustly and was sentenced to banishment to a frontier garrison.

sentences.zh: 詔覆案，改擬帶俸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a review of the case, and the revised sentence allowed him to retain his stipend.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered a retrial, and the sentence was reduced so that he retained his stipend.

sentences.zh: 一鵬與御史李東等執奏，並劾刑部侍郎孟鳳，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Yipeng together with the censor Li Dong and others firmly submitted a memorial, also impeaching the Vice Minister of Punishments Meng Feng; the Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yipeng and censor Li Dong and others pressed their memorial, also impeaching Vice Minister of Punishments Meng Feng, but the Emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 給事中鄧繼曾、修撰呂柟、編修鄒守益以言獲罪，一鵬皆疏救。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Deng Jizeng, the compiler Lu Nan, and the editor Zou Shouyi were punished for their words; Yipeng submitted memorials to rescue them all.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Deng Jizeng, compiler Lu Nan, and editor Zou Shouyi were punished for remonstrating; Yipeng submitted memorials on behalf of each.

sentences.zh: 宮中用度日侈，數倍天順時。

translations.literal: Daily expenses in the palace are extravagant, several times what they were in the Tianshun era.
translations.idiomatic: Daily palace expenditures have grown lavish—several times what they were under Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 一鵬言：「今歲災用詘，往往借支太倉，而清寧、仁壽、未央諸宮，每有贏積，率饋遺戚裏。

translations.literal: Yipeng said: "This year disaster funds fall short, and loans are often drawn from the Great Granary, yet the Qingning, Renshou, Weiyang, and other palaces frequently have surpluses, which are mostly bestowed on imperial relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Yipeng said, "This year disaster relief funds run short and the Great Granary is often tapped for advances, yet the Qingning, Renshou, Weiyang, and other palaces regularly run surpluses that are mostly handed out to imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 曷若留供光祿，彰母後德？」

translations.literal: Would it not be better to retain them to supply the Imperial Household and display the Empress Dowager's virtue?"
translations.idiomatic: Would it not be better to keep those surpluses for the Imperial Household and honor the Empress Dowager's virtue?"

sentences.zh: 帝命乾清、坤寧二宮暫減十之一。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered a temporary reduction of one tenth in the two palaces, Qianqing and Kunning.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered expenditures at the Qianqing and Kunning palaces temporarily cut by one tenth.

sentences.zh: 魯迷貢獅子、西牛、西狗、西馬及珠玉諸物。

translations.literal: Lu Mi presented tribute of lions, western oxen, western dogs, western horses, and various pearls and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Mi presented tribute lions, western oxen, western dogs, western horses, and various pearls and jade.

sentences.zh: 一鵬引漢閉玉門關謝西域故事，請敕邊臣量行賞賚，遣還國，勿使入京，彰朝廷不寶遠物之盛德。

translations.literal: Yipeng cited the Han precedent of closing the Jade Gate Pass to refuse the Western Regions, requesting that border officials be instructed to grant rewards as appropriate, send the tribute envoys back to their country, and not allow them to enter the capital, thereby displaying the court's great virtue of not treasuring distant things.
translations.idiomatic: Yipeng cited the Han precedent of closing the Jade Gate and declining Western tribute, urging that border officials be ordered to give fitting rewards, send the envoys home, and keep them from entering the capital—thus showcasing the court's virtue in not coveting exotic goods.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 尋伏闕爭「大禮」，杖於廷。

translations.literal: Soon he prostrated himself at the palace gate to dispute the "Grand Rites," and was beaten at court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined the palace-gate protest over the "Grand Rites" and was beaten in court.

sentences.zh: 侍郎胡瓚、都督魯綱督師討大同叛卒，列上功狀，請遍頒文武大臣、臺諫、部曹及各邊撫、按、鎮、監賞。

translations.literal: The Vice Minister Hu Zan and Regional Commander Lu Gang supervised troops to suppress the Datong rebel soldiers, submitted a register of merit, and requested that rewards be distributed broadly to civil and military grand ministers, censorate and remonstrating officials, ministry clerks, and the governors, inspectors, commanders, and supervisors of each border region.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Hu Zan and Regional Commander Lu Gang led troops against the Datong mutineers, submitted a merit roster, and asked that rewards be distributed widely among grand ministers, censorate officials, ministry clerks, and frontier governors, inspectors, commanders, and supervisors.

sentences.zh: 一鵬言：「桂勇誅郭監等，在瓚未至之先。

translations.literal: Yipeng said: "Gui Yong executed Guo Jian and the others before Zan had even arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Yipeng said, "Gui Yong had already executed Guo Jian and the others before Zan ever arrived.

sentences.zh: 徐氈兒等之誅，事由朱振，於瓚無與。

translations.literal: The execution of Xu Zhan'er and the others was handled by Zhu Zhen; it had nothing to do with Zan.
translations.idiomatic: The killing of Xu Zhan'er and his fellows was Zhu Zhen's doing and had nothing to do with Zan.

sentences.zh: 瓚欲邀功冒賞，懼眾口非議，乃請並敘以媚之。

translations.literal: Zan wished to claim merit and seize rewards; fearing criticism from many mouths, he therefore requested that all be included in the merit roster to curry favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zan hoped to claim credit and reap rewards; fearing outcry, he asked that everyone be included in the merit list to buy favor.

sentences.zh: 夫自大同構難，大臣臺諫誰為陛下畫一策者？

translations.literal: Since trouble arose at Datong, among the grand ministers and censorate remonstrators, who has drawn a single strategy for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Since the Datong crisis began, which grand minister or censorate official has offered Your Majesty a single workable plan?

sentences.zh: 孤城窮寇尚多逋逃，各邊鎮、撫相去數千里，安在其能犄角也？」

translations.literal: In an isolated city the desperate bandits still have many who have fled; the border commanders and governors are separated by several thousand li—wherein can they coordinate in pincer support?"
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers still have many fugitives at large, and frontier commanders and governors are thousands of li apart—how could they have acted in concert?"

sentences.zh: 請治瓚等欺罔罪，賞乃不行。

translations.literal: He requested that Zan and the others be punished for deception, and the rewards were then not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He called for Zan and his fellows to be punished for fraud, and the rewards were withheld.

sentences.zh: 時諸臣進言多獲譴，而一鵬間得俞旨，益發舒言事。

translations.literal: At the time many officials who remonstrated were punished, yet Yipeng occasionally received the Emperor's assent and increasingly spoke out on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At a time when remonstrance usually brought punishment, Yipeng occasionally won the Emperor's assent and grew bolder in speaking out.

sentences.zh: 論楊宏不宜推寧夏總兵官；

translations.literal: He argued that Yang Hong should not be recommended for the post of Ningxia regional commander;
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Yang Hong was unsuited to be promoted to Ningxia regional commander;

sentences.zh: 席書不宜訐費宏，留其弟春為修撰；

translations.literal: that Xi Shu should not accuse Fei Hong, and that his brother Chun should not be kept on as compiler;
translations.idiomatic: that Xi Shu should not be allowed to attack Fei Hong while keeping his own brother Chun on as a compiler;

sentences.zh: 王憲夤緣貴近，鄧璋敗事甘肅，不宜舉三邊總督；

translations.literal: that Wang Xian had curried favor with the powerful and that Deng Zhang had failed in Gansu, and neither should be recommended for Three Border supreme commander;
translations.idiomatic: that Wang Xian had risen through court connections and that Deng Zhang had failed in Gansu—neither deserved recommendation as Three Border supreme commander;

sentences.zh: 服闋尚書羅欽順、請告祭酒魯鐸、被謫修撰呂柟宜召置經筵；

translations.literal: that the minister Luo Qinshun, who had completed mourning, the chancellor Lu Duo, who had requested leave, and the demoted compiler Lu Nan should be summoned to serve at the imperial lecture;
translations.idiomatic: that Minister Luo Qinshun, who had finished mourning, Chancellor Lu Duo, who had requested leave, and demoted compiler Lu Nan ought to be recalled to the imperial lecture;

sentences.zh: 廷臣乞省親養疾，不宜概不許。

translations.literal: and that court ministers who petitioned to visit family or recuperate from illness should not be denied across the board.
translations.idiomatic: and that petitions from ministers to visit family or recuperate should not be rejected wholesale.

sentences.zh: 諸疏皆侃侃。

translations.literal: All these memorials were forthright and assured.
translations.idiomatic: Every one of these memorials was bold and forthright.

sentences.zh: 會武定侯郭勛欲得虎賁左衛以廣其第，使指揮王琬等言，衛湫隘不足居吏士，而民郭順者願以宅易之。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Wuding Guo Xun wished to obtain the Huben Left Guard to expand his residence, he had the commander Wang Wan and others say that the guard barracks were cramped and insufficient to house officers and men, and that a commoner named Guo Shun was willing to exchange his house for them.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Wuding Guo Xun sought to take over the Huben Left Guard to enlarge his mansion, he had commander Wang Wan and others claim the guard quarters were too cramped for officers and men and that a commoner named Guo Shun was willing to swap his house for the site.

sentences.zh: 順，勛家奴也，其宅更湫隘。

translations.literal: Shun was a household slave of Xun's, and his house was even more cramped.
translations.idiomatic: Shun was a bond-servant in Xun's household, and his dwelling was even more cramped.

sentences.zh: 一鵬與同官張嵩劾勛：「以敝宅易公署，驕縱罔上。

translations.literal: Yipeng together with his colleague Zhang Song impeached Xun: "To exchange a dilapidated house for a public office—arrogant, unrestrained, and deceiving the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yipeng and his colleague Zhang Song impeached Xun: "Trading a ramshackle house for a government compound shows arrogance, license, and contempt for the throne.

sentences.zh: 昔竇憲改沁水園，卒以逆誅。

translations.literal: In the past Dou Xian altered the Qinshui Garden and was ultimately executed for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Dou Xian seized the Qinshui Garden and was eventually executed for treason.

sentences.zh: 勛謀奪朝廷武衛，其惡豈止憲比？

translations.literal: Xun plotted to seize a military guard of the court—is his wickedness not far greater than Dou Xian's?
translations.idiomatic: Xun schemed to seize an imperial military guard—his offense surely exceeds Dou Xian's.

sentences.zh: 部臣附勢曲從，宜坐罪。」

translations.literal: The ministry officials who attached themselves to his power and bent to comply should be punished."
translations.idiomatic: The ministry officials who bent to his power ought to be punished as well."

sentences.zh: 尚書趙璜等因自劾。

translations.literal: Minister Zhao Huang and the others therefore submitted self-impeachments.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhao Huang and his colleagues thereupon impeached themselves.

sentences.zh: 詔還所易，勛甚銜之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the exchange reversed; Xun bore a deep grudge.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the property returned, and Xun nursed a deep grievance.

sentences.zh: 而一鵬復以李福達獄劾勛，桂萼、張璁因坐以妄奏，拷掠除名。

translations.literal: Then Yipeng again impeached Xun over the Li Fuda case; Gui E and Zhang Cong had him charged with making false memorials, tortured him, and stripped him of his name and post.
translations.idiomatic: When Yipeng again impeached Xun in the Li Fuda case, Gui E and Zhang Cong had him convicted of false reporting, tortured, and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 九廟災，言官會薦遺賢及一鵬，竟不復召。

translations.literal: When the Nine Temples burned, censorate officials jointly recommended overlooked worthies and Yipeng, but he was ultimately not recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After the fire at the Nine Temples, censorate officials jointly recommended overlooked talent and Yipeng, but he was never recalled.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long while, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In time he died.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初復官，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing his office was restored, and he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Longqing reign his rank was restored and he was posthumously appointed Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 唐樞，字惟中，歸安人。

translations.literal: Tang Shu, style name Weizhong, was a man of Gui'an.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shu, whose style was Weizhong, was a native of Gui'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Jiajing 5.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a section chief in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed section chief in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 言官以李福達獄交劾郭勛，然不得獄辭要領。

translations.literal: Censorate officials repeatedly impeached Guo Xun over the Li Fuda case, yet could not grasp the essential points of the case records.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate officials kept impeaching Guo Xun over the Li Fuda case, yet never got to the heart of the case records.

sentences.zh: 樞上疏言：

translations.literal: Shu submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shu submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 李福達之獄，陛下駁勘再三，誠古帝王欽恤盛心。

translations.literal: In the Li Fuda case, Your Majesty has ordered repeated review and re-examination—truly the abundant reverent compassion of the ancient sage emperors.
translations.idiomatic: In the Li Fuda case, Your Majesty has ordered the investigation reopened again and again—a mark of the reverent compassion of the sage emperors of old.

sentences.zh: 而諸臣負陛下，欺蔽者肆其讒，謅諛者混其說，畏威者變其辭，訪緝者淆其真。

translations.literal: Yet the officials have failed Your Majesty: the deceivers have freely spread their slander, the flatterers have muddled their accounts, those who fear authority have changed their testimony, and the investigators have confused the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your officials have failed you—deceivers spread slander freely, flatterers muddle the story, the fearful change their testimony, and investigators confuse the facts.

sentences.zh: 是以陛下惑滋甚，而是非卒不能明。

translations.literal: Thus Your Majesty's confusion has grown ever greater, and right and wrong ultimately cannot be clarified.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Your Majesty grows more confused, and the rights and wrongs of the matter still cannot be settled.

sentences.zh: 臣竊惟陛下之疑有六。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that Your Majesty's doubts are six in number.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to think Your Majesty harbors six doubts.

sentences.zh: 謂謀反罪重，不宜輕加於所疑，一也。

translations.literal: First, that the crime of rebellion is grave and should not lightly be applied to one who is merely suspected.
translations.idiomatic: First, that rebellion is a grave charge and should not lightly be laid on a mere suspect.

sentences.zh: 謂天下人貌有相似，二也。

translations.literal: Second, that people throughout the realm may have similar appearances.
translations.idiomatic: Second, that people in the world can look alike.

sentences.zh: 謂薛良言弗可聽，三也。

translations.literal: Third, that the words of Xue Liang cannot be believed.
translations.idiomatic: Third, that Xue Liang's testimony should not be credited.

sentences.zh: 謂李玨初牒明，四也。

translations.literal: Fourth, that Li Jue's initial report was clear.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, that Li Jue's original dispatch was clear.

sentences.zh: 謂臣下立黨傾郭勛，五也。

translations.literal: Fifth, that officials below have formed a faction to overthrow Guo Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, that your ministers have formed a faction to bring down Guo Xun.

sentences.zh: 謂崞、洛證佐皆仇人，六也。

translations.literal: Sixth, that the witnesses from Guo and Luo are all personal enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, that the witnesses from Guo and Luo are all sworn enemies.

sentences.zh: 臣請一一辨之。

translations.literal: Your servant requests to rebut each in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Allow me to address each in turn.

sentences.zh: 福達之出也，始而王良、李鉞從之，其意何為？

translations.literal: When Fuda came forward, Wang Liang and Li Yue first followed him—what was their intent?
translations.idiomatic: When Fuda first appeared, Wang Liang and Li Yue followed him—what did they intend?

sentences.zh: 繼而惠慶、邵進祿等師之，其傳何事？

translations.literal: Then Huiqing, Shao Jinlu, and the others took him as teacher—what did they transmit?
translations.idiomatic: Then Huiqing, Shao Jinlu, and others made him their teacher—what were they taught?

sentences.zh: 李鐵漢十月下旬之約，其行何求？

translations.literal: The agreement Li Tiehan made in the last ten days of the tenth month—what did their actions seek?
translations.idiomatic: The compact Li Tiehan arranged in late tenth month—what were they seeking to accomplish?

sentences.zh: 「我有天分」數語，其情何謀？

translations.literal: The several words 'I have Heaven's allotment'—what scheme lay in that sentiment?
translations.idiomatic: The words 'I have Heaven's mandate'—what plot lay behind them?

sentences.zh: 「太上玄天，垂文秘書」，其辭何指？

translations.literal: The words 'Supreme Mysterious Heaven bestows secret texts and writings'—what do they refer to?
translations.idiomatic: What did he mean by the phrase 'Supreme Mysterious Heaven bestows secret scriptures'?

sentences.zh: 劫庫攻城，張旗拜爵，雖成於進祿等，其原何自？

translations.literal: Raiding treasuries, storming cities, raising banners, and conferring titles—though accomplished by Jinlu and the others, whence did their origin come?
translations.idiomatic: The looting of storehouses, attacks on cities, raising of rebel banners, and bestowal of ranks were carried out by Jinlu and his followers—but where did all of that begin?

sentences.zh: 鉞伏誅於前，進祿敗露於後，反狀甚明。

translations.literal: The axe was laid in submission and execution carried out in front; Jinlu's defeat was exposed afterward—the appearance of rebellion is very clear.
translations.idiomatic: Jinlu was executed with the ceremonial axe, and afterward his plot was fully exposed—the evidence of rebellion could hardly be clearer.

sentences.zh: 故陜西之人曰可殺，山西之人曰可殺，京畿中無一人不曰可殺，惟左右之人曰不可，則臣不得而知也。

translations.literal: Therefore people of Shaanxi say he should be killed, people of Shanxi say he should be killed, in the capital region not one person fails to say he should be killed—only those at Your Majesty's side say no; then your servant cannot know.
translations.idiomatic: People in Shaanxi say he deserves death; people in Shanxi say the same; in the capital, everyone agrees—yet only those around Your Majesty say otherwise. How, then, can I understand your hesitation?

sentences.zh: 此不必疑一也。

translations.literal: This need not be the first doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Your first doubt, then, is groundless.

sentences.zh: 且福達之形最易辨識，或取驗於頭禿，或證辨於鄉音，如李二、李俊、李三是其族，識之矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, Fuda's form is easiest to identify—sometimes verified by a bald head, sometimes distinguished by dialect accent; Li Er, Li Jun, and Li San, who are of his clan, identified him.
translations.idiomatic: Fuda's appearance was easy to recognize—some knew him by his bald head, others by his accent. Li Er, Li Jun, and Li San, members of his clan, all identified him.

sentences.zh: 發於戚廣之妻之口，是其孫識之矣。

translations.literal: It issued from the mouth of Qi Guang's wife—his grandson identified him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Guang's wife spoke up, and her grandson recognized him.

sentences.zh: 始認於杜文柱，是其姻識之矣。

translations.literal: He was first recognized by Du Wenzhu—his relation by marriage identified him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Wenzhu was the first to recognize him—a kinsman by marriage.

sentences.zh: 質證於韓良相、李景全，是其友識之矣。

translations.literal: Corroborated with Han Liangxiang and Li Jingquan—his friends identified him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Liangxiang and Li Jingquan confirmed the identification—they were his friends.

sentences.zh: 一言於高尚節、王宗美，是鄜州主人識之矣。

translations.literal: One account was given to Gao Shangjie and Wang Zongmei—the hosts in Fuzhou identified him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shangjie and Wang Zongmei, who had hosted him in Fuzhou, also recognized him.

sentences.zh: 再言於邵繼美、宗自成，是洛川主人識之矣。

translations.literal: A second account was given to Shao Jimei and Zong Zicheng—the hosts in Luochuan identified him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Jimei and Zong Zicheng, his hosts in Luochuan, identified him as well.

sentences.zh: 三言於石文舉等，是山、陜道路之人皆識之矣。

translations.literal: A third account was given to Shi Wenju and others—people on the roads of Shan and Shaanxi all identified him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wenju and others testified too—travelers on the roads of Shanxi and Shaanxi knew him on sight.

sentences.zh: 此不必疑二也。

translations.literal: This need not be the second doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Your second doubt, likewise, should be set aside.

sentences.zh: 薛良怙惡，誠非善人。

translations.literal: Xue Liang clings to evil—truly he is not a good person.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Liang was a wicked man, to be sure—not someone of good character.

sentences.zh: 至所言張寅之即福達，即李午，實有明據，不得以人廢言。

translations.literal: As for his statement that Zhang Yin is Fuda, is Li Wu—there is truly clear evidence; one cannot reject the words on account of the man.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his claim that Zhang Yin was really Li Fuda, alias Li Wu, rested on solid evidence. A man's character must not discredit truthful testimony.

sentences.zh: 況福達蹤跡譎密，黠慧過人，人鹹墮其術中，非良狡猾亦不能發彼陰私。

translations.literal: Moreover, Fuda's tracks are secret and intricate; he is crafty and clever beyond ordinary men, and people all fell into his schemes—without Liang's cunning one could not expose his hidden private matters.
translations.idiomatic: Fuda moved in secrecy and was cleverer than most; many had been taken in by his tricks. Only someone as shrewd as Xue Liang could have brought his hidden crimes to light.

sentences.zh: 從來發摘告訐之事，原不必出之敦良樸厚之人。

translations.literal: From antiquity, matters of uncovering and informing need not come from honest, good, simple, and solid persons.
translations.idiomatic: Exposés and denunciations have never required a witness who was honest, plain, and upright.

sentences.zh: 此不當疑三也。

translations.literal: This should not be the third doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Your third doubt is equally unfounded.

sentences.zh: 李玨因見薛良非善人，又見李福達無龍虎形、朱砂字，又見五臺縣張子真戶內實有張寅父子，又見崞縣左廂都無李福達、李午名，遂茍且定案，輕縱元兇。

translations.literal: Li Jue, because he saw Xue Liang was not a good person, also saw Li Fuda had no dragon-tiger mark or cinnabar characters, also saw that within Zhang Zizhen's household in Wutai County there were truly Zhang Yin and his sons, and also saw that in Guo County's Left Garrison Brigade there were no names Li Fuda or Li Wu, thus perfunctorily settled the case and lightly released the chief culprit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue dismissed Xue Liang as untrustworthy, found no dragon-tiger birthmark or cinnabar inscription on the suspect, noted Zhang Yin and his sons listed under Zhang Zizhen's household in Wutai County, and found no record of Li Fuda or Li Wu in Guo County's Left Garrison Brigade. On that basis he closed the case in haste and let the real culprit go.

sentences.zh: 殊不知五臺自嘉靖元年黃冊始收，寅父子忽從何來？

translations.literal: He little knew that Wutai's yellow register only began taking new entries from the first year of Jiajing—from where did Yin and his sons suddenly come?
translations.idiomatic: He failed to ask the obvious question: Wutai's household register had only begun accepting new entries in Jiajing 1—so where had Zhang Yin and his sons come from overnight?

sentences.zh: 納粟拜官，其為素封必非一日之積，前此何以隱漏？

translations.literal: Paying grain to receive office—their being wealthy landowners must not be accumulation of a single day; why were they concealed and omitted before this?
translations.idiomatic: A family wealthy enough to buy office with grain payments does not become rich overnight. Why had they never appeared in the records before?

sentences.zh: 崞縣在城坊既有李伏答，乃於左廂都追察，又以李午為真名，求其貫址，何可得也？

translations.literal: In Guo County the urban wards already had Li Fuda on record, yet he pursued investigation in the Left Garrison Brigade and moreover took Li Wu as the true name—how could one obtain his registered domicile?
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuda was already registered in Guo County's urban wards, yet Li Jue searched the Left Garrison Brigade under the name Li Wu and then wondered why he could find no registered address.

sentences.zh: 則軍籍之無考，何足據也？

translations.literal: Then the military register's lack of verification—how is it sufficient to rely upon?
translations.idiomatic: How, then, could an inconclusive search of the military rolls be treated as proof?

sentences.zh: 況福達既有妖術，則龍虎形、朱砂字，安知非前此假之以惑眾，後此去之以避罪？

translations.literal: Moreover, since Fuda had demonic arts, as for the dragon-tiger mark and cinnabar characters—how does one know they were not previously faked to delude the masses and later removed to avoid guilt?
translations.idiomatic: And if Fuda truly possessed occult powers, who is to say he had not faked the dragon-tiger mark and cinnabar inscription to impress followers, then erased them to evade prosecution?

sentences.zh: 亦不可盡謂薛良之誣矣。

translations.literal: One also cannot entirely say Xue Liang's accusations were false.
translations.idiomatic: Nor can Xue Liang's testimony be dismissed outright as fabrication.

sentences.zh: 此不當疑四也。

translations.literal: This should not be the fourth doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Your fourth doubt, too, does not hold.

sentences.zh: 京師自四方來者不止一福達，既改名張寅，又衣冠形貌似之，郭勛從而信之，亦理之所有。

translations.literal: In the capital those who come from all four directions are not only one Fuda; having changed his name to Zhang Yin and with dress and appearance resembling him, Guo Xun accordingly believed it—also something reason allows.
translations.idiomatic: Many men come to the capital from every province—not every one of them is Li Fuda. Having taken the name Zhang Yin and dressed the part, it was understandable that Guo Xun believed him.

sentences.zh: 其為妖賊余黨，亦意料所不能及。

translations.literal: That he was a demonic bandit's remnant associate is also beyond what could be expected.
translations.idiomatic: That he was in fact a surviving accomplice of a heretic rebel was something no one could reasonably have foreseen.

sentences.zh: 在勛自有可居之過，在陛下既宏議貴之恩，諸臣縱有傾勛之心，亦安能加之罪乎？

translations.literal: In Xun's case there is certainly fault that can be assigned; given Your Majesty has already extended generous grace honoring discussion, even if ministers have hearts to overthrow Xun, how could they add guilt to him?
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xun may well bear some blame, but Your Majesty has already shown him great favor. Even if some ministers wished to bring him down, how could they convict him on that basis alone?

sentences.zh: 此不用疑五也。

translations.literal: This need not be the fifth doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Your fifth doubt is likewise unnecessary.

sentences.zh: 鞫獄者曰誣，必言所誣何因。

translations.literal: Those who interrogate cases say 'false accusation'—they must state what cause the false accusation has.
translations.idiomatic: When investigators claim a charge is fabricated, they must explain why it was fabricated.

sentences.zh: 曰讎，必言所讎何事。

translations.literal: Saying 'personal feud,' they must state what matter the feud concerns.
translations.idiomatic: When they invoke personal enmity, they must specify what the grudge was about.

sentences.zh: 若曰薛良，讎也，則一切證佐非讎也。

translations.literal: If one says Xue Liang is the enemy, then all the other witnesses are not enemies.
translations.idiomatic: If Xue Liang alone is dismissed as an enemy, then none of the other witnesses can be.

sentences.zh: 曰韓良相、戚廣，讎也，則高尚節、屈孔、石文舉，非讎也。

translations.literal: Saying Han Liangxiang and Qi Guang are enemies, then Gao Shangjie, Qu Kong, and Shi Wenju are not enemies.
translations.idiomatic: If Han Liangxiang and Qi Guang are enemies, then Gao Shangjie, Qu Kong, and Shi Wenju plainly are not.

sentences.zh: 曰魏泰、劉永振，讎也，則今布按府縣官非讎也。

translations.literal: Saying Wei Tai and Liu Yongzhen are enemies, then the present provincial, surveillance, prefectural, and county officials are not enemies.
translations.idiomatic: If Wei Tai and Liu Yongzhen are enemies, then the provincial, surveillance, prefectural, and county officials who testified cannot be.

sentences.zh: 曰山、陜人，讎也，則京師道路之人非讎也。

translations.literal: Saying Shan and Shaanxi people are enemies, then people on the roads in the capital are not enemies.
translations.idiomatic: If everyone from Shanxi and Shaanxi is an enemy, then the witnesses encountered on the roads of the capital cannot be.

sentences.zh: 此不用疑六也。

translations.literal: This need not be the sixth doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Your sixth and final doubt should be dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 望陛下六疑盡釋，明正福達之罪。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will fully release all six doubts and clearly establish Fuda's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to lay all six doubts to rest and pronounce Li Fuda's guilt clearly.

sentences.zh: 庶群奸屏跡，宗社幸甚。

translations.literal: Perhaps all wicked persons will withdraw their traces—the altars of state will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Then the wicked will have nowhere to hide, and the dynasty will be the better for it.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝大怒，斥為民。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; the Emperor was greatly enraged and dismissed him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the Emperor flew into a rage and stripped Shu of his office, reducing him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 其後《欽明大獄錄》刪樞疏不載。

translations.literal: Afterward, the 'Records of Grand Cases in the August Ming' deleted Shu's memorial and did not record it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the "Records of Grand Cases in the August Ming" was compiled, Shu's memorial was cut and omitted.

sentences.zh: 樞少學於湛若水，深造實踐。

translations.literal: Shu in his youth studied under Zhan Ruoshui and deeply cultivated practical learning.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Shu studied under Zhan Ruoshui and pursued a rigorous course of practical self-cultivation.

sentences.zh: 又留心經世略，九邊及越、蜀、滇、黔險阻厄塞，無不親歷。

translations.literal: He also focused on statecraft strategy; the Nine Frontiers and the dangerous passes and narrow barriers of Yue, Shu, Dian, and Qian—nothing did he not personally experience.
translations.idiomatic: He also devoted himself to statecraft, personally traveling the Nine Frontiers and the treacherous passes of Guangdong, Sichuan, Yunnan, and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 躡屩茹草，至老不衰。

translations.literal: Wearing straw sandals and eating coarse herbs, until old age he did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: He tramped rough roads in straw sandals and lived on simple fare, and kept at it until old age.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Longqing reign his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 以年老，加秩致仕。

translations.literal: Due to old age, he was given added rank and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his advanced age, he was promoted in rank and allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 會高拱憾徐階，謂階恤錄先朝建言諸臣，乃彰先帝之過，請悉停之，樞竟不錄。

translations.literal: It happened that Gao Gong resented Xu Jie, saying Xu's compassionate posthumous honors for former-court memorializing ministers was revealing the former emperor's fault, and requesting that all be stopped—Shu in the end was not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong, who resented Xu Jie, argued that restoring the honors of ministers punished under the previous reign for their memorials would expose the late emperor's errors, and he persuaded the court to halt the program. Shu was never included.

sentences.zh: 杜鸞，字羽文，陜西鹹寧人。

translations.literal: Du Luan, style name Yuwen, was a man of Xianning in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Du Luan, whose style was Yuwen, was a native of Xianning in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 正德末進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate at the end of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the final years of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 授大理評事。

translations.literal: He was appointed reviewing officer in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed reviewing officer at the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，伏闕爭《大禮》，杖午門外。

translations.literal: In early Jiajing, he prostrated at the palace gate disputing the 'Great Rites' and was beaten outside the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he joined the protest at the palace gate over the Great Rites and was beaten outside the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 長沙盜李鑒與父華劫村聚，華誅，鑒得脫。

translations.literal: The Changsha bandit Li Jian and his father Hua raided village settlements; Hua was executed, and Jian escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jian, a bandit from Changsha, and his father Hua had robbed villages. Hua was executed, but Jian got away.

sentences.zh: 後復行劫，捕獲之。

translations.literal: Later he again committed robbery and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to banditry and was eventually captured.

sentences.zh: 席書時撫湖廣，劾知府宋卿故入鑒。

translations.literal: Xi Shu at the time governed Huguang and impeached Prefect Song Qing for intentionally wrongly convicting Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shu, then grand coordinator of Huguang, impeached Prefect Song Qing for deliberately framing Li Jian.

sentences.zh: 帝遣大臣按之，言鑒盜有狀，帝命逮鑒至京。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched a grand minister to investigate; he reported that Jian's banditry had evidence, and the Emperor ordered Jian arrested and brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent a senior official to review the case, who confirmed the evidence of Li Jian's crimes. The Emperor then ordered him brought to the capital for trial.

sentences.zh: 書上言：「臣以議禮忤朝臣，問官故與臣左。

translations.literal: Shu submitted a memorial saying: 'Your servant, because of disputing the rites, offended court ministers; the examining officials intentionally opposed your servant.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shu memorialized the throne: 'Because I took the opposing side in the Rites dispute, the court officials who examined this case were bound to rule against me.

sentences.zh: 乞敕法司會官覆。」

translations.literal: I beg that the judiciary be ordered to convene officials for a review."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the judicial authorities be ordered to rehear the case with a joint panel of officials."

sentences.zh: 於是鸞會御史蘇恩再訊，無異詞，疏言：「書以惡卿故為鑒奏辨，且以議禮為言。

translations.literal: Thereupon Luan, together with Censor Su En, examined the case again; there was no differing testimony. He submitted a memorial saying: 'Shu, because of hatred of Qing, pleaded for Jian, moreover using the rites dispute as his argument.
translations.idiomatic: Du Luan then joined Censor Su En in a second inquiry. The testimony was unchanged, and he reported: 'Xi Shu pleaded for Li Jian out of spite toward Song Qing, and invoked the Rites dispute to do it.

sentences.zh: 夫大禮之議，發於聖孝。

translations.literal: The Grand Rites dispute arose from sage filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Rites controversy arose from Your Majesty's filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 書偶一言當意，動援此以挾陛下，壓群僚。

translations.literal: Shu, by chance having one word hit the mark, always invokes this to coerce Your Majesty and suppress the myriad officials.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shu happened to strike the right note once, and ever since he has wielded the Rites issue to pressure Your Majesty and intimidate the rest of the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 壞亂政體，莫此為甚。」

translations.literal: Ruining and disordering the governmental system—nothing is worse than this."
translations.idiomatic: Nothing has done more to corrupt the conduct of government."

sentences.zh: 帝重違書意，竟免鑒死，戍遼東。

translations.literal: The Emperor heavily went against Shu's intent and in the end exempted Jian from death, exiling him to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, unwilling to cross Xi Shu, spared Li Jian's life and banished him to Liaodong instead.

sentences.zh: 已，復有張寅之獄。

translations.literal: Soon after, there was again the Zhang Yin case.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward came the Zhang Yin case.

sentences.zh: 鸞與刑部郎中司馬相、御史高世魁司其牘。

translations.literal: Luan, together with Bureau Director Sima Xiang of the Ministry of Punishments and Censor Gao Shikui, managed its documents.
translations.idiomatic: Du Luan, together with Sima Xiang of the Ministry of Punishments and Censor Gao Shikui, handled the case files.

sentences.zh: 鸞上言：「往者李鑒之獄，陛下徇席書言，誤恩廢法，權幸遂以鬻獄為常，請托無忌。

translations.literal: Luan submitted a memorial saying: 'Previously, in the Li Jian case, Your Majesty followed Xi Shu's words, mistakenly favoring and abolishing law; powerful favorites thus made selling justice normal, and requests and entreaties were without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Du Luan memorialized: 'In the Li Jian case, Your Majesty heeded Xi Shu and set aside the law in a misguided show of favor. Since then the powerful have treated the sale of justice as routine, and patronage has gone unchecked.

sentences.zh: 今勛謀又成矣。

translations.literal: Now Xun's scheming has again succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Now Guo Xun's scheme has succeeded once more.

sentences.zh: 書曰『以議禮招怨』，勛亦曰『以議禮招怨』。

translations.literal: Shu said, 'Invoked the rites dispute to incur resentment'; Xun also said, 'Invoked the rites dispute to incur resentment.'
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shu said he was being targeted 'because of the Rites dispute'; Guo Xun says the same.

sentences.zh: 書曰『欲殺鑒以仇臣』，勛亦曰：『欲殺寅以仇臣』。

translations.literal: Shu said, 'Wished to kill Jian to enemy your servant'; Xun also said, 'Wished to kill Yin to enemy your servant.'
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shu claimed his enemies 'wanted Li Jian dead to get at me'; Guo Xun now claims they 'want Zhang Yin dead to get at me.'

sentences.zh: 簧鼓聖聰，如出一口。

translations.literal: Playing reeds and drums upon the sage hearing, as from one mouth.
translations.idiomatic: They whisper the same sophistry into the imperial ear, as if speaking from a single script.

sentences.zh: 以陛下尊親之盛典，為奸邪掩覆之深謀，將使賄賂公行，亂賊接踵，非聖朝福也。」

translations.literal: Using Your Majesty's ceremony of honoring kin as wicked persons' deep plot of covering over, bribery will be practiced openly and rebellious bandits will follow one after another—this is not the blessed dynasty's fortune."
translations.idiomatic: They are turning Your Majesty's solemn rites of honoring his father into a cover for wicked men. Bribery will flourish openly, rebels will follow in succession, and the dynasty will suffer for it."

sentences.zh: 已而桂萼等力反前獄，鸞坐除名。

translations.literal: Soon Gui E and others forcefully reversed the former case, and Luan was sentenced to dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E and his allies then overturned the earlier verdict, and Du Luan was stripped of his rank and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 初，書之欲寬李鑒也，給事中管律言：「比言事者，每借議禮為詞。

translations.literal: Initially, when Shu wished to leniently treat Li Jian, Supervising Secretary Guan Lu said: 'Lately memorialists each borrow the rites dispute as their language.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi Shu first moved to leniency for Li Jian, Supervising Secretary Guan Lu observed: 'Memorialists of late constantly invoke the Rites dispute in their petitions.

sentences.zh: 或乞休，或引罪，或為人辨訴，於議禮本不相涉，而動必援引牽附，何哉？

translations.literal: Some beg retirement, some cite guilt, some plead for others—these have nothing to do with the rites dispute in origin, yet always they invoke and attach to it. Why?
translations.idiomatic: Whether asking to retire, confessing fault, or pleading someone else's case, the matter has nothing to do with the Rites—yet they drag it in every time. Why?

sentences.zh: 蓋小人欲中傷人，以非此不足激陛下怒；

translations.literal: Probably petty persons wish to harm people—unless it is not this, it is insufficient to inflame Your Majesty's anger;
translations.idiomatic: Petty men do it to wound their enemies—nothing else reliably provokes Your Majesty's wrath;

sentences.zh: 而欲自固其寵，又非此不足得陛下歡也。

translations.literal: and wishing to secure their own favor, unless it is not this, it is insufficient to obtain Your Majesty's pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: and to keep their own favor, nothing else so reliably wins Your Majesty's approval.

sentences.zh: 乞誡自今言事者，據事直陳，毋假借，以累聖德。」

translations.literal: I beg that from now on memorialists be admonished to state matters directly according to the facts, not to borrow falsely, so as not to burden sage virtue."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter memorialists be instructed to speak plainly to the facts and stop borrowing the Rites issue, lest they tarnish Your Majesty's reputation."

sentences.zh: 帝是其言，命都察院曉示百官。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words and ordered the Censorate to inform all officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed and ordered the Censorate to circulate the admonition to the entire bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 越二日，御史李儼以世廟成，請恤錄議禮獲罪諸臣，且請詳察是非：「議禮是而行事非者，不以是掩非。

translations.literal: Two days later, Censor Li Yan, on the completion of the Spirit Temple, requested compassionate posthumous honors for ministers punished in the rites dispute, and moreover requested thorough examination of right and wrong: 'Where the rites dispute was correct but conduct was wrong, do not use the correct to cover the wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later, with the Spirit Temple completed, Censor Li Yan asked that the ministers punished over the Rites be posthumously restored, and urged a careful sorting of right from wrong: 'Where a man was right about the Rites but wrong in his conduct, his Rites stance must not excuse his misconduct.

sentences.zh: 議禮非而行事是者，不以非掩是。

translations.literal: Where the rites dispute was wrong but conduct was correct, do not use the wrong to cover the correct.
translations.idiomatic: Where a man was wrong about the Rites but right in his conduct, his error on the Rites must not obscure his merits.

sentences.zh: 使黨與全消，時靡有爭，則大公之治也。」

translations.literal: Making factions entirely dissolve and the age without contention—then this is governance of great fairness."
translations.idiomatic: Only when factions are fully dissolved and disputes cease will the court achieve truly impartial governance."

sentences.zh: 未幾，給事中陳臯謨亦言：「獻皇帝追崇之禮，實出陛下至情。

translations.literal: Before long, Supervising Secretary Chen Gaomo also said: 'The posthumous honors rites for Emperor Xian truly stem from Your Majesty's utmost feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Supervising Secretary Chen Gaomo added: 'The rites honoring the late Emperor Xian sprang from Your Majesty's deepest filial feeling.

sentences.zh: 書輩乃貪為己功，互相黨援，恣情喜怒，作福作威。

translations.literal: Shu and his company greedily made it their own merit, mutually forming factional support, indulging emotions of joy and anger, making fortune and making authority.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shu and his allies seized the credit for themselves, formed factions, and ruled by caprice— dispensing favors and punishments at will.

sentences.zh: 若李鑒父子，成案昭然。

translations.literal: Like Li Jian and his father—the concluded case is brilliantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Take Li Jian and his father: their guilt was plain.

sentences.zh: 書曲為申救，謂『眾以議禮憾臣，因陷鑒死』。

translations.literal: Shu twisted pleading to rescue them, saying, 'The masses, because of resentment over the rites dispute toward your servant, thus trapped Jian to death.'
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shu bent the law to save them, claiming that 'my enemies in the Rites dispute are trying to kill Li Jian to get at me.'

sentences.zh: 夫議禮者，朝廷之公典，合與不合，何至深讎？

translations.literal: The rites dispute is the court's public statute—agree or disagree, how does it become deep enmity?
translations.idiomatic: The Rites dispute was a matter of public policy. Agreement or disagreement on it hardly makes men mortal enemies.

sentences.zh: 縱使讎書，鑒非書子弟親戚交遊也，何故讎之？

translations.literal: Even supposing enmity toward Shu, Jian is not Shu's sons, younger brothers, relatives, or friends—why be his enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Xi Shu had enemies, Li Jian was no relation, friend, or associate of his. Why would anyone take revenge on Jian?

sentences.zh: 至郭勛黨庇奸人，請屬事露，則又代奸人妄訴，亦以議禮激眾怒為言，不至於濫恩廢法不已，豈不大可異哉！

translations.literal: As for Guo Xun's faction sheltering wicked persons—when the matter of requests and entreatments was exposed, he again on behalf of the wicked person falsely pleaded, also using the rites dispute to inflame public anger as his words, not stopping until indiscriminate favor abolished law— is this not greatly strange!
translations.idiomatic: As for Guo Xun, he shields criminals and, when his back-channel dealings are exposed, pleads their case with the same Rites excuse to stir public outrage— as if no favor is too great and no law too sacred. Is this not outrageous?

sentences.zh: 乞亟斥書、勛而置鑒重典，窮按勛請托事，使人心曉然，知權奸不足恃，國法不可幹，然後逆節潛消，悻門永塞。」

translations.literal: I beg urgently to dismiss Shu and Xun and impose on Jian the heavy statute, thoroughly investigate Xun's request-and-entreatment matters, make people's hearts clearly understand that powerful wicked men are insufficient to rely upon and national law cannot be interfered with—then rebellious conduct will secretly dissolve and the gate of resentment will be forever blocked."
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to dismiss Xi Shu and Guo Xun at once, impose the full penalty on Li Jian, and thoroughly investigate Guo Xun's patronage network. Let everyone see that powerful schemers cannot be trusted and the law cannot be bought—only then will sedition wither and the door to corruption be shut for good."

sentences.zh: 帝弗聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 葉應驄，字肅卿，鄞人。

translations.literal: Ye Yingcong, style name Suqing, was a man of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yingcong, whose style was Suqing, was a native of Yin.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Zhengde 12.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a section chief in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He received an appointment as section chief in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 偕同官諫南巡，杖三十。

translations.literal: Together with colleagues he remonstrated against the southern tour and was beaten thirty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: He joined his colleagues in protesting the southern tour and was beaten thirty strokes.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，歷郎中。

translations.literal: In early Jiajing, he served through bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he rose to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 伏闕爭「大禮」，再下獄廷杖。

translations.literal: He prostrated at the gate disputing the "Great Rites" and again was imprisoned and beaten at court.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the palace-gate protest over the "Great Rites" and was imprisoned and beaten at court a second time.

sentences.zh: 給事中潮陽陳洸素無賴。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Chen Guang of Chaoyang was by nature without reliance.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Chen Guang of Chaoyang was a man of bad character.

sentences.zh: 家居與知縣宋元翰不相能，令其子柱訐元翰謫戍。

translations.literal: At home he was incompatible with Magistrate Song Yuanhan; he had his son Zhu accuse Yuanhan, who was banished to frontier garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: At home he feuded with Magistrate Song Yuanhan and had his son Zhu lodge accusations that got Yuanhan exiled to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 元翰摭洸罪及帷薄事刊布之，名《辨冤錄》。

translations.literal: Yuanhan gathered Guang's crimes and bedroom scandals, printed and published them, naming it 'Record of Vindicating Wrong.'
translations.idiomatic: Song Yuanhan collected evidence of Chen Guang's crimes and private misconduct, and published it under the title "Record of Vindicating the Wronged."

sentences.zh: 洸由是不齒於清議，尚書喬宇出之為湖廣僉事。

translations.literal: Guang thereby was not ranked among pure discussion; Minister Qiao Yu sent him out as assistant commissioner in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guang fell out of favor with the moral critics at court, and Minister Qiao Yu had him posted away as assistant commissioner in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 洸初嘗言獻帝不可稱皇。

translations.literal: Guang at first once said Emperor Xian could not be called emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guang had once argued that the late Emperor Xian ought not to be styled emperor.

sentences.zh: 而是時張璁、桂萼輩以議禮驟顯，洸乃上疏言璁等議是，宜急去本生之稱，因詆宇及文選郎夏良勝，而稱引其黨前給事中於桂、閻閎、史道，前御史曹嘉。

translations.literal: But at that time Zhang Cong, Gui E, and their faction suddenly rose to prominence through the Rites dispute. Guang then submitted a memorial saying Zhang and the others' position was correct—that the title of biological father should be removed at once—and thereby slandered Qiao Yu and Selection Secretary Xia Liangsheng, while citing and praising his faction: former supervising secretaries Yu Gui, Yan Hong, and Shi Dao, and former censor Cao Jia.
translations.idiomatic: By then, however, Zhang Cong, Gui E, and their allies had shot to power on the strength of the Rites dispute. Chen Guang seized the moment with a memorial endorsing their view and urging the immediate abolition of the title of biological father. In the same breath he attacked Qiao Yu and Selection Secretary Xia Liangsheng, while praising his own allies among them: the former supervising secretaries Yu Gui, Yan Hong, and Shi Dao, and the former censor Cao Jia.

sentences.zh: 帝即還洸等職，謫良勝於外。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately restored Guang and the others to their posts and banished Liangsheng to an outside assignment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor at once restored Chen Guang and his allies to office and posted Xia Liangsheng away from the capital.

sentences.zh: 洸遂劾大學士費宏、尚書金獻民、趙鑒、侍郎吳一鵬、朱希周、汪偉、郎中余才、劉天民、員外郎薛蕙、給事中鄭一鵬悉邪黨，而薦廖紀等十五人。

translations.literal: Guang then impeached Grand Secretary Fei Hong, Ministers Jin Xianmin and Li Jian, Vice Ministers Wu Yipeng, Zhu Xizhou, and Wang Wei, Bureau Directors Yu Cai and Liu Tianmin, Section Vice Director Xue Hui, and Supervising Secretary Zheng Yipeng—all as an evil faction—and recommended fifteen men including Liao Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guang next denounced Grand Secretary Fei Hong, Ministers Jin Xianmin and Li Jian, Vice Ministers Wu Yipeng, Zhu Xizhou, and Wang Wei, Bureau Directors Yu Cai and Liu Tianmin, Section Vice Director Xue Hui, and Supervising Secretary Zheng Yipeng as members of a corrupt faction, while recommending fifteen men including Liao Ji to replace them.

sentences.zh: 俄又劾吏部尚書楊旦等。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he again impeached Minister of Personnel Yang Dan and others.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he impeached Minister of Personnel Yang Dan and others as well.

sentences.zh: 帝益大喜。

translations.literal: The Emperor was even more greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 立罷旦，擢紀代之。

translations.literal: Dan was immediately dismissed, and Ji was promoted to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dan was dismissed on the spot, and Liao Ji was promoted to take his place.

sentences.zh: 璁、萼輩遂引以擊異己。

translations.literal: Zhang, Gui, and their faction then brought him in to attack those who differed from them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong, Gui E, and their followers then used him as a weapon against their opponents.

sentences.zh: 給事中趙漢、御史朱衣等交章劾洸，而御史張日韜、戴金、藍田又特疏論之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Zhao Han and Censor Zhu Yi and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Guang, while Censors Zhang Ritao, Dai Jin, and Lan Tian also filed special memorials discussing the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhao Han, Censor Zhu Yi, and others filed one memorial after another impeaching Chen Guang, while Censors Zhang Ritao, Dai Jin, and Lan Tian submitted separate memorials of their own.

sentences.zh: 田並劾席書，且封上元翰《辨冤錄》。

translations.literal: Tian also impeached Xi Shu and, moreover, sealed and submitted Yuanhan's Record of Vindicating the Wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Tian also impeached Xi Shu and submitted Song Yuanhan's Record of Vindicating the Wronged under seal.

sentences.zh: 都御史王時中請罷洸聽勘。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Shizhong requested that Guang be dismissed pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Shizhong asked that Chen Guang be removed from office and held for trial.

sentences.zh: 洸奏：「群奸恨臣抗議大禮，將令撫按殺臣，請遣一錦衣往」。

translations.literal: Guang memorialized: 'The mass of villains hate me for resisting the Great Rites. They will have the provincial governor and censor put me to death. I ask that one Embroidered Uniform Guard be sent.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guang memorialized: 'The whole pack of schemers hates me for opposing the Great Rites and will have the provincial authorities kill me. I beg that an officer of the Embroidered Uniform Guard be sent to investigate.'

sentences.zh: 洸意，錦衣可利誘也。

translations.literal: Guang's idea was that the Embroidered Uniform Guard could be bribed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guang calculated that an Embroidered Uniform Guard officer could be bought off.

sentences.zh: 得旨遣應驄及錦衣千戶李經。

translations.literal: An edict was received dispatching Yingcong and Embroidered Uniform Guard thousand-household Li Jing.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order came down dispatching Ye Yingcong together with Li Jing, a thousand-household of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 應驄與焚香誓天，會御史熊蘭、塗相等雜治，具上洸罪狀至百七十二條。

translations.literal: Yingcong burned incense and swore before Heaven; together with Censors Xiong Lan, Tu Xiang, and others he conducted a joint investigation and submitted in full Guang's criminal charges, amounting to one hundred seventy-two items.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yingcong burned incense and swore an oath before Heaven, then joined Censors Xiong Lan, Tu Xiang, and others in a joint inquiry. In all they submitted one hundred seventy-two counts against Chen Guang.

sentences.zh: 除赦前及曖昧者勿論，當論者十三條。

translations.literal: Excepting those before amnesty and those ambiguous, which were not to be discussed, thirteen items merited judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Charges predating the amnesty and those too unclear to stand were set aside; thirteen counts remained for judgment.

sentences.zh: 罪惡極，宜斬，妻離異，子柱絞。

translations.literal: The crimes were extreme; he should be decapitated, his wife divorced from him, and his son Zhu strangled.
translations.idiomatic: The crimes were judged capital. Chen Guang should be beheaded, his wife divorced from him, and his son Zhu executed by strangulation.

sentences.zh: 洸懼，亡詣闕申訴。

translations.literal: Guang was afraid and fled to the palace gate to plead his case.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Chen Guang fled to the palace gate to plead his case in person.

sentences.zh: 帝持應驄奏不下。

translations.literal: The Emperor withheld Yingcong's memorial and did not release it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor kept Ye Yingcong's report and refused to act on it.

sentences.zh: 尚書趙鑒、副都御史張潤、給事中解一貫、御史鄭本公等連章執奏。

translations.literal: Minister Li Jian, Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhang Run, Supervising Secretary Jie Yigui, Censor Zheng Bengong, and others submitted successive memorials insisting on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Jian, Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhang Run, Supervising Secretary Jie Yigui, Censor Zheng Bengong, and others filed memorial after memorial pressing the case.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，始命覆核。

translations.literal: The Emperor, having no choice, finally ordered a re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, left with no alternative, finally ordered a review.

sentences.zh: 郎中黃綰力持應驄議。

translations.literal: Bureau Director Huang Wan firmly upheld Yingcong's position.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Director Huang Wan staunchly defended Ye Yingcong's findings.

sentences.zh: 書、萼為居間不能得，要璁共奏，謂洸議禮臣，為法官所中。

translations.literal: Shu and Gui interceded as mediators but could not succeed; they wanted Zhang to join in a joint memorial, saying that Guang, as a Rites-dispute official, had been struck down by the judge.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shu and Gui E tried to mediate but failed; they then pressed Zhang Cong to join them in a memorial claiming that Chen Guang, a supporter of the Rites cause, had been undone by the investigating magistrate.

sentences.zh: 帝入其言，命免罪為民。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted their words and ordered that he be absolved of guilt and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took their side and ordered Chen Guang absolved of criminal guilt and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 大理卿湯沐及鑒、一貫更爭之，不聽。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of Justice Tang Mu, along with Jian and Yigui, argued further, but the Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister of Justice Tang Mu, together with Li Jian and Jie Yigui, protested again, but the Emperor would not hear them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，「大禮」書成，並原洸妻子。

translations.literal: Before long, when the "Great Rites" book was completed, Guang's wife and son were also pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward, when the "Great Rites" compendium was finished, Chen Guang's wife and son were pardoned as well.

sentences.zh: 應驄尋遷吉安知府，母喪歸。

translations.literal: Yingcong was soon transferred to prefect of Ji'an; he returned home upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yingcong was soon transferred to prefect of Ji'an, then went home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 六年，驄、萼益用事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Yingcong and Gui wielded power ever more.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Gui E and his faction tightened their grip on power still further.

sentences.zh: 而萼方掌刑部，廷臣馬錄等以劾郭勛下獄。

translations.literal: Moreover, Gui was then in charge of the Ministry of Punishments; court officials such as Ma Lu were imprisoned for impeaching Guo Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E was then running the Ministry of Punishments, and court officials including Ma Lu had been thrown into prison for impeaching Guo Xun.

sentences.zh: 洸謂乘此故案可反也，上書訐應驄等。

translations.literal: Guang said that by seizing this occasion the old case could be reversed; he submitted a memorial accusing Yingcong and others.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guang decided that the moment offered a chance to overturn the old verdict and submitted a memorial accusing Ye Yingcong and his associates.

sentences.zh: 萼因訟洸冤。

translations.literal: Gui E thereby pleaded Guang's grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E took up Chen Guang's cause and pressed his grievance at court.

sentences.zh: 遂逮洸、應驄、元翰、綰，而令按察使張祐等還籍候命，詞連四百人。

translations.literal: They were then arrested: Guang, Yingcong, Yuanhan, and Wan; provincial surveillance commissioners Zhang You and others were ordered to return to their native places pending orders; the case implicated four hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guang, Ye Yingcong, Song Yuanhan, and Huang Wan were arrested; surveillance commissioners such as Zhang You were ordered home to await further instructions; and the case dragged in four hundred people.

sentences.zh: 九卿及錦衣衛廷訊，應驄對曰：「某所持者王章耳，必欲直洸，惟諸公命。」

translations.literal: The Nine Ministers and the Embroidered Uniform Guard interrogated at court; Yingcong replied: "What I hold to is the royal statutes alone. If you must whitewash Guang, that is for you gentlemen to command."
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Ministers and the Embroidered Uniform Guard interrogated the case at court. Ye Yingcong answered: "All I upheld was the law of the realm. If you gentlemen mean to clear Chen Guang, that is your command to give."

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書胡世寧等心知洸罪重，而懲前大獄，不敢執。

translations.literal: Minister of Punishments Hu Shining and others knew in their hearts that Guang's crimes were grave, but chastened by the earlier great case, they did not dare hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Punishments Hu Shining and the others knew perfectly well that Chen Guang's crimes were serious, but shaken by the earlier great purge, none dared stand firm.

sentences.zh: 會是日黃霧四塞，獄弗竟。

translations.literal: It happened that day that yellow fog filled the four quarters, and the trial was not concluded.
translations.idiomatic: That same day yellow fog closed in on every side, and the trial could not be brought to a conclusion.

sentences.zh: 次日，又大風拔木。

translations.literal: The next day a great wind uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: The next day a violent wind tore trees up by the roots.

sentences.zh: 有詔修省，不用刑。

translations.literal: An edict ordered self-examination and rectification; punishments were not to be used.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called for moral self-examination throughout the realm and suspended the use of punishments.

sentences.zh: 乃當應驄按事不實律，為民，元翰、綰及田等貶斥有差，洸授冠帶。

translations.literal: Yingcong was then judged under the statute for investigating matters not in accordance with fact and made a commoner; Yuanhan, Wan, and Tian and others were demoted and banished to varying degrees; Guang was granted cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yingcong was convicted under the statute for investigating a case on false grounds and reduced to commoner status; Song Yuanhan, Huang Wan, Lan Tian, and others were demoted and banished in varying degrees; and Chen Guang was restored to minor official standing with cap and sash.

sentences.zh: 霍韜再疏為洸訟不能得，洸益憾應驄。

translations.literal: Huo Tao again memorialized pleading Guang's case but could not succeed; Guang hated Yingcong all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Tao memorialized again on Chen Guang's behalf but could not prevail, and Chen Guang came to hate Ye Yingcong all the more bitterly.

sentences.zh: 逾數年，更令人奏應驄勘獄時，酷殺無辜二十六人，下巡按李美覆勘。

translations.literal: After several years, others were again made to memorialize that when Yingcong investigated cases he cruelly killed twenty-six innocent persons; the case was sent down to touring censor Li Mei for re-investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, Chen Guang had others submit a memorial accusing Ye Yingcong of having cruelly killed twenty-six innocent people while investigating cases. The matter was referred to touring censor Li Mei for review.

sentences.zh: 美言死者皆有狀，非故殺。

translations.literal: Mei said the dead all had substantiated grounds and it was not deliberate killing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mei reported that each of the dead had been lawfully condemned and that there had been no deliberate murder.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書許贊白應驄無罪。

translations.literal: Minister of Punishments Xu Zan reported that Yingcong was without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Punishments Xu Zan declared Ye Yingcong innocent.

sentences.zh: 帝特謫應驄戍遼東。

translations.literal: The Emperor specially banished Yingcong to garrison service in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor nonetheless banished Ye Yingcong to frontier service in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 是獄也，始終八載。

translations.literal: This case, from beginning to end, lasted eight years.
translations.idiomatic: That case dragged on for eight years from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 凡攻洸與治洸獄者無不得罪，逮捕至百數十人。

translations.literal: All who attacked Guang and those who tried Guang's case were without exception punished; arrests reached more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who had attacked Chen Guang or handled his case was punished in turn, and more than a hundred people were arrested.

sentences.zh: 天下惡萼輩奸橫，益羞言議禮臣矣。

translations.literal: All under Heaven hated Gui and his ilk for their wicked arrogance, and were ever more ashamed to speak of Rites-dispute officials.
translations.idiomatic: People throughout the empire loathed Gui E and his followers for their treachery and bullying, and grew ever more ashamed to hear the Rites-faction officials praised.

sentences.zh: 應驄赴戍所，道經蘇州。

translations.literal: Yingcong went to his garrison post; passing through Suzhou on the way.
translations.idiomatic: On his way to his place of exile, Ye Yingcong passed through Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 知府治具候之，立解維去，致饋不受。

translations.literal: The prefect prepared a feast to receive him; he immediately cast off the mooring lines and departed, and gifts sent after him he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect prepared a banquet to welcome him, but Ye Yingcong cast off at once and sailed away; even gifts sent after him he refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 十六年赦歸。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was pardoned and allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 明堂大享禮成，復寇帶。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall grand sacrifice was completed, he was again granted cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: After the Bright Hall grand sacrifice was completed, he was again granted official cap and sash.

sentences.zh: 應驄敦行誼，好著書，數更患難氣不挫。

translations.literal: Yingcong was earnest in conduct and friendship, fond of writing books, and though he underwent repeated hardships his spirit was not broken.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yingcong was devoted in friendship, loved to write, and though he suffered one ordeal after another, his spirit never broke.

sentences.zh: 黃綰，息人。

translations.literal: Huang Wan was a man of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan was a native of Xi.

sentences.zh: 為刑部主事，諫南巡被杖。

translations.literal: Serving as section chief in the Ministry of Punishments, he remonstrated against the southern tour and was beaten.
translations.idiomatic: As a section chief in the Ministry of Punishments, he protested the southern tour and was beaten with the rod.

sentences.zh: 歷郎中，出為紹興知府，以寬大為治。

translations.literal: He served through bureau director and went out as prefect of Shaoxing, governing with leniency and magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to bureau director, then was appointed prefect of Shaoxing, where he governed with leniency and restraint.

sentences.zh: 被征時，士民哭震野，爭致贐，綰止取二錢。

translations.literal: When he was recalled, scholars and commoners wept so that the fields resounded; they vied to offer burial gifts, but Wan accepted only two cash.
translations.idiomatic: When he was recalled to the capital, scholars and commoners wept until the countryside rang with lament; they competed to send him parting gifts, but Huang Wan accepted only two cash.

sentences.zh: 至京，下詔獄，瘐死。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the capital he was placed in the imperial prison and died of illness in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the capital he was thrown into the imperial prison, where he wasted away and died.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Longqing reign he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 藍田，即墨人。

translations.literal: Lan Tian was a man of Jimo.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Tian was a native of Jimo.

sentences.zh: 爭「大禮」被杖。

translations.literal: He disputed the "Great Rites" and was beaten.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the protest over the "Great Rites" and was beaten with the rod.

sentences.zh: 張璁掌都察院，考察其屬，落職歸。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong took charge of the Censorate and, in examining his subordinates, had him dismissed from office and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong took charge of the Censorate and reviewed its personnel, Lan Tian was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 解一貫，字曾唯，交城人。正德十六年進士。除工科給事中。陳講學、修德、親賢、孝親、任相、遠奸、用諫、謹令、戒欲、恤民十事。世宗嘉納之。嘉靖元年偕御史出核牧馬草場。太監閻洪等奏遣中官一人與俱，一貫言不可，乃已。還朝，劾太監谷大用、李璽奪產殃民罪，帝宥之。而內臣、勛戚所據莊田，率歸之民。帝為後父陳萬言營第，極壯麗。一貫力請裁節，復助楊廷和爭織造，皆不納。歷刑科左右給事中。雲南巡按郭楠以建言，廣東按察使張祐、副使孫懋以辱官校，皆逮治；御史方啟顏以杖死宦官家人落職；元城知縣張好古以拘責戚畹家族鐫級，一貫皆論救。忤旨，停俸。

translations.literal: Jie Yiguan, courtesy name Zengwei, was from Jiaocheng. He became a jinshi in the sixteenth year of Zhengde and was appointed Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Works. He presented ten matters: explaining learning, cultivating virtue, drawing near to the worthy, being filial to parents, appointing ministers, distancing villains, employing remonstrance, making orders careful, restraining desire, and caring for the people. Shizong praised and accepted them. In the first year of Jiajing, he went out with censors to audit pasturelands for herding horses. The eunuch Yan Hong and others memorialized requesting that one palace eunuch be sent with them. Yiguan said this was impermissible, and the matter stopped. Returning to court, he impeached the eunuchs Gu Dayong and Li Xi for the crimes of seizing property and harming the people; the emperor pardoned them. Yet the estates occupied by inner ministers, meritorious nobles, and imperial relatives were generally returned to the people. The emperor built a residence for Chen Wanyan, the father of the empress, and it was extremely magnificent. Yiguan strongly requested restraint and reduction, and again assisted Yang Tinghe in contesting the weaving offices; neither was accepted. He successively served as Left and Right Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Justice. Guo Nan, regional inspector of Yunnan, was arrested for speaking out; Zhang You, Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong, and Sun Mao, Vice Surveillance Commissioner, were arrested for insulting palace constables; Fang Qiyan, a censor, lost office for flogging a eunuch's household servant to death; and Zhang Haogu, magistrate of Yuancheng, was demoted for detaining and rebuking relatives of an imperial in-law. Yiguan argued to save all of them. He offended the emperor's will and had his salary stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Yiguan, courtesy name Zengwei, was a native of Jiaocheng. A jinshi of Zhengde 16, he was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Works. He set out ten proposals: explain learning, cultivate virtue, draw near to worthy men, honor parents, appoint ministers, keep villains at a distance, employ remonstrance, make commands careful, restrain desire, and care for the people. Shizong approved and accepted them. In Jiajing 1 he went out with censors to audit horse-pasture lands. The eunuch Yan Hong and others requested that a palace eunuch be sent along, but Yiguan said this could not be allowed, and the matter was dropped. Back at court he impeached the eunuchs Gu Dayong and Li Xi for seizing property and harming the people; the emperor pardoned them, but estates occupied by eunuchs, meritorious nobles, and imperial relatives were generally returned to the people. The emperor built an extremely magnificent residence for Empress Dowager Chen's father, Chen Wanyan. Yiguan strongly urged restraint, and also helped Yang Tinghe oppose the weaving offices, but neither proposal was accepted. He later served as Left and Right Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice. When Guo Nan, regional inspector of Yunnan, was arrested for speaking out; Zhang You, Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong, and Vice Commissioner Sun Mao for insulting palace constables; Censor Fang Qiyan lost office for flogging a eunuch's servant to death; and Zhang Haogu, magistrate of Yuancheng, was demoted for detaining and rebuking relatives of an imperial in-law, Yiguan argued to save them all. He offended the throne and had his salary suspended.

sentences.zh: 尋進吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to chief supervising secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Yigui was soon promoted to chief supervising secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.

sentences.zh: 教授王價、錄事錢予勛以考察罷，假議禮希復用。

translations.literal: Instructor Wang Jia and recorder Qian Yixun were dismissed in the examination; they feigned Rites-dispute loyalty hoping to be restored to use.
translations.idiomatic: Instructor Wang Jia and recorder Qian Yixun had been dismissed in the personnel review and now pretended devotion to the Rites cause in hopes of being reappointed.

sentences.zh: 一貫等言：「如此，將壞祖宗百年制。」
