translations.literal: Yiguan and others said: "If this is allowed, it will ruin the hundred-year system of our ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: Jie Yiguan and his colleagues said: "If this is permitted, it will destroy a system our ancestors maintained for a century."

sentences.zh: 事竟寢。

translations.literal: The matter in the end was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼日擊費宏不已，一貫偕同官言：「宏立朝行事，律以古大臣固不能無議。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong and Gui E daily attacked Fei Hong without cease. Yigui together with his colleagues said: 'Hong's conduct in office, measured by the standard of ancient great ministers, naturally cannot be without criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E attacked Fei Hong day after day without letup. Jie Yigui and his colleagues submitted a memorial saying: 'Measured by the standards of the great ministers of old, Fei Hong's conduct in office is certainly open to criticism.

sentences.zh: 但入仕至今，未聞有大過。

translations.literal: But from entering office until now, we have not heard of any great fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the day he entered office until now, we have heard of no grave offense on his part.

sentences.zh: 至璁、萼平生奸險，特以議禮一事偶合聖心。

translations.literal: As for Cong and Gui, wicked and treacherous all their lives—they merely happened to accord with the sacred mind on the one matter of the Rites dispute.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E, by contrast, have been treacherous and ruthless all their lives; they won favor only because their view on the Rites dispute happened to suit Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 超擢以來，憑恃寵靈，淩轢朝士。

translations.literal: Since their extraordinary promotion they have relied on imperial favor and trampled court officials.
translations.idiomatic: Since their sudden rise they have leaned on imperial favor and ridden roughshod over their colleagues at court.

sentences.zh: 與宏積怨已久，欲奪其位而居之。

translations.literal: They have nursed resentment against Hong for long and wish to seize his position and occupy it.
translations.idiomatic: They have long nursed a grudge against Fei Hong and now seek to drive him out and take his place.

sentences.zh: 陛下以累疏俱付所司，而於其終乃曰『爾等宜各修乃職』，蓋所以陰折其奸謀者至矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty referred the successive memorials all to the responsible offices, yet at the end said, 'You each should attend to your duties'—this was precisely to secretly thwart their wicked schemes to the fullest extent.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty referred the stream of memorials to the responsible offices, yet ended by saying, 'Each of you should attend to his own duties'—a subtle but unmistakable rebuke meant to break their scheming.

sentences.zh: 二三臣不體至意，或專攻宏，或兼攻璁、萼，不知能去宏，不能去璁、萼也。

translations.literal: Two or three ministers did not grasp the supreme intent—some attacked Hong exclusively, others attacked Cong and Gui as well—not understanding that Hong can be removed but Cong and Gui cannot.
translations.idiomatic: A few ministers failed to grasp Your Majesty's deeper intent: some attacked Fei Hong alone, others Zhang Cong and Gui E as well, not understanding that Hong might be removed, but Cong and Gui would not go with him.

sentences.zh: 君子難進易退，小人則不然。

translations.literal: The superior man finds it hard to advance but easy to withdraw; the petty man is not so.
translations.idiomatic: A man of integrity finds it hard to rise but easy to step aside; a petty man is not like that.

sentences.zh: 宏恤人言，顧廉恥，猶可望以君子。

translations.literal: Hong cares about people's words and respects integrity and shame; one may still hope for him as a superior man.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Hong cares what others say of him and still has a sense of honor; one may still hope to treat him as a man of integrity.

sentences.zh: 璁、萼則小人之尤，何所忌憚？

translations.literal: Cong and Gui are petty men of the worst sort—what do they fear or shrink from?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E are petty men of the worst kind. What would they not dare to do?

sentences.zh: 茍其計得行，則奸邪氣勢愈增，善類中傷無已，天下事將大有可慮者。」

translations.literal: If their scheme succeeds, wicked and evil momentum will increase all the more, the good will be injured without end, and affairs under Heaven will become greatly worrisome."
translations.idiomatic: If their plot succeeds, the wicked will grow bolder still, good men will be slandered without end, and the affairs of the realm will become deeply alarming."

sentences.zh: 時鄭洛書、張錄皆論三人事，而一貫言尤切。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Luoshu and Zhang Lu both discussed the three men's affairs, and Yigui's words were especially cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Luoshu and Zhang Lu also spoke on the three men's conduct at that time, but Jie Yigui's language was the sharpest of all.

sentences.zh: 詔下之所司。

translations.literal: An edict sent the matter down to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 璁、萼等銜不已，竟謫開州判官以卒。

translations.literal: Cong, Gui, and the others nursed resentment without end; in the end he was banished as assistant magistrate of Kaizhou and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong, Gui E, and their allies never forgave the affront; in the end Jie Yigui was banished to serve as assistant magistrate of Kaizhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 鄭洛書，字啟範，莆田人。

translations.literal: Zheng Luoshu, style name Qifan, was a man of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Luoshu, whose style was Qifan, was a native of Putian.

sentences.zh: 弱冠登進士，授上海知縣，有善政。

translations.literal: At weak crown he passed the metropolitan examination, was appointed magistrate of Shanghai, and had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in his early twenties, was appointed magistrate of Shanghai, and governed well.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年召拜御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiajing he was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 4 he was summoned to the capital and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼以陳九川事訐費宏，洛書與同官鄭氣言：「九川事，人謂璁、萼與謀，固已得罪公論，而宏取與之際亦未明。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong and Gui E used the Chen Jiuchuan affair to accuse Fei Hong. Luoshu together with colleague Zheng Qi said: 'In the Jiuchuan affair, people say Cong and Gui plotted together—they have already offended public judgment—but the circumstances of Hong's taking and giving are also not clear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E used the Chen Jiuchuan affair to attack Fei Hong. Zheng Luoshu and his colleague Zheng Qi submitted a memorial saying: 'In the Jiuchuan case, many believe Zhang Cong and Gui E plotted together—a view that has already offended public opinion—but the question of what Fei Hong took or gave is also still unclear.

sentences.zh: 夫朝廷有紀綱，大臣重進退，宏、璁、萼皆不可不去。

translations.literal: The court has its statutes; great ministers prize advancement and withdrawal—Hong, Cong, and Gui all cannot fail to be removed.
translations.idiomatic: The court has its standards, and great ministers are judged by how they advance and withdraw from office. Fei Hong, Zhang Cong, and Gui E all ought to step down.

sentences.zh: 宏不去，則有持祿保位之誚，璁、萼不去，亦冒蹊田奪牛之嫌。」

translations.literal: If Hong does not go, there is the reproach of holding salary and preserving position; if Cong and Gui do not go, they also bear the suspicion of opening a path through the field to take the ox."
translations.idiomatic: If Fei Hong does not leave, he will be accused of clinging to salary and rank; if Zhang Cong and Gui E do not leave, they will look like men who cut a path through another's field to steal his ox."

sentences.zh: 詔責洛書妄言。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Luoshu for reckless words.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked Zheng Luoshu for reckless speech.

sentences.zh: 帝賜尚書趙鑒、席書詩翰，洛書言：「陛下眷禮大臣，此虞廷賡歌之風也。

translations.literal: The Emperor bestowed poetic writings on Ministers Li Jian and Xi Shu. Luoshu said: 'Your Majesty's affectionate courtesy toward great ministers—this is the style of the Yu court's responsive songs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor bestowed poems and calligraphy on Ministers Li Jian and Xi Shu. Zheng Luoshu said: 'Your Majesty's gracious treatment of your ministers recalls the tradition of responsive song at the court of Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 願推此心以念舊。

translations.literal: I wish you would extend this heart to remember the old.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will extend the same spirit to remember those who served you before.

sentences.zh: 如致仕大臣劉健、謝遷、林俊、孫交等，特降宸章，咨訪時政，則聖德益宏。

translations.literal: Such as retired great ministers Liu Jian, Xie Qian, Lin Jun, Sun Jiao, and others—specially send down imperial compositions, consult on current policy—then sagely virtue will be all the greater.
translations.idiomatic: For retired ministers such as Liu Jian, Xie Qian, Lin Jun, and Sun Jiao, send down special imperial writings and seek their counsel on current affairs—then Your Majesty's virtue will shine all the brighter.

sentences.zh: 又推此心以赦過。

translations.literal: Again extend this heart to pardon errors.
translations.idiomatic: Extend the same spirit, too, to pardon past offenses.

sentences.zh: 如遷謫豐熙、劉濟、余寬、王元正等，特垂仁恩，量與牽復，則聖度益廣。」

translations.literal: Such as the banished Feng Xi, Liu Ji, Yu Kuan, Wang Yuanzheng, and others—specially extend benevolent favor, and according to measure grant restoration—then sagely magnanimity will be all the broader."
translations.idiomatic: For exiled officials such as Feng Xi, Liu Ji, Yu Kuan, and Wang Yuanzheng, show special mercy and restore them to office as each case warrants—then Your Majesty's magnanimity will be seen to reach farther still."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The memorial was noted without further action.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was acknowledged, but nothing more was done.

sentences.zh: 李福達獄起，帝將親鞫之，洛書曰：「陛下操獨斷之威，使法官盡得罪，雖有張釋之、於定國，不獲抗辨於人主之前，何以使刑罰中！」

translations.literal: The Li Fuda case arose; the Emperor was about to interrogate it personally. Luoshu said: "Your Majesty wields the authority of sole judgment, causing judges all to be punished—even if there were a Zhang Shizhi or Yu Dingguo, they could not argue before the sovereign lord—how can punishments be made to hit the mark!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Li Fuda case arose and the Emperor prepared to try it in person, Zheng Luoshu said: "If Your Majesty wields the power of sole judgment and leaves every judge in fear of punishment, then even men as upright as Zhang Shizhi and Yu Dingguo could not speak freely before the throne. How, then, can punishments be just?"

sentences.zh: 帝怒，將罪之，楊一清力解而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and was about to punish him; Yang Yiqing forcefully interceded and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and was about to punish him, but Yang Yiqing interceded forcefully and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 尋出視南畿學政，道聞喪歸。

translations.literal: Soon he went out to oversee education policy in the Southern Metropolitan Region; on the road he heard of bereavement and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out to oversee education in the Southern Metropolitan Region, but on the road he received word of a death in the family and returned home.

sentences.zh: 十二年京察事竣，更命科道官互糾，洛書被劾落職。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when the capital evaluation was concluded, officials were further ordered to mutually impeach one another among the censorate; Luoshu was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, after the capital evaluation was finished, censorate officials were ordered to impeach one another in turn, and Zheng Luoshu was denounced and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 給事中饒秀為御史所劾，無所泄憤，復劾洛書及王重賢等九人貪汙阘茸。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Rao Xiu, having been impeached by a censor with no outlet for his fury, again impeached Luoshu and Wang Chongxian and eight others for greed, corruption, and incompetence.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Rao Xiu, impeached by a censor and with no other outlet for his anger, turned around and accused Zheng Luoshu, Wang Chongxian, and seven others of corruption and incompetence.

sentences.zh: 重賢等皆降黜。

translations.literal: Chongxian and the others were all demoted and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongxian and the others were all demoted and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 時論駭之。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion was shocked.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion was appalled.

sentences.zh: 洛書家居再逾歲卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: Luoshu at home passed away after two more years, age thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Luoshu lived at home a little more than two years longer and died at the age of thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子開，往依上海。

translations.literal: His son Kai went to rely on Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kai went to live in Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 上海人治田百畝資之。

translations.literal: People of Shanghai worked a hundred mu of fields to support him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shanghai worked a hundred mu of land to support him.

sentences.zh: 歲一至，收其入以歸。

translations.literal: Once each year he came, collected its yield, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he would travel there, collect the harvest, and return home.

sentences.zh: 張錄，字宗制，城武人。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu, styled Zongzhi, was a native of Chengwu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu, courtesy name Zongzhi, was from Chengwu.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: Presented Scholar in the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in Zhengde 6 (1511).

sentences.zh: 授太常博士，擢御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an erudite at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，伏闕爭「大禮」，下獄廷杖。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing, he prostrated at the palace gate disputing the "Great Rites," and was imprisoned and beaten at court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he joined the palace-gate protest over the "Great Rites" and was imprisoned and flogged at court.

sentences.zh: 出按畿輔，劾宣府諸將失事，皆伏辜。

translations.literal: Sent out to inspect the capital region, he impeached the various generals of Xuanfu for failures, and all paid the penalty.
translations.idiomatic: As an inspecting censor in the capital region, he impeached the generals stationed at Xuanfu for military failures; all were convicted.

sentences.zh: 西域魯迷貢獅子、西牛方物，言所貢玉石計費二萬三千余金，往來且七年，邀中國重賞。

translations.literal: Lu Mi of the Western Regions presented lions, a zebu, and regional products, stating the jade and stones presented cost more than 23,000 units of gold; they had come and gone for nearly seven years, seeking heavy rewards from China.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from Lu Mi in the Western Regions brought lions, a zebu, and other tribute, claiming the jade they presented had cost more than 23,000 taels of gold; their embassies had shuttled back and forth for nearly seven years in hopes of lavish rewards from the Ming court.

sentences.zh: 錄言：「明王不貴異物。

translations.literal: Lu stated: "An enlightened king does not value strange things.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu memorialized: "A sage ruler does not prize exotic curios.

sentences.zh: 今二獅日各飼一羊，是歲用七百余羊也。

translations.literal: Now the two lions each day are fed one sheep each—that is more than seven hundred sheep used in a year.
translations.idiomatic: At present the two lions consume one sheep apiece daily—more than seven hundred sheep over the course of a year.

sentences.zh: 牛食芻菽，今乃食果餌，則食人之食矣。

translations.literal: Oxen eat fodder and beans; now they eat fruit delicacies—thus they eat people's food.
translations.idiomatic: Cattle are meant to eat hay and grain, yet this beast is fed sweetmeats and fruit—it consumes food meant for human beings.

sentences.zh: 願返其獻，歸其人，薄其賞，以阻希望心。」

translations.literal: I wish to return their presentation, send back their people, reduce their reward, in order to block the heart of hope."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that their tribute be sent back, their envoys returned home, and their rewards kept modest, so as to discourage such hopeful schemes."

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed his advice.

sentences.zh: 張璁擢兵部侍郎，錄與諸御史爭之，不聽。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong was promoted to Vice Minister of War; Lu and the various censors disputed it, but the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong was elevated to Vice Minister of War, Zhang Lu and fellow censors protested, but the emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 璁與桂萼屢攻費宏，錄言：「今水旱相仍，變異叠出，正臣工修省時。

translations.literal: Cong and Gui E repeatedly attacked Fei Hong; Lu stated: "Now flood and drought follow in succession, anomalies appear one after another—this is precisely the time for ministers to practice self-examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E kept assailing Fei Hong. Zhang Lu memorialized: "Floods and droughts come one after another, and ominous portents multiply—this is precisely when officials should examine their conduct and reform.

sentences.zh: 諸人為國股肱，相傾排若此，欲弭災變，不亦難乎？

translations.literal: These men are the arms and thighs of the state, yet mutually overthrowing and excluding one another like this—to wish to appease disasters and anomalies, is it not also difficult?
translations.idiomatic: These men are the pillars of the realm, yet they tear one another down like this—how can we hope to avert heaven's warnings?

sentences.zh: 乞並黜三人，以回天譴。」

translations.literal: I beg that all three be dismissed together to turn back heaven's wrath."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all three be removed from office at once, so that heaven's reproof may be withdrawn."

sentences.zh: 帝為戒諭璁、萼。

translations.literal: The emperor admonished and instructed Cong and E.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a warning reproach to Zhang Cong and Gui E.

sentences.zh: 後璁以侍郎總臺事，修前憾。

translations.literal: Later Cong, as vice minister in overall charge of censorial affairs, nursed old resentments.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as vice minister overseeing censorial affairs, Zhang Cong settled old scores.

sentences.zh: 言錄不諳憲體，遂罷歸。

translations.literal: He said Lu did not understand censorial form, and Lu was thereupon dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed Zhang Lu did not understand proper censorial conduct, and Lu was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 家居二十年，卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for twenty years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for twenty years, then died.

sentences.zh: 陸粲，字子余，長州人。

translations.literal: Lu Can, styled Ziyu, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Can, courtesy name Ziyu, was from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 少謁同里王鏊，鏊異之曰：「此子必以文名天下。」

translations.literal: In youth he paid a visit to Wang Ao of his native place; Ao considered him remarkable and said: "This youth will certainly make a literary name throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he called on Wang Ao, a fellow townsman; Ao took notice of him and said, "This boy is destined to win literary fame throughout the empire."

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年成進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiajing he became Presented Scholar and was selected as Hanlin Academician Expected.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in Jiajing 5 (1526) and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 七試皆第一。

translations.literal: In seven examinations he was each time first.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in all seven examinations.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼盡出庶吉士為部曹、縣令，粲以才獨得工科給事中。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong and Gui E entirely sent Hanlin bachelors out as ministry section chiefs and county magistrates; Can alone, for his talent, obtained the post of supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E had all the Hanlin bachelors transferred to ministry posts and county magistracies, but Lu Can alone—on account of his talent—was retained as supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works.

sentences.zh: 勁挺敢言。

translations.literal: Strong and upright, he dared to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and outspoken, he fearlessly spoke his mind.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「我朝太祖至宣宗，大臣造膝陳謀，不啻家人父子。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: "From our dynasty's Taizu to Xuanzong, great ministers spoke their plans at close knee, no different from family father and son.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "From the Hongwu Emperor to the Xuande Emperor, senior ministers counseled the throne face to face, as intimately as father and son within a household.

sentences.zh: 自英宗幼沖，大臣為權宜計，常朝奏事，先日擬旨，其余政事具疏封進，沿襲至今。

translations.literal: From Yingzong's youth on the throne, great ministers for expediency's sake, in regular court reporting affairs, drafted rescripts the day before; other governance was fully memorialized, sealed and submitted—this has been inherited down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: After the young Emperor Yingzong came to the throne, ministers adopted a temporary practice: at regular audiences they would submit memoranda drafted the day before for imperial rescripts, while other business was sent in sealed memorials—a habit that persists to this day.

sentences.zh: 今陛下銳意圖治，願每日朝罷，退御便殿，延見大臣；

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is keen to seek good governance; I wish that each day after court, retiring to the convenient hall, you extend audience to great ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is now determined to restore good governance. I ask that after each morning audience you withdraw to the Privy Chamber and receive senior ministers;

sentences.zh: 侍從臺諫輪日奏對；

translations.literal: Attendants and censorial remonstrators in rotation by day report and respond;
translations.idiomatic: let attending officials and remonstrating censors take turns presenting their counsel each day;

sentences.zh: 撫按藩臬廷辭入謝，召訪便宜；

translations.literal: Grand coordinators, inspecting censors, provincial princes, and surveillance commissioners at court leave-taking to enter thanks—you should summon them to consult on convenience;
translations.idiomatic: when grand coordinators, inspecting censors, princes, and provincial surveillance commissioners take their leave at court, summon them to seek their practical advice on local affairs;

sentences.zh: 復妙選博聞有道之士，更番入直，講論經史，如仁宗弘文閣故事。

translations.literal: Further, carefully select men of broad learning and the Way, in rotation enter duty, discuss and expound classics and histories, like Renzong's Hongwen Pavilion precedent.
translations.idiomatic: moreover, select accomplished scholars of wide learning, who would serve in rotation at court to lecture on the classics and histories, following the Hongwen Pavilion precedent of the Renzong era.

sentences.zh: 則上下情通，而天下事畢陳於前矣。」

translations.literal: Then above and below sentiments will connect, and all affairs under heaven will be fully laid out before you."
translations.idiomatic: Then the feelings of court and realm would flow freely, and every matter of state be set plainly before Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed his advice.

sentences.zh: 既言資格獨重進士，致貢舉無上進階，州縣教職過輕，王官終身禁錮，皆宜變通。

translations.literal: He further stated that seniority alone valued Presented Scholars, causing the tribute-student and recommendation paths to have no advancement, prefectural and county teaching posts to be too lightly regarded, and Wang officials to be lifelong confined—all ought to be flexibly reformed.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to argue that overvaluing examination rank alone blocked career paths for tribute students and recommendees, made prefectural and county teaching posts too slight, and locked minor officials into posts for life—all policies that cried out for reform.

sentences.zh: 因陳久任使、慎考察、汰冗官諸事，而終之以復制科，仿唐、宋法，數歲一舉，以待異才：「高者儲之禁近，其次分置諸曹，先有官者遞進，庶人才畢出，野無遺賢。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he set forth matters of long tenure in office, careful evaluation, and weeding out redundant officials, and ended by reviving the special examinations, imitating Tang and Song methods, holding them every several years to await exceptional talent: "The highest should be stored in forbidden proximity; the next placed in the various bureaus; those already holding office should advance in turn—thus talent will all emerge and none will be left in the wilds."
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed long tenure for capable officials, careful performance reviews, and cuts to redundant posts, and concluded by urging revival of the special examination system on the Tang and Song model, held every few years to surface unusual talent: "The most gifted should be groomed for palace service, the next tier assigned to the ministries, and incumbent officials allowed to advance in turn—so that talent of every kind would come forward and no worthy man be left neglected."

sentences.zh: 尋偕御史郗元洪清核馬房錢谷。

translations.literal: Soon he joined Censor Chi Yuanhong in clearing and auditing the stables' grain and funds.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he worked with Censor Chi Yuanhong to audit accounts at the imperial stables.

sentences.zh: 抗疏折御馬太監閻洪，宿弊為清。

translations.literal: In a forceful memorial he refuted Stud Eunuch Yan Hong, and longstanding abuses were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: In a bold memorial he took on Imperial Stud Eunuch Yan Hong, and long-standing abuses were cleaned up.

sentences.zh: 與同官劉希簡爭張福獄。

translations.literal: With colleague Liu Xijian he disputed the Zhang Fu case.
translations.idiomatic: He locked horns with fellow supervising secretary Liu Xijian over the Zhang Fu case.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，俱下詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; both were sent to the edict prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and had both men thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 杖三十，釋還職。

translations.literal: Beaten thirty blows, released and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: They were flogged thirty strokes and then released to resume their posts.

sentences.zh: 事具《熊浹傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is fully given in the Biography of Xiong Jia.
translations.idiomatic: The full account of this affair is given in the biography of Xiong Jia.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼並居政府，專擅朝事。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong and Gui E both occupied the government, monopolizing court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E held power together and dominated court affairs at will.

sentences.zh: 給事中孫應奎、王準發其私，帝猶溫旨慰諭。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Sun Yingkui and Wang Zhun exposed their private conduct; the emperor still sent warm edicts to comfort and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Sun Yingkui and Wang Zhun exposed their misconduct, yet the emperor responded with soothing edicts of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 粲不勝憤，上疏曰：

translations.literal: Can, unable to contain fury, submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lu Can, unable to contain his anger, submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 璁、萼，兇險之資，乖僻之學。

translations.literal: Cong and E—natures of fierce danger, learning of perverse deviation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E are men of vicious temperament who subscribe to perverse doctrines.

sentences.zh: 曩自小臣贊大禮，拔置近侍，不三四年位至宰弼。

translations.literal: Formerly, from minor officials supporting the Great Rites, they were pulled up and placed in close attendance; in less than three or four years they reached the rank of chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Only a few years ago they were obscure officials who lent their voices to the Great Rites controversy; whisked into the emperor's inner circle, they rose within three or four years to the highest offices of state.

sentences.zh: 恩隆寵異，振古未聞。

translations.literal: Favour lofty and treatment exceptional—unheard of since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Such extravagant favour is without precedent in all history.

sentences.zh: 乃敢罔上逞私，專權招賄，擅作威福，報復恩仇。

translations.literal: Yet they dare deceive the ruler and indulge private ends, monopolize power and invite bribes, arbitrarily wield authority and blessings, and repay kindness and settle grudges.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they dare deceive the throne, abuse their power, solicit bribes, lord it over the court, and settle personal scores.

sentences.zh: 璁狠愎自用，執拗多私。

translations.literal: Cong is fierce, obstinate, and self-willed; stubborn with much private motive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong is cruel, opinionated, and willful, twisting every dispute to private ends.

sentences.zh: 萼外若寬迂，中實深刻。

translations.literal: E outwardly seems broad and obtuse; inwardly he is truly harsh and deep.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E wears a mask of mildness, but at heart he is ruthlessly vindictive.

sentences.zh: 忮忍之毒一發於心，如蝮蛇猛獸，犯者必死。

translations.literal: The poison of jealous forbearance, once released from the heart, is like vipers and fierce beasts—whoever offends must die.
translations.idiomatic: Once his spite takes hold, he strikes like a viper or maddened beast—whoever crosses him is doomed.

sentences.zh: 臣請姑舉數端言之。

translations.literal: Your subject begs to cite for the moment several instances in speaking.
translations.idiomatic: I shall cite only a few of their outrages.

sentences.zh: 萼受尚書王瓊賂遺鉅萬，連章力薦，璁從中主之，遂得起用。

translations.literal: E received bribes and gifts amounting to tens of thousands from Minister Wang Qiong; he submitted consecutive memorials forcefully recommending him; Cong from within supported it, and Qiong was thereupon able to rise and be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E accepted bribes of tens of thousands from Minister Wang Qiong and lobbied relentlessly for his recall; Zhang Cong backed the move from behind the scenes, and Qiong was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 昌化伯邵傑，本邵氏養子，萼納重賄，竟使奴隸小人濫襲伯爵。

translations.literal: Changhua Earl Shao Jie was originally an adopted son of the Shao clan; E accepted heavy bribes and in the end caused a slave-like petty man to usurp succession to the earldom.
translations.idiomatic: Changhua Earl Shao Jie was merely an adopted son of the Shao family; Gui E took a large bribe and helped this base-born upstart seize an hereditary earldom.

sentences.zh: 萼所厚醫官李夢鶴假托進書，夤緣受職，居室相鄰，中開便戶往來，常與萼家人吳從周等居間。

translations.literal: E's favored physician-official Li Menghao, under false pretense of presenting books, schemed by connection to receive office; their dwellings adjoined, with a convenience door opened between for coming and going; he often acted as intermediary with E's household members Wu Congzhou and others.
translations.idiomatic: Li Menghao, a physician Gui E favored, gained office by pretending to offer books as tribute; their houses stood side by side with a private door between them for constant traffic, and Li regularly served as a go-between for Gui E's household retainers such as Wu Congzhou.

sentences.zh: 又引鄉人周時望為選郎，交通鬻爵。

translations.literal: He further introduced his fellow townsman Zhou Shiwang as selection bureau director, communicating and selling offices.
translations.idiomatic: He also installed his countryman Zhou Shiwang as Selection Bureau director, who traded in offices and sold appointments.

sentences.zh: 時望既去，胡森代之。

translations.literal: After Shiwang had left, Hu Sen replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Shiwang left, Hu Sen took his place.

sentences.zh: 森與主事楊麟、王激又輔臣鄉里親戚也。

translations.literal: Sen together with section chiefs Yang Lin and Wang Ji were again fellow hometowns and kinsmen of the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sen, together with section chiefs Yang Lin and Wang Ji, were also hometown relatives of the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 銓司要地，盡布私人。

translations.literal: The crucial posts of the appointment bureau were entirely spread with private men.
translations.idiomatic: Every key post in the appointment bureau was filled with their own men.

sentences.zh: 典選僅逾年，引用鄉故，不可悉數。

translations.literal: Overseeing selection for barely more than a year, he employed fellow townsfolk and old associates—they cannot all be counted.
translations.idiomatic: In little more than a year of managing appointments, he packed the bureaucracy with hometown connections beyond count.

sentences.zh: 如致仕尚書劉麟，其中表親也。

translations.literal: For example, retired Minister Liu Lin—he was a maternal cousin on the mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Retired Minister Liu Lin, for instance, was a maternal cousin of Gui E.

sentences.zh: 侍郎嚴嵩，其子之師也。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Yan Song was his son's teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Yan Song had been tutor to his son.

sentences.zh: 僉都御史李如圭，由按察使一轉徑入內臺，南京太仆少卿夏尚樸，由知府期月遂得清卿，禮部員外張假歷律而結知，御史戴金承風搏擊，甘心鷹犬，皆萼姻黨，相與朋比為奸者也。

translations.literal: Assistant Censor-in-Chief Li Rugui, from Surveillance Commissioner in one transfer went straight into the inner censorate; Nanjing Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Xia Shangpu, from prefect in one month then obtained a pure ministerial post; Ministry of Rites Section Vice Director Zhang Jia climbed through the ranks in order and formed connections; Censor Dai Jin caught the wind to strike, willing to be hawk and hound—all were E's affinal party, mutually banding together as villains.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Censor-in-Chief Li Rugui leapt from surveillance commissioner straight into the inner censorate; Nanjing Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Xia Shangpu rose from prefect to a prestigious central post in a single month; Ministry of Rites Section Vice Director Zhang Jia climbed the ladder of promotion and won Gui E's favor; Censor Dai Jin joined the attack at the first sign of favor—all were Gui E's in-laws and cronies, banding together in corruption.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書李時柔和善逢，猾狡多智，南京禮部尚書黃綰曲學阿世，虛談眩人，諭德彭澤夤緣改秩，躐玷清華，皆陰厚於璁而陽附於萼者也。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Li Shi was gentle, soft, and skilled at flattery; crafty and cunning with much wit; Nanjing Minister of Rites Huang Guan had crooked learning and fawned on the age, empty talk to dazzle people; Preceptor Peng Ze schemed by connection to change rank, leaping to stain pure elegance—all secretly thick with Cong while outwardly attaching to E.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Li Shi was smooth and adept at flattery; cunning and shrewd. Nanjing Minister of Rites Huang Guan peddled distorted learning and pandered to the times with empty talk designed to dazzle. Preceptor Peng Ze schemed his way into a higher rank, staining a once-pure office—all of them secretly loyal to Zhang Cong while openly attaching themselves to Gui E.

sentences.zh: 璁等威權既盛，黨與復多，天下畏惡，莫敢訟言。

translations.literal: Cong and the others' authoritative power already flourishing, and their faction numerous besides, all under heaven feared and loathed them; none dared speak in accusation.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhang Cong and his allies wielding such power and commanding so large a faction, the realm feared and detested them, and no one dared bring charges openly.

sentences.zh: 不亟去之，兇人之性不移，將來必為社稷患。

translations.literal: If not urgently removed, the nature of fierce men will not change; in the future they will surely become a calamity for state and altars.
translations.idiomatic: Unless they are removed at once, these ruthless men will never change; they are certain to become a grave threat to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 帝大感悟，立下詔暴璁、萼罪狀，罷其相；

translations.literal: The emperor greatly came to enlightened feeling, immediately issued an edict exposing Cong and E's crimes, and removed them from the chancellorship;
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, the emperor at once issued an edict publicizing the crimes of Zhang Cong and Gui E and dismissed them from the chief ministership;

sentences.zh: 而以粲不早發，下之吏。

translations.literal: Yet because Can had not spoken out earlier, he was handed over to the judicial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: but because Lu Can had not spoken sooner, he was turned over to the judicial authorities for prosecution.

sentences.zh: 既而詹事霍韜力詆粲，謂楊一清嗾之。

translations.literal: Before long, Junior Tutor Huo Tao forcefully slandered Can, saying Yang Yiqing had instigated him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Junior Tutor Huo Tao launched a furious attack on Lu Can, claiming Yang Yiqing had put him up to it.

sentences.zh: 希簡言：「璁、萼去位由聖斷。

translations.literal: Xijian stated: "Cong and E's removal from office was by the sage's decision.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xijian responded: "Zhang Cong and Gui E lost office by the emperor's own sacred decision.

sentences.zh: 且使犬謂之嗾，韜以言官比之犬，侮朝廷。」

translations.literal: Moreover, to make a dog be called instigating—Tao compared speaking officials to dogs, insulting the court."
translations.idiomatic: To say furthermore that a dog was set to incite them is to compare remonstrating officials to dogs—an insult to the entire court."

sentences.zh: 而帝竟納韜言，召璁還，奪一清官，下希簡詔獄，釋還職，謫粲貴州都鎮驛丞。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor ultimately accepted Tao's words, recalled Cong, stripped Yiqing of office, sent Xijian to the edict prison, released and restored him to office, and demoted Can to post station assistant at Duzhen in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor ultimately heeded Huo Tao, recalled Zhang Cong, stripped Yang Yiqing of office, threw Liu Xijian into the imperial prison but then released him to resume his post, and demoted Lu Can to post-station assistant at Duzhen in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 稍遷永新知縣。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Magistrate of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to magistrate of Yongxin county.

sentences.zh: 前後獲盜數百人，奸猾屏跡。

translations.literal: Before and after he captured bandits numbering several hundred; the crafty and slippery vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: In the course of his tenure he captured several hundred bandits, and local ruffians were driven into hiding.

sentences.zh: 久之，以念母乞歸。

translations.literal: After a long time, because of longing for his mother he begged to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he requested leave to return home to care for his aging mother.

sentences.zh: 論薦者三十余疏，皆報罷。

translations.literal: Those discussing recommendation: more than thirty memorials—all answered with dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty memorials recommending him for reappointment were all rejected.

sentences.zh: 霍韜亦薦粲，粲曰：「天下事大壞憸人手，尚欲以余波汙我耶？」

translations.literal: Huo Tao also recommended Can; Can said: "Affairs under heaven have been greatly ruined in the hands of the treacherous—do you still wish to stain me with the lingering ripples?"
translations.idiomatic: Huo Tao also recommended Lu Can for office. Lu Can replied, "The empire has already been ruined in the hands of such schemers—are you trying to smear me with their leftover filth?"

sentences.zh: 母歿，毀甚，未終喪而卒。

translations.literal: His mother died; he was greatly grief-stricken and, before the mourning period ended, he died.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died he mourned with devastating grief and died before the mourning period was finished.

sentences.zh: 劉希簡，字以順，漢州人。

translations.literal: Liu Xijian, styled Yishun, was a native of Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xijian, courtesy name Yishun, was from Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 進士。

translations.literal: Presented Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He was a jinshi graduate.

sentences.zh: 除行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier.

sentences.zh: 為工科給事中，甫五月，兩以直言得罪，聲大振。

translations.literal: Serving as supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works, in only five months he twice offended through straight speech, and his reputation greatly resounded.
translations.idiomatic: As supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works, within only five months he twice offended the throne by speaking bluntly, and his reputation spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 久之，謫縣丞。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was demoted to county assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was demoted to county assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 終鞏昌知府。

translations.literal: He ended as Prefect of Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 王準。

translations.literal: Wang Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhun —

sentences.zh: 字子推，世籍秦府儀衛司。

translations.literal: Styled Zitui; his family was registered in the Qin Prince's Guard Command.
translations.idiomatic: Courtesy name Zitui; his family held hereditary registration in the Qin Prince's guard command.

sentences.zh: 準以進士授知縣。

translations.literal: Zhun, as Presented Scholar, was appointed county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhun, as a jinshi graduate, was appointed county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 為禮科給事中，巡視京營，劾郭勛專恣罪。

translations.literal: Serving as supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites, he inspected the capital garrisons and impeached Guo Xun for monopolizing power and acting wilfully.
translations.idiomatic: As supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites, he inspected the capital garrisons and impeached Guo Xun for abusing his authority.

sentences.zh: 明年，劾璁、萼引私人。

translations.literal: The next year, he impeached Cong and E for bringing in private men.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he impeached Zhang Cong and Gui E for installing their own partisans.

sentences.zh: 璁、萼罷，準亦下吏，謫富民典史。

translations.literal: Cong and E were dismissed; Zhun also was handed to the clerks and demoted to clerk of Fumin.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong and Gui E were dismissed, Wang Zhun was also handed over to the judicial authorities and demoted to clerk at Fumin.

sentences.zh: 稍遷知縣。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted again to county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 都御史汪鋐萘希璁指，以考察罷之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Yang, following Cong's pointer, had him dismissed through evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Yang, ingratiating himself with Zhang Cong's wishes, had him dismissed through a performance review.

sentences.zh: 邵經邦，字仲德，仁和人。

translations.literal: Shao Jingbang, styled Zhongde, was a native of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Jingbang, courtesy name Zhongde, was from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年進士。

translations.literal: Presented Scholar in the sixteenth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in Zhengde 16 (1521).

sentences.zh: 授工部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed section chief in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He became section chief in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 榷荊州稅，甫三月，稅額滿，遂啟關任商舟往來。

translations.literal: Levying tax at Jingzhou, in only three months the tax quota was filled, and he thereupon opened the pass to allow merchant boats to come and go.
translations.idiomatic: While collecting customs duties at Jingzhou, he filled the tax quota within three months and then opened the checkpoint to allow merchant vessels to pass freely.

sentences.zh: 進員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to section vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to section vice director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年冬十月，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the eighth year of Jiajing, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Jiajing 8 (1529), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 經邦時官刑部，上疏曰：

translations.literal: Jingbang at the time held office in the Ministry of Punishments and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shao Jingbang was then serving in the Ministry of Punishments and submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 茲者正陽之月，有日食之異。

translations.literal: At this time, in the month of Correct Yang, there was the anomaly of a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Now, in the first month of the year, a solar eclipse has occurred.

sentences.zh: 質諸《小雅十月》之篇，變象懸符。

translations.literal: If one tests it against the chapter 'Tenth Month' in the Minor Odes, the signs of change hang in correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against the 'Tenth Month' ode in the Book of Songs, the omen of change is unmistakable.

sentences.zh: 說《詩》者謂陰壯之甚，由不用善人，而其咎專歸皇父。

translations.literal: Those who expound the Odes say that when yin grows excessively strong, it is because good men are not employed, and the blame is assigned solely to Royal Father.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators on the Odes hold that when yin overwhelms yang, it is because worthy men are not used—and the fault is laid entirely at Royal Father's door.

sentences.zh: 然則今之調和變理者，得無有皇父其人乎？

translations.literal: Then might not those who now harmonize and transform affairs be a Royal Father in person?
translations.idiomatic: Might those who now hold the reins of state and claim to set things right not be playing the part of Royal Father themselves?

sentences.zh: 邇陛下納陸粲言，命張璁、桂萼致仕。

translations.literal: Recently Your Majesty accepted Lu Can's words and ordered Zhang Cong and Gui E to retire from office.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago Your Majesty heeded Lu Can and dismissed Zhang Cong and Gui E from office.

sentences.zh: 尋以璁議禮有功，復召輔政。

translations.literal: Soon, because Cong had merit in debating the rites, he was again summoned to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on the grounds that Zhang Cong had served the rites debate well, he was recalled to serve as chief counselor.

sentences.zh: 人言籍籍，陛下莫之恤也。

translations.literal: People's words buzzed everywhere, yet Your Majesty did not pity or heed them.
translations.idiomatic: Public murmuring spread far and wide, yet Your Majesty paid it no heed.

sentences.zh: 乃天變若此，安可勿畏？

translations.literal: Yet Heaven's transformation is like this—how can one fail to fear it?
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven sends such a sign, how can we not tremble before it?

sentences.zh: 夫議禮與臨政不同。

translations.literal: Now, debating rites and presiding over government are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Debating ritual and governing the realm are two different matters.

sentences.zh: 議禮貴當，臨政貴公。

translations.literal: In debating rites, correctness is prized; in presiding over government, impartiality is prized.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual debate calls for what is right; governance calls for what is fair.

sentences.zh: 正皇考之徽稱，以明父子之倫，禮之當也。

translations.literal: To rectify the honored title of the Imperial Father and thereby clarify the principle of father and son is what ritual requires.
translations.idiomatic: Establishing the proper honorific for Your Majesty's father and thereby affirming the bond between father and son is indeed what ritual demands.

sentences.zh: 雖排眾論，任獨見，而不以為偏。

translations.literal: Even if one rejects the crowd's opinions and trusts one's own view alone, this need not be regarded as partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Even to override popular opinion and stand on one's own judgment need not count as bias—so long as the matter is ritual, not politics.

sentences.zh: 若夫用人行政，則當辨別忠邪，審量才力，與天下之人共用之，乃為公耳。

translations.literal: As for employing men and administering affairs, one ought to distinguish loyal from treacherous, weigh talent and capacity, and share office with all under Heaven—only then is it impartial.
translations.idiomatic: But in appointing officials and running the government, one must distinguish the loyal from the corrupt, weigh each man's ability, and share power with the worthy across the realm. That alone is true impartiality.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以璁議禮有功，不察其人，不揆其才，而加之大任，似私議禮之臣也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, because Cong had merit in debating rites, without examining the man or measuring his talent, has laid upon him a great charge—this resembles favoring a minister for private reasons in the rites debate.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now rewards Zhang Cong's service in the rites controversy with high office without scrutinizing his character or capacity. This looks like patronage of a partisan in the ritual dispute.

sentences.zh: 私議禮之臣，是不以所議者為公禮也。

translations.literal: To favor a minister in the rites debate is not to treat what was debated as public ritual.
translations.idiomatic: To reward a partisan of the rites debate is to treat the rites themselves as a private matter, not a public one.

sentences.zh: 夫禮唯至公，乃可萬世不易。

translations.literal: Ritual, only when it is utterly impartial, can remain unchanged for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual endures for all time only when it rests on absolute impartiality.

sentences.zh: 設近於私，則固可守也，亦可變也。

translations.literal: If it approaches the private, then though it may be kept, it may also be changed.
translations.idiomatic: But if ritual is tainted by private interest, what can be upheld today can just as easily be overturned tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 陛下果以尊親之典為至當，而欲子孫世世守之乎？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly holds the rites of honoring one's kin to be utterly correct and wishes descendants to guard them generation after generation—
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly believes the rites honoring your father are beyond reproach and wishes your descendants to uphold them forever—

sentences.zh: 則莫若於諸臣之進退，一付諸至公，優其賚予，全其終始，以答其議禮之功，而博求海內碩德重望之賢，以弼成正大光明之業，則人心定，天道順，俾萬年之後，廟號世宗，子孫百世不遷，顧不偉歟？

translations.literal: —then there is nothing better than to entrust all ministers' advancement and dismissal wholly to utmost impartiality, enrich their rewards and grants, preserve them from beginning to end to repay their merit in debating rites, and broadly seek throughout the realm men of great virtue and heavy reputation to assist in completing a grand, upright, and luminous enterprise. Then people's hearts would be settled, Heaven's Way would accord, and ten thousand years hence, with the temple name Shizong, descendants for a hundred generations would not be displaced—is this not magnificent?
translations.idiomatic: —then entrust every minister's appointment and dismissal to absolute fairness. Reward those who served the rites debate generously and honor them to the end, then seek out the most respected worthies across the empire to help complete a great and luminous reign. Hearts would be at rest, Heaven would be appeased, and ten thousand years from now Your Majesty's temple name Shizong would stand unshaken for a hundred generations. Would that not be magnificent?

sentences.zh: 如徒加以非分之任，使之履盈蹈滿，犯天人之怒，亦非璁等福也。

translations.literal: If one merely adds an unmerited charge and makes them tread where the cup overflows and the measure is full, provoking the wrath of Heaven and men, this is also not a blessing for Cong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: But to heap undeserved power upon them, driving them past the brim until they provoke the wrath of Heaven and the people—that would be no blessing to Zhang Cong and his allies either.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，立下鎮撫司拷訊。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged and had him immediately sent to the Embroidered Uniform Guard for interrogation under torture.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage and had him thrown into the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison for torture and interrogation.

sentences.zh: 獄上，請送法司擬罪。

translations.literal: When the case was submitted, they requested that he be sent to the judicial offices to have punishment determined.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was reported, the prison authorities asked that he be handed over to the regular courts for sentencing.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此非常犯，不必下法司。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "This is not an ordinary offense; there is no need to send it down to the judicial offices."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "This is no ordinary crime. It need not go to the regular courts."

sentences.zh: 遂謫戍福建鎮海衛。

translations.literal: He was thereupon banished to garrison duty at Zhenhai in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished to serve at the Zhenhai garrison in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 十六年，皇子生，大赦。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, a prince was born and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 16 (1537), the birth of a prince was marked by a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 惟經邦與豐熙等八人不在赦例。

translations.literal: Only Jingbang and Feng Xi and seven others were excluded from the amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Jingbang, Feng Xi, and six others alone were excluded from the pardon.

sentences.zh: 經邦之戍所，閉戶讀書。

translations.literal: At Jingbang's place of garrison duty, he closed his door and read books.
translations.idiomatic: In exile, Shao Jingbang shut himself in and devoted himself to study.

sentences.zh: 與熙及同戍陳九川，時相討論。

translations.literal: With Xi and Chen Jiuchuan, who shared the same garrison, he often discussed together.
translations.idiomatic: He and Feng Xi, along with fellow exile Chen Jiuchuan, often met to discuss and debate.

sentences.zh: 居鎮海三十七年卒。

translations.literal: He resided at Zhenhai for thirty-seven years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at Zhenhai for thirty-seven years before he died.

sentences.zh: 閩人立寓賢祠祀三人。

translations.literal: The people of Min erected a Shrine to Exiled Worthies and sacrificed to the three men.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fujian built a Shrine to Exiled Worthies in their honor.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Longqing reign, his official rank was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 劉世揚，字實甫，閩人。正德十二年進士。改庶吉士，除刑科給事中。世宗即位，議加興獻帝皇號，世揚疏諫。都察院牒司禮監，攝中官吳善良。帝手批原牒付刑科，以善良付司禮。世揚言：「祖宗制，凡降詔旨必書於題奏疏揭，或登聞鼓狀，乃發六科，宣於諸曹。或國有大事，上命先發，諸曹必補牘，於次日早朝進之，無竟批文牘者。今旨從中出，褻天語，更舊制，不可。」帝不聽。已，列先朝直臣舒芬、馬汝驥、王思、汪應軫、張原等二十人，請加恩以旌忠直，諸臣各進秩一等。嘗因災異，世揚請仿古人幾杖箴銘之義，取聖賢格言書殿廡，帝納之。

translations.literal: Liu Shiyang, courtesy name Shifu, was from Min. He became a jinshi in the twelfth year of Zhengde. He was transferred to be a shujishi and appointed Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Justice. When Shizong ascended the throne, there was discussion of adding an imperial title to Emperor Xingxian, and Shiyang submitted a memorial remonstrating. The Censorate sent a dispatch to the Directorate of Ceremonial, summoning the eunuch Wu Shanliang. The emperor personally wrote on the original dispatch and sent it to the Office of Scrutiny for Justice, handing Shanliang over to the Directorate of Ceremonial. Shiyang said: "According to ancestral regulations, whenever edicts and commands are issued, they must be written on titled memorials, sealed memorials, or statements from the Drum of Appeal, and only then sent to the Six Offices of Scrutiny and announced to the various offices. Or if the state has a great matter and the imperial command is first issued, the various offices must supplement it with documents and present them at early court the next day. There has never been a case of simply approving a written dispatch. Now an order has emerged from within; it profanes the imperial words and changes the old system. This cannot be permitted." The emperor did not listen. Later, Shiyang listed twenty upright ministers of the former reign, including Shu Fen, Ma Ruji, Wang Si, Wang Yingzhen, and Zhang Yuan, and requested that grace be added to honor loyalty and uprightness; each of the ministers was advanced one rank. Once because of disasters and anomalies, Shiyang requested imitation of the ancient meaning of admonitions and inscriptions on armrests and staffs, taking the wise words of sages and worthies and writing them in the palace halls and side buildings. The emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shiyang, courtesy name Shifu, was from Min. A jinshi of Zhengde 12, he was made a shujishi and then Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice. When Shizong came to the throne and officials discussed adding an imperial title to Emperor Xingxian, Shiyang remonstrated by memorial. The Censorate sent a dispatch to the Directorate of Ceremonial summoning the eunuch Wu Shanliang. The emperor personally annotated the original dispatch and sent it to the Office of Scrutiny for Justice, handing Shanliang over to the Directorate of Ceremonial. Shiyang said, "Under the ancestral system, whenever edicts are issued, they must be written on titled memorials, sealed memorials, or statements from the Drum of Appeal, and only then sent to the Six Offices of Scrutiny and proclaimed to the various offices. If the state has a major affair and an imperial command is issued first, the offices must supplement it with documents and present them at early court the next day. There has never been a practice of simply approving a written dispatch. Now an order has come out from within the palace, profaning the imperial word and changing the old system. This cannot be allowed." The emperor did not listen. Later Shiyang listed twenty upright ministers of the former reign, including Shu Fen, Ma Ruji, Wang Si, Wang Yingzhen, and Zhang Yuan, and requested special grace to honor loyalty and uprightness; each was advanced one rank. On another occasion, because of disasters and portents, Shiyang asked the emperor to imitate the ancient practice of admonitory inscriptions on armrests and staffs by writing maxims of sages and worthies in the palace halls and corridors. The emperor accepted this.

sentences.zh: 歷吏科左給事中，進都給事中。

translations.literal: He passed through Left Supervising Secretary in the Personnel Section and was promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Left Supervising Secretary in the Personnel Section to Chief Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 與同官李仁劾詹事顧鼎臣汙佞，且言今日詹事即他日輔臣。

translations.literal: Together with his colleague Li Ren, he impeached Guardian of the Heir Gu Dingchen as filthy and fawning, and further said that today's Guardian of the Heir is tomorrow's chief counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He and his colleague Li Ren impeached Guardian of the Heir Gu Dingchen for corruption and sycophancy, warning that today's tutor to the heir is tomorrow's chief minister.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，詰詹事進輔臣，出何典例？

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged and demanded: when a Guardian of the Heir becomes chief counselor, what canonical precedent provides for this?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and demanded to know what precedent justified the claim that a tutor to the heir would become chief counselor.

sentences.zh: 世揚等引罪。

translations.literal: Shiyang and the others acknowledged their offense.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shiyang and the others pleaded guilty.

sentences.zh: 帝怒不解，予杖，下詔獄，既乃得釋。

translations.literal: The Emperor's anger was not relieved; they were given the beating staff, sent to the imperial prison, and only afterward were released.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's wrath did not abate. They were beaten, thrown into the imperial prison, and released only afterward.

sentences.zh: 帝以久旱躬禱，世揚言在獄系囚及建言謫戍諸臣怨咨之氣，上幹天和，請悉疏釋。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally prayed because of prolonged drought. Shiyang said that prisoners held in jail and the ministers who had offered remonstrances and been banished to garrison duty bore resentful and complaining qi that ascended and disturbed Heaven's harmony, and he requested that all be released by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor prayed in person during a prolonged drought, Liu Shiyang argued that the resentment of prisoners and exiled remonstrators was disturbing Heaven's harmony, and he asked that they all be freed.

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: The Emperor could not employ this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼被劾罷，帝責諫官不言。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong and Gui E were impeached and dismissed; the Emperor blamed the remonstrating officials for not speaking.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong and Gui E were impeached and removed, the Emperor rebuked the censors for having said nothing.

sentences.zh: 世揚等乃盡劾璁、萼黨尚書王瓊而下數十人，章下吏部。

translations.literal: Shiyang and the others thereupon fully impeached dozens of men from Cong's and E's faction, from Minister Wang Qiong downward, and the memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shiyang and his colleagues then impeached dozens of Zhang Cong and Gui E's allies, from Minister Wang Qiong on down, and the memorial was forwarded to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 而尚書方獻夫亦璁、萼黨也，但去編修金璐、御史敖鉞、太仆丞姚奎、郎中劉汝輗、員外郎張、郭憲、待詔葉幼學、儲良才八人而已。

translations.literal: But Minister Fang Xianfu was also of Cong's and E's faction, and he removed only eight men: Compiler Jin Lu, Censor Ao Yue, Assistant Director of the Imperial Stud Yao Kui, Bureau Director Liu Ruheng, Section Vice Director Zhang, Guo Xian, Drafting Attendant Ye Youxue, and Chu Liangcai.
translations.idiomatic: But Minister Fang Xianfu, himself a Zhang Cong and Gui E ally, dismissed only eight men: Compiler Jin Lu, Censor Ao Yue, Assistant Director of the Imperial Stud Yao Kui, Bureau Director Liu Ruheng, Section Vice Director Zhang, Guo Xian, Drafting Attendant Ye Youxue, and Chu Liangcai.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復偕同官趙漢等陳修省八事。

translations.literal: Before long, he again joined his colleagues Zhao Han and others in presenting eight matters of self-examination and reform.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, he joined Zhao Han and other colleagues in submitting eight proposals for court self-reform.

sentences.zh: 中言：「大學士石瑤貞介，歿未易名。

translations.literal: Among them he said: "Grand Secretary Shi Yao was upright and incorruptible; since his death his name ought not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Among their recommendations: "Grand Secretary Shi Yao was upright and incorruptible. His posthumous name should not be altered.

sentences.zh: 尚書李鐩，國之盜臣，身後遺金得謚。

translations.literal: Minister Li Song was a thieving minister of the state; after his death he left gold and yet received a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Song was a thief in the state's service, yet after his death hoarded gold was found in his home and he still received a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 給事中鄭一鵬坐論楊一清再杖削職，一清敗，一鵬宜復官。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zheng Yipeng, because he discussed Yang Yiqing, was again beaten and stripped of office; when Yiqing fell, Yipeng ought to have his office restored."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zheng Yipeng was beaten and demoted for criticizing Yang Yiqing. Now that Yang Yiqing has fallen, Zheng Yipeng should be restored to office."

sentences.zh: 世揚發璁、萼黨，見憾於璁，一鵬又嘗忤璁、萼。

translations.literal: Shiyang had exposed Cong's and E's faction and was resented by Cong; Yipeng had also once offended Cong and E.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shiyang had exposed Zhang Cong and Gui E's faction and earned Zhang Cong's enmity; Zheng Yipeng, too, had once crossed them.

sentences.zh: 會璁已再相，而瑤實前賜謚，璁因激帝怒，謂給事言皆妄。

translations.literal: It happened that Cong had again become chief counselor, and Yao had in fact already been granted a posthumous title previously. Cong therefore stirred the Emperor's anger, saying the supervising secretaries' words were all false.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong had by then returned as chief counselor. Shi Yao had already received his posthumous title, so Zhang Cong goaded the Emperor into fury, declaring the censors' charges entirely false.

sentences.zh: 乃謫世揚江西布政司照磨，停漢等俸，然鐩謚亦由此奪。

translations.literal: Shiyang was thereupon banished to Registrar in the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission; Han and the others had their salaries suspended; yet Li Song's posthumous title was also taken away because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shiyang was demoted to registrar in the Jiangxi provincial administration; Zhao Han and the others had their salaries suspended. Li Song's posthumous title was revoked as well.

sentences.zh: 世揚屢遷河南提學僉事。

translations.literal: Shiyang was repeatedly transferred to Assistant Education Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shiyang was eventually promoted to Assistant Education Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 告歸，卒。

translations.literal: He requested return home and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired home and died there.

sentences.zh: 趙漢，字鴻逵，平湖人。

translations.literal: Zhao Han, styled Hongkui, was a native of Pinghu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Han, courtesy name Hongkui, was from Pinghu.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: Presented Scholar in the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in Zhengde 6 (1511).

sentences.zh: 授建昌推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor at Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 擢南京戶科給事中，改兵科。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Revenue Section at Nanjing and transferred to the Military Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Revenue Section at Nanjing, then transferred to the Military Section.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，尚書林俊以執奏獄囚李鳳陽，被旨詰責。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, Minister Lin Jun, because he insisted on memorializing about the imprisoned convict Li Fengyang, received an edict interrogating and rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign, Minister Lin Jun was rebuked by imperial edict for insisting on memorializing about the prisoner Li Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 漢因言：「太監崔文亂政，巧逞奸欺，不特庇一李鳳陽而已。

translations.literal: Han thereupon said: "Eunuch Cui Wen disorders government, cleverly deploying treachery and deceit—not merely sheltering one Li Fengyang alone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Han responded: "The eunuch Cui Wen is corrupting government with cunning deceit. He is not merely shielding Li Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書趙璜發文家人罪。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhao Huang exposed the crimes of Wen's household retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhao Huang exposed crimes committed by Cui Wen's household servants.

sentences.zh: 文輒捕其諜者，痛杖幾死，曰『此杖寄與趙尚書』，其無狀至此。

translations.literal: Wen immediately arrested Huang's spies, beat them painfully nearly to death, and said, 'These blows I send as a gift to Minister Zhao'—his shamelessness reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wen immediately seized Zhao Huang's informants and beat them nearly to death, saying, 'Send these blows to Minister Zhao with my compliments.' His audacity knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 望急譴逐，毋為新政累。」

translations.literal: I hope he will be urgently reprimanded and expelled, lest he become a burden on the new governance."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that he be swiftly punished and removed before he undermines the new administration."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 已，哭爭「大禮」，系詔獄廷杖。

translations.literal: Later, he wailed and contended over the 'Grand Rites,' was imprisoned in the imperial prison, and beaten at court.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined the tearful protest over the "Grand Rites" controversy, was imprisoned, and beaten at court.

sentences.zh: 歷吏科左給事中。

translations.literal: He passed through Left Supervising Secretary in the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left Supervising Secretary in the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 以疾去。

translations.literal: Because of illness he departed.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned due to illness.

sentences.zh: 起故官，遷工科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was raised to his former office and transferred to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Works Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to his former rank and promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Works Section.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「內閣桂萼、翟鑾稱病三月，未嘗以曠職懇辭。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "Grand Secretaries Gui E and Zhai Luan have claimed illness for three months yet have never earnestly resigned for neglect of duty.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Grand Secretaries Gui E and Zhai Luan have claimed illness for three months without formally requesting leave.

sentences.zh: 張璁久專政權，亦未聞引賢共濟。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong has long monopolized governmental power, and one has not heard of him bringing in the worthy to share in rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong has monopolized power for years, yet has never brought in worthy colleagues to share the burden of governance.

sentences.zh: 乞諭鑾、萼亟去，簡用兩京大臣及家居耆舊，以分璁任。」

translations.literal: I beg that Luan and E be urgently ordered to depart, and that grand ministers of the two capitals and elderly worthies at home be selected and employed to divide Cong's responsibilities."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Zhai Luan and Gui E be dismissed at once, and that senior ministers from both capitals and respected elders be appointed to share Zhang Cong's duties."

sentences.zh: 上摘其訛字詰之，諭璁毋避，趣赴閣。

translations.literal: The Emperor picked out his erroneous characters and interrogated him, instructed Cong not to avoid office, and urged him to hurry to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor seized on a typo in the memorial and interrogated Zhao Han, then told Zhang Cong to stop shirking and return to the Grand Secretariat at once.

sentences.zh: 璁因言漢忠謀，宜令備列堪內閣者。

translations.literal: Cong thereupon said Han was plotting disloyalty and that he ought to be ordered to list in full those fit for the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong then accused Zhao Han of disloyalty and said he should be made to name every man he considered fit for the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝即令漢舉所欲用，漢惶恐言：「臣欲璁引賢，無私主。」

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately ordered Han to recommend those he wished to employ. Han said in fear: "Your servant wished Cong to bring in the worthy; I have no private patron."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor immediately ordered Zhao Han to name his preferred appointees. Zhao Han said in alarm, "I only wanted Zhang Cong to bring in worthy men. I have no private favorites."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，責漢對不以實，趣以名上。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged, rebuked Han for not answering with truth, and urged him to submit names.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious, accused Zhao Han of evading the question, and ordered him to submit names at once.

sentences.zh: 漢益懼，言：「輔臣簡命，出自朝廷，非小臣所敢預。」

translations.literal: Han grew even more fearful and said: "The selection and appointment of chief counselors come from the court; it is not what a petty minister dares to presume upon."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Han grew still more frightened and said, "The appointment of chief counselors is the court's prerogative. A lowly official like myself dare not intrude."

sentences.zh: 帝乃宥之，奪俸一月。

translations.literal: The Emperor then pardoned him and confiscated one month's salary.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor relented and docked his salary for one month.

sentences.zh: 尋出為陜西右參政，告歸。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as Right Administration Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi and requested return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted as Right Administration Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi, then retired home.

sentences.zh: 久之，以故官起山西。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was raised to his former office in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he was recalled to his former rank in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 不數月復致仕。

translations.literal: In not many months he again retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he retired again.

sentences.zh: 子伊，廣西副使。

translations.literal: His son Yi was Vice Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao Yi served as Vice Commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 年四十，即以養父歸。

translations.literal: At age forty, he immediately returned home to support his father.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he retired to care for his father.

sentences.zh: 屢征不起。

translations.literal: Repeated summonses he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated imperial summonses could not bring him back.

sentences.zh: 魏良弼，字師說，新建人。

translations.literal: Wei Liangbi, styled Shishuo, was a native of Xinjian.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liangbi, courtesy name Shishuo, was from Xinjian.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年進士。

translations.literal: Presented Scholar in the second year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in Jiajing 2 (1523).

sentences.zh: 授松陽知縣，召拜刑科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Songyang and summoned to serve as Supervising Secretary in the Punishments Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Songyang, then summoned to serve as Supervising Secretary in the Punishments Section.

sentences.zh: 采木侍郎黃衷事竣歸家，乞致仕，未許。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Timber Huang Zhong, his mission completed, returned home and begged to retire from office, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Huang Zhong, who had been dispatched to procure timber, returned home after completing his mission and requested retirement, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 緝事者奏衷潛入京師。

translations.literal: Investigators memorialized that Zhong had secretly entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Investigators reported that Huang Zhong had secretly entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪衷職。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged and stripped Zhong of his office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and stripped Huang Zhong of his rank.

sentences.zh: 良弼言衷大臣，入都豈能隱，乞正言者欺罔罪，不報。

translations.literal: Liangbi said Zhong was a great minister—entering the capital, how could he hide? He begged that the accusers be punished for deception, but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liangbi argued that as a senior minister Huang Zhong could hardly have entered the capital in secret, and asked that the accusers be punished for false reporting. He received no response.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼初罷相，詔察其黨。

translations.literal: When Zhang Cong and Gui E were first dismissed as chief counselors, an edict ordered an investigation of their faction.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong and Gui E were first removed as chief counselors, an edict was issued to investigate their faction.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉世揚等議及良弼。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Shiyang and others discussed Liangbi in their deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Shiyang and others named Wei Liangbi in their deliberations.

sentences.zh: 以吏部言，得留。

translations.literal: On the Ministry of Personnel's word, he was allowed to remain.
translations.idiomatic: On the Ministry of Personnel's recommendation, he was allowed to keep his post.

sentences.zh: 尋命巡視京營。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to inspect the Capital Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed to inspect the Capital Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 劾罷提督五軍營保定伯梁永福、太仆卿曾直，罪武定侯郭勛家奴，論團營兵政之弊，又請發銀米振京師饑，直聲大著。

translations.literal: He impeached and had dismissed Liang Yongfu, Baron of Baoding, Superintendent of the Five Armies Camps, and Zeng Zhi, Minister of the Imperial Stud; punished the household slaves of Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun; discussed the abuses of the Training Division's military administration; and also requested the issuance of silver and grain to relieve famine in the capital—his upright reputation greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and removed Liang Yongfu, Baron of Baoding, superintendent of the Five Armies Camps, and Zeng Zhi, Minister of the Imperial Stud; punished servants of Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun; exposed abuses in the Training Division's military administration; and called for silver and grain to relieve famine in the capital. His reputation for integrity soared.

sentences.zh: 會南京御史馬敭等以劾吏部尚書王瓊被逮，良弼請釋之。

translations.literal: It happened that Nanjing Censor Ma Yang and others, because they impeached Minister of Personnel Wang Qiong, were arrested; Liangbi requested their release.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing Censor Ma Yang and others were arrested for impeaching Minister Wang Qiong, Wei Liangbi asked that they be freed.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，並下詔獄。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged and had them all sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and had them all thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 論贖還職，仍奪俸一年。

translations.literal: They were sentenced to ransom and return to office, yet still had one year's salary confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: They were sentenced to pay a fine and return to office, with one year's salary docked.

sentences.zh: 三遷至禮科都給事中。

translations.literal: After three promotions he reached Chief Supervising Secretary in the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became Chief Supervising Secretary in the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 十一年八月，彗星見東井，芒長丈余。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eleventh year, a comet appeared at Eastern Well, its tail more than one zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Jiajing 11 (1532), a comet appeared in the Eastern Well constellation, its tail more than ten feet long.

sentences.zh: 良弼引占書言：「彗星晨見東方，君臣爭明。

translations.literal: Liangbi cited prognostic books, saying: "When a comet appears in the morning in the east, ruler and ministers contend for brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liangbi cited prognostic texts: "When a comet appears in the morning sky in the east, ruler and ministers struggle for supremacy.

sentences.zh: 彗孛出井，奸臣在側。

translations.literal: When a broom star emerges from the Well, treacherous ministers are at the side.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet rises from the Well constellation, treacherous ministers stand at the ruler's side.

sentences.zh: 大學士張孚敬專橫竊威福，致奸星示異，亟宜罷黜。」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Fuxing is domineering and usurps authority and blessings, causing the treacherous star to display its anomaly—he ought urgently to be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Fuxing has grown tyrannical and usurped imperial power, provoking this ominous sign. He should be removed at once."

sentences.zh: 孚敬奏良弼挾私。

translations.literal: Fuxing memorialized that Liangbi was acting from private motives.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fuxing countered with a memorial accusing Wei Liangbi of acting from private spite.

sentences.zh: 帝已疑孚敬，兩疏皆報聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor already harbored suspicion of Fujing; both memorials were merely reported as received.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor already doubted Zhang Fujing, and both memorials were simply acknowledged without action.

sentences.zh: 給事中秦鰲疏再入，孚敬竟罷去。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Qin Ao's memorial came in again, and Fujing was at last dismissed and removed.
translations.idiomatic: When Supervising Secretary Qin Ao submitted his memorial again, Zhang Fujing was finally dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 逾月，良弼復偕同官劾吏部尚書汪鋐。

translations.literal: After a month, Liangbi again together with his colleagues impeached Minister of Personnel Wang Zong.
