translations.idiomatic: A month later, Wei Liangbi again joined his colleagues in impeaching Minister of Personnel Wang Zong.

sentences.zh: 帝方向鋐，奪良弼俸。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then inclined toward Zong and stripped Liangbi of his salary.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was siding with Wang Zong and docked Wei Liangbi's salary.

sentences.zh: 鋐、孚敬俱恨良弼。

translations.literal: Zong and Fujing both hated Liangbi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zong and Zhang Fujing both bore a grudge against Wei Liangbi.

sentences.zh: 明年元日，副都御史王應鵬坐事下詔獄。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day the next year, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yingpeng, implicated in an offense, was sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day the following year, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yingpeng was imprisoned in the imperial prison on a criminal charge.

sentences.zh: 良弼言履端之始，不宜以微過系大臣。

translations.literal: Liangbi said that at the beginning of the year, one ought not to detain a great minister over a minor fault.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liangbi argued that at the start of the new year it was wrong to imprison a senior minister over a trifling offense.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，再下詔獄。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and again sent him to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged and had him thrown back into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 獄卒訝曰：「公又來耶！」

translations.literal: The prison guard said in astonishment: "My lord, have you come again!"
translations.idiomatic: The jailer exclaimed in surprise, "My lord, have you come again!"

sentences.zh: 為垂涕。

translations.literal: and shed tears on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: And he wept for him.

sentences.zh: 尋復職，奪俸。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored to office, but his salary was taken.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored to office, though his salary was withheld.

sentences.zh: 時孚敬復起柄政，與鋐修前郤，以考察後命科道官互糾，又奏上十一人，又不及良弼。

translations.literal: At that time Fujing rose again to wield power, mended his former rift with Zong, and after the evaluation ordered censorate officials to impeach one another; he again submitted eleven names, again not including Liangbi.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhang Fujing had returned to power, reconciled with Wang Zong, and after the performance review ordered censorate officials to cross-impeach one another. He submitted eleven names again—again omitting Wei Liangbi.

sentences.zh: 孚敬益怒，擬旨切責，令吏部再考。

translations.literal: Fujing grew even angrier, drafted a rescript sharply rebuking them, and ordered the Ministry of Personnel to evaluate again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fujing grew still angrier, drafted an edict of sharp rebuke, and ordered the Ministry of Personnel to conduct another review.

sentences.zh: 鋐乃別糾二十六人，而良弼及秦鰲、葉洪皆前劾孚敬、鋐者，中外大駭。

translations.literal: Zong then separately impeached twenty-six men, among them Liangbi, Qin Ao, and Ye Hong—all who had earlier impeached Fujing and Zong—and court and countryside were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zong then singled out twenty-six officials for impeachment, including Wei Liangbi, Qin Ao, and Ye Hong—all men who had earlier attacked Zhang Fujing and Wang Zong—and the shock reverberated inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 良弼竟坐不謹削籍。

translations.literal: Liangbi in the end was convicted of lack of discretion and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liangbi was ultimately dismissed for indiscretion and removed from the official register.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，詔起廢籍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, an edict restored him from dismissed status.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign, an edict recalled him from disgrace.

sentences.zh: 以年老即家拜太常少卿，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Because of old age he was appointed at home as Vice Minister of Ceremonies, retired, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his age he was appointed Vice Minister of Ceremonies at home, then retired and died.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚忠簡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, he was posthumously enfeoffed with the title Loyal and Simple.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was posthumously granted the title Loyal and Simple.

sentences.zh: 葉洪，字子源，德州人。

translations.literal: Ye Hong, styled Ziyuan, was a native of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Hong, courtesy name Ziyuan, was from Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年進士。

translations.literal: Presented Scholar in the eighth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in Jiajing 8 (1529).

sentences.zh: 授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary of the Revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Revenue section of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 十一年肇舉祈谷禮於圜丘，帝不親祀。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the grain-praying rite was first performed at the Circular Mound, and the Emperor did not sacrifice in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the grain-praying rite was first held at the Circular Mound Altar, but the Emperor did not perform the sacrifice himself.

sentences.zh: 洪疏諫，帝責洪妄言。

translations.literal: Hong submitted a memorial remonstrating, and the Emperor rebuked Hong for reckless speech.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Hong memorialized in protest, and the Emperor rebuked him for reckless speech.

sentences.zh: 尋巡視京營，進工科右給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he inspected the capital garrison and was promoted to right supervising secretary of the Works section.
translations.idiomatic: He soon inspected the capital garrisons and was promoted to right supervising secretary in the Works section.

sentences.zh: 汪鋐遷吏部尚書，洪極論其奸，忤旨奪俸。

translations.literal: Wang Zong was transferred to Minister of Personnel; Hong argued at length his treachery, offended the imperial will, and had his salary taken.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zong was promoted to Minister of Personnel, Ye Hong denounced his corruption at length, defied the throne, and had his salary docked.

sentences.zh: 明年考察，鋐修怨，遂坐洪浮躁，貶寧國縣丞。

translations.literal: The next year in the evaluation, Zong nursed his grudge and had Hong convicted of frivolity, demoting him to assistant magistrate of Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: At the next performance review Wang Zong settled old scores and had Ye Hong convicted of frivolity, demoting him to assistant magistrate of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 居二年，復以大計奪其職。

translations.literal: After two years, he again lost his post in the major evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he lost his post again in the major triennial review.

sentences.zh: 言者屢訟冤，不復用。

translations.literal: Memorialists repeatedly pleaded his injustice, but he was not employed again.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists repeatedly pleaded his case, but he was never reappointed.

sentences.zh: 秦鰲，字子元，昆山人。

translations.literal: Qin Ao, styled Ziyuan, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Ao, courtesy name Ziyuan, was from Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年進士。

translations.literal: Presented Scholar in the fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations in Jiajing 5 (1526).

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 擢兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary of the Military section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Military section.

sentences.zh: 劾魏國公徐鵬舉、中官賴義不法狀，義罷還。

translations.literal: He impeached the Duke of Wei, Xu Pengju, and the eunuch Lai Yi for unlawful conduct; Yi was dismissed and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Duke of Wei Xu Pengju and the eunuch Lai Yi for misconduct, and Lai Yi was dismissed and recalled.

sentences.zh: 彗星見，劾張孚敬妒賢病國，擬議詔旨，輒引以自歸。

translations.literal: When a comet appeared, he impeached Zhang Fujing for envying the worthy and harming the state, and for whenever drafting rescripts always citing them to vindicate himself.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared, he impeached Zhang Fujing for envying talent and harming the state, charging that whenever Fujing drafted rescripts he cited them as vindication of himself.

sentences.zh: 帝遂罷孚敬。

translations.literal: The Emperor then dismissed Fujing.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then dismissed Zhang Fujing.

sentences.zh: 已，孚敬再相。

translations.literal: Soon after, Fujing became chancellor again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhang Fujing returned as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 汪鋐承風指以考察謫鰲東陽縣丞。

translations.literal: Wang Zong, following the wind and pointer, through evaluation demoted Ao to assistant magistrate of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zong, taking his cue from above, used a performance review to demote Qin Ao to assistant magistrate of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 屢遷福建右參議。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred until Right Assistant Commissioner in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to Right Assistant Commissioner in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died while holding office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 又有張寅者，太倉人。

translations.literal: There was also a Zhang Yin, a native of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a man named Zhang Yin, from Taicang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初進士。

translations.literal: Presented Scholar at the beginning of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examinations early in the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 歷南京御史。

translations.literal: He served successively as censor in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a censor in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 嘗劾禮部侍郎黃綰十罪。

translations.literal: He once impeached Vice Minister of Rites Huang Wan on ten counts.
translations.idiomatic: He once impeached Vice Minister of Rites Huang Wan on ten counts of misconduct.

sentences.zh: 比張孚敬罷政，寅言其憸邪蠹政，不可悉數，請追所賜封誥、銀章之屬，明正其辟。

translations.literal: When Zhang Fujing was dismissed from power, Yin said he was treacherous and corrupt, ruining governance beyond full enumeration, and requested recovery of conferred patents, silver seals, and the like, clearly establishing his crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Fujing fell from power, Zhang Yin charged that his treachery and corruption had ruined governance beyond reckoning, and asked that the patents of ennoblement, silver seals, and other honors he had received be revoked and his guilt formally established.

sentences.zh: 並劾左都御史汪鋐陰賊邪媚。

translations.literal: He also impeached Left Censor-in-Chief Wang Zong for secretly acting as a villainous flatterer.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Left Censor-in-Chief Wang Zong for secretly serving as a treacherous sycophant.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謫高唐判官。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and demoted him to judge of Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged and demoted him to judge at Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 屢遷南京文選郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred until Director of Selection in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to Director of Selection in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 會簡宮僚，改春坊右司直兼翰林院檢討。

translations.literal: When palace staff were being selected, he was changed to Right Director in the Eastern Palace, concurrently Hanlin Academician Reader.
translations.idiomatic: When palace staff were being selected, he was appointed Right Director in the Eastern Palace and concurrently Hanlin Academician Reader.

sentences.zh: 未幾，被劾罷。

translations.literal: Before long, he was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was impeached and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《書》曰：「非佞折獄，惟良折獄，罔非在中。」

translations.literal: The commentator says: The Book says: "It is not the flatterer who decides cases—the good man decides cases, and none fail to hit the center."
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: The Book of Documents says, "It is not the flatterer who decides cases—the upright man decides cases, and all without exception attain the true measure."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「明啟刑書，胥占鹹庶中。」

translations.literal: Again it says: "With clear understanding he opens the penal code; all officials and the common people alike attain what is correct in the center."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "With clear understanding he opens the penal laws; all officials and common people alike obtain what is right and true."

sentences.zh: 正言折獄之不可不得其中也。

translations.literal: Correct speech: in deciding cases one cannot fail to attain the center.
translations.idiomatic: This rightly states that in deciding cases one cannot fail to hit the true measure.

sentences.zh: 張寅、李钅盬，罪狀昭然。

translations.literal: Zhang Yin and Li Jian—the proofs of guilt were brilliantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the cases of Zhang Yin and Li Jian, the evidence of guilt was plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 中於郭勛、席書之說，廷臣獲罪，而寅還職，钅盬宥死。

translations.literal: Taken in by the words of Guo Xun and Xi Shu, court ministers were punished, while Yin was restored to office and Jian was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Taken in by Guo Xun and Xi Shu, court ministers were punished while Zhang Yin was restored to office and Li Jian was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 陳洸罪至百七十二條，竟得免死，而猶上書訟冤，凡攻洸之惡與治洸之獄者，逮捕至百數十人。

translations.literal: Chen Guang's crimes numbered as many as one hundred seventy-two, yet he escaped death; he still submitted a memorial claiming injustice, and all who had attacked Guang's evils or prosecuted his case were arrested, numbering more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guang's crimes ran to one hundred seventy-two counts, yet he escaped death and still memorialized claiming injustice. Everyone who had denounced his conduct or prosecuted his case was arrested—more than a hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 皆由議禮觸眾怒，一言有以深入帝隱。

translations.literal: All this arose from touching the crowd's anger over the Rites dispute—a single word could penetrate deeply into the emperor's hidden sentiments.
translations.idiomatic: All of this arose from touching the public fury over the Rites dispute—a single word could strike deep into the emperor's hidden resentments.

sentences.zh: 甚矣，佞人之可畏也。

translations.literal: Extreme indeed is the dreadfulness of flatterers!
translations.idiomatic: How greatly to be feared are flatterers!

sentences.zh: 夫反成案似於明，出死罪似於仁，而不知其借端報復，刑罰失中。

translations.literal: Reversing a concluded case seems clarity; sparing a capital offender seems benevolence—yet one does not see that they seize the opportunity for revenge, and punishments miss the center.
translations.idiomatic: Reversing a settled verdict looks like clarity; sparing a capital offender looks like mercy—yet one fails to see that they seize the chance for revenge, and justice misses its true measure.

sentences.zh: 佞良之辨，可弗審歟！

translations.literal: The distinction between flatterer and good man—can it not be carefully examined!
translations.idiomatic: The distinction between the flatterer and the upright man—can it not be weighed with care!
